children.text: ekastvaṃ viṣameṣu khinnamanasāṃ sarvābalānāṃ gatiḥ gopyevaṃ gaditaḥ sa leśamavatādgoṣṭhe hasantyā hariḥ // VjivC_3.180 //
children.translated_text: You alone are the refuge of all helpless women whose hearts are distressed in difficulties." — Thus addressed by the <s>gopī</s> (cowherd woman) who was laughing in the cowpen, may that <s>Hari</s> protect you even a little! [<s>Vakroktijīvita</s> Commentary 3.180]

children.text: evaṃ vākyabandhavaicitryaśaktabuddhiviracitaṃ carvaṇīyaṃ śleṣamabhidhāya, sāmyaikanibandhanatvādupamārūpakaśleṣakāraṇaikaṃ vyatirekamabhidhatte--- sati tacchabdavācyatve dharmasāmye 'nyathāsthiteḥ /
children.translated_text: Having thus described <s>śleṣa</s> (double meaning), which is delectable and crafted by an intellect skilled in the variety of sentence-construction, since it is based solely on similarity, he states <s>vyatireka</s> (contrast), which shares a single cause with <s>upamā</s> (simile), <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor), and <s>śleṣa</s> (double meaning) — 'When there is expressibility by that word, and when similarity of attribute obtains, from a difference in condition,
the separation from another for the purpose of establishing the superiority of the subject at hand —
whether verbal or apprehended — is called <s>vyatireka</s> (contrast).' [<s>Vakroktijīvita</s> 3.48]

children.text:
satītyādiḥ /
sa cāsau śabdaśceti vigṛhya tacchabdena śaktyā śleṣanimittabhūtaḥ śabdaḥ parāmṛśyate, tasya "vācyatve" abhidheyatve "sati" "dharmasāmye" parasparaparispandasādṛśye vidyamāne, (vikalpanā) yāṃ tathāvidhaśabdavācyatvasya dharmasāmyasya cobhayaniṣṭhatvādubhayoḥ prakṛtatvāt /
prastutāprastutayoreva tayoḥ dharmādekasya yathāruci kenāpi vivakṣi(tadharmānta) reṇa "anyathāsthaiteḥ" anyathābhāvenāvasthiteḥ "vyatirecanaṃ"---pṛthakkaraṇaṃ "anyasmāt" upameyasyopamānāt, upamānasya vā tasmāt /
saḥ "vyatirekaḥ" vyatirekanāmā alaṅkāro "'bhidhīyate" kathyate /
kimarthaṃ---"prastutotkarṣasiddhaye", "prastutasya" varṇyamānavṛtteḥ "utkarṣasiddhaye" chāyātiśayaniṣpattaye /
sa dvividhaḥ saṃbhavati "śābdaḥ pratīyamāno vā" = "śābdaḥ" = kavipravāhaprasiddhaḥ tatsamarpaṇasamarthābhidhānenābhidhīyamānaḥ /
"pratīyamānaḥ" = vākyārthasāmarthyamātrāvabodhyaḥ /
tatra prathamatāratamyādupamāvyatireko yathā---
children.translated_text:
'When' etc.
Analyzing 'that word' as 'that itself being the word,' by 'that word' the word that serves as the cause of <s>śleṣa</s> (double meaning) through its [denotative] power is referred to. 'When there is expressibility' — when there is denotability — 'when similarity of attribute' — when a resemblance in mutual activity exists — (the option arises) because both word-expressibility of that kind and similarity of attribute pertain to both, since both are the subject at hand.
Of those two — the subject and the non-subject — from one of the attributes, through some other attribute intended at will (different from the stated attribute), 'from a difference in condition' — from a state of being otherwise — 'the separation' — the distinguishing — 'from another' — of the compared from the standard of comparison, or of the standard from the compared.
That figure called <s>vyatireka</s> (contrast) 'is stated' — is described.
For what purpose? — 'For the establishment of the superiority of the subject at hand' — of the thing being described, for the accomplishment of a surpassing excellence.
It is of two kinds: 'verbal or apprehended.' 'Verbal' means well-known in the tradition of poets, expressed by a denotative expression capable of conveying that [contrast]. 'Apprehended' means knowable merely through the force of sentence-meaning.
Among these, the <s>upamā</s>-based <s>vyatireka</s>, from the primacy of the first [type], is as follows:

children.text: emea jaṇo tissā dei kavolovamāi sasibiṃbam /
children.translated_text: [Prakrit:] People give the moon-disc as a comparison for her cheek;

children.text: paramatthaviāre uṇa cando via varāo // VjivC_3.181 //
children.translated_text: but upon true examination, the moon is like the moon itself — the poor thing! [<s>Vakroktijīvita</s> Commentary 3.181]
[Sanskrit rendering:] People give the moon-disc as a comparison for her cheek;
but upon true examination, the moon is like the moon itself — the poor thing!
(Sanskrit rendering)
Or, for example:
Desiring to see the charming play of the eyelash-creepers of your thousand eyes,

children.text: vāpīṣu nīlotpalinī-vikāsaramyāsu nandanti na ṣaṭpadaughāḥ // VjivC_3.182 //
children.translated_text: the swarms of bees find no delight even in lovely pools where blue lotuses bloom. [<s>Vakroktijīvita</s> Commentary 3.182]
Or, for example:

children.text: prāptaśrīreṣa kasmāt puranapi mayi te manthakhedaṃ vidadhyāt nidrāmapyasya pūrvāmanalasamanaso naiva saṃbhāvayāmi /
children.translated_text: "Since he has attained sovereignty, why would he again inflict upon me the toil of churning? I cannot even conceive that his earlier slumber was that of one whose mind is like fire [in restlessness].

children.text: setuṃ badhnāti bhūyaḥ kimiti ca sakaladvīpanāthānuyātaḥ tvayyāyāte vikalpāniti dadhata ivābhāti kampaḥ payodheḥ // VjivC_3.183 //
children.translated_text: Why does he again build a bridge? And why, followed by the lords of all the islands, does he come to you?" — As if entertaining such doubts at your arrival, the trembling of the ocean appears. [<s>Vakroktijīvita</s> Commentary 3.183]

children.text:
atra varṇyamānasya nārāyaṇatvasamāropaṃ vinā tadārambhasaṃbhāvanā na saṃbhavatīti tasya tattvādhyāropaṇāt pratīyamānatayā rūpakameva pūrvasūribhiḥ samāmnātam; vācyavyatirekaḥ tatkathamasyopapadyate /
satyamuktam, kintu yuktiratrābhidhīyate, tasmāddividhaṃ pratīyamānaṃ vastu, pratipādanaguṇībhūtasvārthavācakavyāpāragocaraḥ, tathāvidhārthasāmarthyaviṣayo vā /
tatra vācakamupamānamityālocya vivakṣitārthopapattinimittaṃ vācyasāmarthyameva samāśritya pūrvasūribhiratadāmnātam /
vācakavyāpāraḥ punaranyathaiva vyavasthitaḥ /
tathā ca prāpta(śrī) prabhṛtīni padāni ākṣiptapratiyogitayopanibaddhāni, prastutasya prāktanaparispandaviśiṣṭataradevatātvapratipādakaparāṇi prakaṭameva rūpakavyatirekaṃ gamayanti /
tadidamuktam--
children.translated_text:
Here, without the superimposition of the identity of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>) upon the person being described, the imagining of those undertakings is impossible; hence, because of the superimposition of that identity, this has been traditionally classified by earlier authorities as <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor) in its apprehended form. [One might object:] It is expressed <s>vyatireka</s> (contrast) — how then does it apply here?
True, that has been said. But the reasoning here is stated: therefore, the apprehended object is of two kinds — that which falls within the scope of the denotative operation whose own meaning has become subsidiary to the act of presentation, and that which is the domain of the force of such meaning alone.
Among these, considering the standard of comparison as the denotative element, and relying solely upon the force of the expressed meaning as the ground for the intended meaning's establishment, the earlier authorities did not classify it as such.
But the denotative operation is in fact established differently.
Thus, words like 'having attained sovereignty' etc., being constructed with the implication of a counterpart, being oriented toward establishing the subject as a deity superior to the earlier-known activity — they clearly convey <s>rūpaka</s>-based <s>vyatireka</s> (metaphor-based contrast).
This has been stated:
"Where a meaning or a word, having made its own meaning subsidiary, suggests

children.text: vyaṅktaḥ kāvyaviśeṣaḥ sadhvaniriti sūribhiḥ kathitaḥ // VjivC_3.184 //
children.translated_text: another meaning — that special kind of poetry is called <s>sadhvani</s> (possessing suggestion) by the learned." [<s>Vakroktijīvita</s> Commentary 3.184]

Therefore, nothing is inconsistent.
The <s>śleṣa</s>-based <s>vyatireka</s> (contrast based on double meaning) is as follows:

children.text: ślāghyāseṣatanuṃ sudarśanakaraḥ sarvaṅgalīlājita- tryailokyāṃ caraṇāravindalalitenākrāntaloko hariḥ /
children.translated_text: "<s>Hari</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s> / a lion) — whose praiseworthy form is entire, whose hand is <s>Sudarśana</s> (the discus / beautiful), who has conquered the three worlds through the grace of all his limbs, who has pervaded the world with his lotus-feet's playful beauty;

children.text: bibhrāṇā mukhamindurūpamakhilaṃ candrātmacakṣurdadhat sthāne yāṃ svatanorapaśyadadhikāṃ sā rukmiṇīvo 'vatāt // VjivC_3.185 //
children.translated_text: She who bears a face like the moon, whose eyes are entirely moon-like — may that <s>Rukmiṇī</s>, whom he saw as surpassing his own body, protect you!" [<s>Vakroktijīvita</s> Commentary 3.185]
He states another variety of this [<s>vyatireka</s>]:
"The contrast that consists in the separation of one [thing] specifically
from a commonly known general activity, without intending the other — [that is another <s>vyatireka</s>]." [<s>Vakroktijīvita</s> 3.49]

children.text:
lokaprasiddhetyādiḥ---"paraḥ" anyaḥ sa vyatirekālaṅkāraḥ /
kīdṛśaḥ "yadekasya" vastunaḥ "vyatirekaḥ "pṛthakkaraṇaṃ /
kasmāt "lokaprasiddhasāmānyaparispandāt = "lokaprasiddhaḥ "---jagatpratītaḥ sāmānyabhūtaḥ sarvasādhāraṇaḥ yaḥ"parispandaḥ " vyāpāraḥ tasmāt /
kuto hetoḥ "viśeṣataḥ" kutaścidatiśayāt /
kathaṃ "tadavivakṣayā" tadityupamādīnāṃ parāmarśaḥ, teṣām "avivakṣayā" tānyavivikṣitvā yo vihitaḥ /
ayamatrābhiprāyaḥ---yadayameva (vivakṣitaḥ) sāmānyabhūtatvena te punarasyaiva śeṣāḥ prastāvapūrvamabhihitāḥ /
parasyodāharaṇaṃ yathā---
children.translated_text:
'Commonly known' etc. — 'The other' is that figure called <s>vyatireka</s> (contrast). Of what kind? — Where there is 'the separation of one' thing. From what? — From 'the commonly known general activity' — 'commonly known' means recognized by the world; 'general' means common to all; 'activity' means operation — from that.
For what reason? — 'Specifically' — on account of some particular excellence.
How? — 'Without intending the other' — 'that' refers to <s>upamā</s> (simile) and the like; 'without intending those' — having not intended them, that which is fashioned.
The purport here is this: this very [contrast] that is intended, being of a general nature — those [other figures] are merely subsidiaries of this same one, stated with a preliminary occasion.
An example of the latter is as follows:

children.text: cāpaṃ puṣpitabhūtalaṃ suracitā maurvo dvirephāvalī pūrṇendorudaye 'bhiyogasamayaḥ puṣpākaro 'pyāsaraḥ /
children.translated_text: "The bow is the flowering earth; the well-fashioned bowstring is a line of bees; the time of engagement is at the rising of the full moon; the quiver too is the spring season;

children.text: śastrāṇyutpalaketakīsumanaso yodhātmanaḥ kāmināṃ trailokye madanasya ko 'pi lalitollekho jīgiṣāgrahaḥ // VjivC_3.186 //
children.translated_text: the weapons are <s>utpala</s>, <s>ketakī</s>, and <s>sumanas</s> flowers; the warriors are lovers themselves — in the three worlds, some exquisite sketch of <s>Madana</s>'s (Love's) desire for conquest!" [<s>Vakroktijīvita</s> Commentary 3.186]

children.text:
atra sakalalokaprasiddhaśastrādyupakaraṇakalāpājjigīṣā vyavahārānmanmathasya sukumāropakaraṇatvājjigīṣāvyavahāro vyatiricyate /
nanu bhūtalādīnāṃ cāpādirūpaṇādrūpakavyatireka evāyam ? naitadasti /
rūpakavyatireke hi rūpaṇaṃ vidhāya tasmādeva vyatirecanaṃ vidhīyate ; etasmina punaḥ sakalalokaprasiddhāt sāmānyatātparyādvyatirecanam /
bhūtalādīnāṃ cāpādirūpaṇaṃ viśeṣaṇāntaranimittamātramavadhāryatām /
evaṃ vyatirekaṃ vicārya śleṣābhisaṃbhinnatvāducitāvasaraṃ virodhaṃ vicārayati---
children.translated_text:
Here, from the entire arsenal of weapons and equipment known to the whole world, the martial activity of <s>Manmatha</s> (Love) is contrasted [with ordinary warfare] on account of the delicacy of his equipment.
Now, is this not simply <s>rūpaka</s>-based <s>vyatireka</s>, since the earth etc. are metaphorically cast as bows etc.? This is not so.
For in <s>rūpaka</s>-based <s>vyatireka</s>, having performed the metaphorical identification, the contrast is made from that very identification. But here, the contrast is from the general purport known to the whole world.
The metaphorical casting of the earth etc. as bows etc. should be understood as merely the occasion for another kind of qualification.
Having thus examined <s>vyatireka</s>, since it is intertwined with <s>śleṣa</s>, he examines <s>virodha</s> (contradiction) at the appropriate juncture:
"<s>Virodha</s> (contradiction) is that which, by effecting the conjunction of words expressing contradictory meanings,
outlines the reasoned consistency of the apprehension." [<s>Vakroktijīvita</s> 3.50]

children.text:
virodhetyādi /
yo 'laṅkāraḥ parasparaviruddhārthapratītyā, "viruddhārthavācināṃ" viruddhavastuvacanānāṃ yuktiyuktatāmullikhati tadabhidhāyinā padāntareṇa arthasāmarthyena vā samarpayan yuktyā prakāreṇopapadyamānatayā saṅgatiṃ vidadhāti /
tasya padārthatvāt samanvayaṃ karoti virodhābhidhānaḥ sa bhaṇyate /
yathā
children.translated_text:
'<s>Virodha</s>' etc.
That figure which, through the apprehension of mutually contradictory meanings, 'outlines the reasoned consistency' — by means of another word that expresses it, or through the force of meaning, 'effecting the conjunction' — establishes the conjunction as something that is warranted through a particular mode — of 'words expressing contradictory meanings' — words that denote contradictory things. That [figure], because of being a word-meaning, establishes coherence — it is called <s>virodha</s> (contradiction).
For example:
"A bad husband yet the beloved of his wife; a great fault yet the abode of all arts." [<s>Vakroktijīvita</s> Commentary 3.187]

children.text:
atra "api" śabdena virodhapratipattiḥ /
kvacidarthasāmarthyena virodhaḥ pratīyate /
yathā
children.translated_text:
Here, the word 'api' (even/yet) conveys the apprehension of contradiction.
Sometimes, contradiction is apprehended through the force of meaning alone.
For example:
"<s>Gaurī</s> and so on, by you..." [<s>Vakroktijīvita</s> Commentary 3.188]

<s>Virodha</s> (contradiction) can also occur mixed with <s>śleṣa</s> (double meaning) and other [figures].
For example:

children.text: "maulāvartāntamate vicittoyare aṇaṃ aparihatvena pari lañcitakamantā visesasāhoti ahaṃ /
children.translated_text: "At the crown... the water... without abandoning... specificity... I..."
[<s>Vakroktijīvita</s> Commentary 3.189]

children.text:
rūpakādiṣvapyete bhedāḥ saṃbhavantīti svayamutprekṣaṇīyam /
evaṃ virodhaṃ vicārya samāsoktyādervirodhacchāyānupraveśaprasaṅgataḥ tadvicāramāracayati---
children.translated_text:
These varieties can also occur within <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor) and other [figures] — this should be imagined by oneself.
Having thus examined <s>virodha</s> (contradiction), since there is occasion for the shadow of contradiction to enter into <s>samāsokti</s> (condensed expression) and the like, he arranges the examination of that:
"<s>Samāsokti</s> (condensed expression) and <s>sahokti</s> (co-expression) are not considered as [independent] figures of speech,
because they are [subsumable] under other figures, and because they lack beauty." [<s>Vakroktijīvita</s> 3.51]

children.text:
samāsoktirityādi /
yeyaṃ "samāsoktiḥ" alaṅkṛtira (bhihitā) (sā) "nālaṅkāratayā matā" na vibhūṣaṇabhāvena pratibhātā, yasmāt pṛthaṅ nopapadyate /
kena hetunā "alaṅkārāntaratvena" vibhūṣaṇāntarabhāvena /
"śobhāśūnyatayā tathā" kāntirahitatvena ca /
tadidamuktaṃ bhavati--yadi rāmaṇīyakatvaṃ saṃbhavati prakarāntaravihite tasmin bhūṣaṇāntare 'ntarbhavati /
ramaṇīyatvābhāve śobhāśūnyatvaṃ paryavasyati tasyāḥ /
tathā ca lakṣaṇodāharaṇe---
children.translated_text:
'<s>Samāsokti</s>' etc.
This <s>samāsokti</s> that has been described as a figure — it 'is not considered as [having the status of] a figure of speech' — it does not appear as an ornament, because it does not stand independently on its own.
For what reason? — 'Because of being [subsumable] under another figure' — because of being included in another ornament.
'And because of lacking beauty' — because of being devoid of charm.
What has been said amounts to this: if it possesses attractiveness, then, as fashioned by another mode, it is subsumed under that other ornament. In the absence of attractiveness, it results in the utter lack of beauty.
Thus, the definition and illustration:
"Where from the statement concerning one, the meaning of another is understood, being characterized by the same qualifications —
that is declared to be <s>samāsokti</s> (condensed expression), because of its condensed meaning." As follows: [<s>Vakroktijīvita</s> Commentary 3.190]
"Broad-shouldered, straight, without crookedness, firm, bearing many great fruits —
this tree grew tall and was felled by the wind." [<s>Vakroktijīvita</s> Commentary 3.191]

children.text:
atra taroḥ mahāpuruṣasya ca dvayorapi mukhyatve mahāpuruṣapakṣe viśeṣaṇāni santīti viśeṣyābhidhāyi padāntaramabhidhātavyam /
athavā viśeṣaṇānyathānupapattyā pratīyamānatayā viśeṣyaṃ parikalpyate /
tadevaṃvidhakalpanasya sphuritaṃ na kiñciditi sphuṭameva śobhāśūnyatā /
tathāvidhasvabhāvayoranayoḥ prādhānyenaikavākyopāvarohayuktirabhidheyā, yataḥ parasparābhidhānasaṃbandhaṃ vinā na kiñcidetadupapadyate /
na ca kāmaripormūrtirumā vā jagat pāyādityanena nyāyena tayoḥ saṅgatirghaṭate, yasmāttatra dvayorapi parameśvarayoḥ pālanasāmarthyopapatteḥ tathāvidhasyāpyarthasyāpyucitatvenāśaṃsanīyatvāttathāvidhaśabdavācyatvānna kiñcidanupapannam /
etasmin punaḥ parasparābhisaṃbandhaṃ vinā tulyakālamekavākyopāvarohe na kiñcinnabandhanamiti yatkiṅkacidetat /
atha tathā kaścidevaṃvidho vidhinā pumān pātitaḥ, yathāyaṃ nabhasvatā taruḥ ityāśrīyate, tadevaṃ sphuṭamevopamānopameyabhāvaḥ /
tasmādalaṅkārānta (rāntar) bhāvaḥ (kena) vāryate /
yadi vā mahāpuruṣasya pratīyamāna (tve), vācyatayā tarurupapadyate, tadevamaprastutaprasaṃsaiṣā /
tasmātpunarapitadeva vyavasthitam /
viśeṣaṇā(nā)mubhayārthatve śleṣānupraveśo durnivāraḥ (iti) tenāpi tadevāpatati /
nidarśanāntaramapi samāsokteḥ pṛthakkṛtanibandhanaṃ yathā---
children.translated_text:
Here, since both the tree and the great man are primary [referents], and since qualifications exist for the great-man interpretation, another word specifying the qualified entity must be stated.
Alternatively, through the impossibility of the qualifications applying otherwise, the qualified entity is conceived as apprehended.
But the flash of such a conception amounts to nothing — hence the lack of beauty is evident.
The proper device for these two, whose nature is as described, is primarily the construal of descent into a single sentence, since without the relational connection of mutual expression, nothing here is possible.
Nor can the conjunction of the two be established by the principle 'May the form of the Enemy of <s>Kāma</s> (<s>Śiva</s>) or <s>Umā</s> protect the world,' because there, the capacity for protection being possible for both supreme deities, and because such a meaning too is appropriate and thus desirable, and because of being expressible by such words — nothing is inconsistent.
But here, without the mutual relation, there is no basis whatsoever for the descent of both into a single sentence simultaneously — hence this amounts to nothing.
If, on the other hand, it is taken as: 'Such-and-such a man was brought down by fate, just as this tree [was felled] by the wind,' then clearly there is the relation of standard and subject of comparison.
Therefore, who can prevent its subsumption under another figure?
Or if the great man is apprehended, the tree serves as the expressed meaning — then this is simply <s>aprastutapraśaṃsā</s> (praise of the irrelevant).
Therefore, once again, the same [conclusion] stands.
When the qualifications have dual reference, the entry of <s>śleṣa</s> (double meaning) is unavoidable — and through that too, the same result obtains.
Another illustration of <s>samāsokti</s>, showing the basis for its separate [treatment], is as follows:
"The <s>sandhyā</s> (twilight / union) is full of passion, the day (her husband) is before her, the lake (tears) is [near] —

children.text: aho daivagatiścitrā tathāpi na samāgamaḥ // VjivC_3.192 //
children.translated_text: alas, how wondrous is the course of fate — and yet there is no union!" [<s>Vakroktijīvita</s> Commentary 3.192]

children.text:
atra sandhyādivasayormukhyatayā prastutatvena, samānaviśeṣaṇaprastutakāntāvṛttāntapratītiḥ prastutayoḥ sāmyasamanvayāttathābhāvaṃ samarpayantī pratīyamānopamāsvarūpaṃ nāti vartate /
kāntāvṛttāntasya vā mukhyatayā pratīyamānatve sandhyādivasayorupadiśyamānatvamityaprastutapraśaṃsaiva /
"sahoktiśca nālaṅkāratayā matā" pūrvoktenaiva hetudvayena /
tathā ca lakṣaṇamudāharaṇaṃ caitasyāḥ---
children.translated_text: Here, since the twilight and the day are primarily the contextual subjects, the apprehension of the beloved's story — which is contextual through sharing the same qualifications — delivers such identity through the conformity of similarity between the two contextual subjects, and does not greatly exceed the nature of <s>pratīyamānopamā</s> (implied simile). Or, if the beloved's story is primarily apprehended, the twilight and day are being indicated — hence it is indeed <s>aprastutapraśaṃsā</s> (praise of the non-contextual). "And <s>sahokti</s> (co-expression) is not regarded as a figure" — for the very same two reasons stated earlier. And thus, the definition and illustration of this [figure] are:
Where two things, sharing the same temporal activity,

children.text: vākyenaikena kathyete sā sahoktirmatā yathā // VjivC_3.193 //
children.translated_text: Are spoken of in a single sentence — that is regarded as <s>sahokti</s> (co-expression); for example: // <s>Vjīv</s>C 3.193 //
"The nights, with directions made turbid by snowfall, causing tight embraces,

children.text: vṛddhimāyānti yāminyaḥ kāmināṃ prītibhiḥ saha // VjivC_3.194 //
children.translated_text: Increase together with the joys of lovers." // <s>Vjīv</s>C 3.194 //

children.text:
atra parasparasāmyasamanvayo manohāritānibandha (na) mityupamaiva tadabhāve, "śiṣyeṇa sahopādhyāyaḥ paṭhati", "putreṇa saha pitā tiṣṭhati " ityādau śobhāśūnyatve 'pi sā syāt /
tadevametayoḥ yuktiyuktamalaṅkaraṇatvamapasārya pramāṇopapannamabhidhatte /
tatra sahoktestāvat---
children.translated_text: Here, the mutual conformity of similarity is the basis of charm — hence it is indeed <s>upamā</s> (simile). In its absence, as in 'the teacher reads together with the student' or 'the father stands together with the son,' it would exist even where there is no beauty. Thus, having set aside the reasonably argued status of these two as figures, [the author] states what is established by valid reasoning. Among these, regarding <s>sahokti</s> first:
Where, by a single sentence, for the accomplishment of the meaning to be described,

children.text: uktiryugapadarthānāṃ sā sahoktiḥ satāṃ matā // Vjiv_3.52 //
children.translated_text: There is a simultaneous expression of [multiple] objects — that is <s>sahokti</s>, as recognized by the wise. // <s>Vjīv</s> 3.52 //

children.text:
yatretyādi /
sā sahoktiralaṅkṛtiḥ, "matā" = pratibhātā, "satāṃ" tadvidāṃ saṃmatetyarthaḥ /
kīdṛśī---"yatra" = yasyāṃ, "ekenaiva vākyena" abhinnenaiva padasamūhena "arthānāṃ" vākyārthatātparyabhūtānāṃ vastūnāṃ "yugapat" = tulyakālam "uktiḥ" = abhihitiḥ /
kimarthaṃ---"varṇanīyārthasiddhaye" = "varṇanīyasya" = pradhānatvena vivakṣitasyārthasya "siddhaye" = saṃpattaye /
tadidamuktaṃ bhavati---yatra vākyāntaravaktavyamapi vastu prastutārthaniṣpattaye vicchittyā tenaiva vākyenābhidhīyate /
yathā
children.translated_text: 'Where' etc. That <s>sahokti</s> is a figure of speech; 'recognized' means apprehended; 'by the wise' means approved by those learned [in this subject] — this is the meaning. Of what kind? — 'Where' = in which; 'by a single sentence' = by an undivided group of words; 'of objects' = of things that constitute the purport of the sentence-meaning; 'simultaneously' = at the same time; 'expression' = declaration. For what purpose? — 'For the accomplishment of the meaning to be described' = for the 'accomplishment' = attainment of the 'meaning' = thing 'to be described' = intended as primary. What is being said is this: where a thing that ought to be stated in another sentence is expressed with charm in that very sentence for the accomplishment of the contextual meaning. For example:

children.text: he hasta dakṣiṇa mṛtasya śiśordvijasya jīvātave visṛja śūdramunau kṛpāṇam /
children.translated_text: "O right hand! Release the sword upon the <s>Śūdra</s> sage, for the revival of the dead <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> boy.

children.text: rāmasya pāṇirasi nirbharagarbhakhinna- devīvivāsanapaṭoḥ karuṇā kutaste // VjivC_3.195 //
children.translated_text: You are the hand of <s>Rāma</s>, expert in the decree of banishing the queen pregnant and heavily burdened — whence would you have compassion?" // <s>Vjīv</s>C 3.195 //

children.text:
atra mukhyārthasiddhaye yad(vākyāṃntarā)bhidheyaṃ vastu vicchittyā tadekenaiva (vākyeno) panibaddham /
yadi ca nyāyyatvā davaśyaṃ karaṇīyamapi nikṛtilakṣaṇaṃ vastu karuṇāspadatvādakaraṇīyakalpaṃ (tathāpi) naivopekṣaṇīyānuṣṭhānam; nirbharagarbhakhinnadevīvivāsanapaṭoḥ dāśaratheḥ pāṇirasītyucitānurodhitvāt kutaste karuṇā(saṃbhavaḥ)tadavadhyasyāpi śūdramuneḥ brāhmaṇaśiśujīvitarakṣaṇāya maṇḍalāgraṃ samarpayetyekaṃ vastu /
dvitīyaṃ, yadi nyāyyamavaśyakaraṇīyamapi tathāvidhakāruṇikatvādudāracetasā na karaṇīyameveti manyase, tathāpi rāmasya nirbharagarbhakhinnadevīvivāsanapaṭoḥ niṣkaruṇacūḍāmaṇeḥ karastvamiti munimāraṇaṃ kiyanmātraṃ taveti vipralambhaśṛṅgāraparipoṣāt kimapi rāmaśabdasya rūḍhivaicitryavakratvamubhayatrāpi sphurati /
tathā ca---
children.translated_text: Here, for the accomplishment of the primary meaning, a thing [normally] to be expressed in another sentence is charmingly bound within a single sentence. Moreover, even if a thing characterized as cruelty must necessarily be done because it is just, and even if it should almost not be done because it is a ground for compassion, still it is an observance not to be neglected — because [the hand] is that of <s>Dāśaratha</s>'s son (<s>Rāma</s>), skilled in the decree of banishing the queen heavily burdened with pregnancy; hence, 'whence would you have compassion?' — due to conformity with propriety. Therefore, even that <s>Śūdra</s> sage who should not be killed — deliver the sword-point for the protection of the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> boy's life: this is one meaning. The second: if you think that even though it is just and must necessarily be done, still a noble-minded one should not do it because of such compassionate nature — even so, you are the hand of <s>Rāma</s>, the crest-jewel of the merciless, skilled in the decree of banishing the queen heavily pregnant — so what is the killing of a sage to you? Thus, from the nourishing of <s>vipralambhaśṛṅgāra</s> (love-in-separation), a certain obliqueness through the variety of the conventional meaning of the word '<s>Rāma</s>' shines forth in both [readings]. And thus:

children.text: ucyatāṃ sa vacanīyamaśeṣaṃ neśvare paruṣatā sakhi sādhvī /
children.translated_text: "Tell him everything that should be said — harshness toward a lord is not proper, friend;

children.text: ānayainamanunīya kathaṃ vā vipriyāṇi janayannanuneyaḥ // VjivC_3.196 //
children.translated_text: Bring him back conciliated — but how can one who causes displeasure be conciliated?" // <s>Vjīv</s>C 3.196 //

children.text: kiṃ gatena na hi yuktamupaituṃ kaḥ priye subhagamānini mānaḥ /
children.translated_text: "What use is his going? It is not fitting to approach [him]. What pride, O beloved one who considers yourself fortunate!

children.text: yoṣitāmiti kathāsu sametaiḥ kāmibhirbahurasā dhṛtirūhe // VjivC_3.197 //
children.translated_text: With such talk among women, the lovers who had gathered nourished a greatly savored steadfastness." // <s>Vjīv</s>C 3.197 //

children.text:
atra vicchittyā tātparyārthavācakamupanibaddham /
tathāhi---nāyikāyāḥ sakhyāścāvabaddhayorapi pratyekaṃ vallabhatatsandhānapravaṇatayā sakalameva vākyaṃ (vācaka) miti pratīyate /
yathā vā---
children.translated_text: Here, what conveys the purport-meaning is charmingly composed. For even though the heroine and her friend are in [separate] conversation, through the eagerness of each for reconciliation with the beloved, the entire sentence is perceived as expressive [of both]. Or for example:
"O lord of all kings, a woman was seen — beautiful in all limbs,

children.text: rāmā ramyā vanoddeśe mayā virahitā tvayā // VjivC_3.198 //
children.translated_text: Lovely, in a forest region — by me, [who am] separated from you." // <s>Vjīv</s>C 3.198 //

children.text:
atra pradhānabhūtavipralambhaśṛṅgārarasaparipoṣa (vicchitta) ye vākyārthadvayamupanibaddham /
nanu cānekārthasaṃbhave 'tra śleṣānupraveśaḥ kathaṃ na bhavatīti ? abhidhīyate /
tatra yasmāt dvayorekatarasya vā mukhyabhāve śleṣaḥ, atra punastathāvidhābhāvāt, bahūnāṃ dvayorvā sarveṣāṃ guṇabhāvaḥ pradhānārthaparatvenāvasānāt /
anyacca tasminnekenaiva śabdena yugapat pradīpaprakāśavadarthadvayaprakāśanaṃ śabdārthadvayaprakāśanaṃ veti śābdastatra sāmānyārtho vijṛmbhate /
sahoktau punastathāvidhasyāṅgabhāvādekenai(va) vākyena punaḥ punarāvartamānatayā vastvantaraprakāśanaṃ vidhīyate, tasmādāvṛttiratra śabda (sya) prādhānyatāṃ pratipadyate /
(yadi) "sarvakṣitibhṛtāṃ nātha" ityatra vākyaikadeśe śleṣānupraveśaḥ saṃbhavatītyucyate, tathāpi na kaściddoṣaḥ, yasmādalaṅkaraṇamalaṅkaraṇāntaraṃ kvacidaṅgabhāvaṃ gamayatīti /
atra vākyaikadeśe śleṣasyāṅgatvaṃ, mukhyabhāvaḥ punaḥ sahoktereva /
(nanu) tadevamāvṛttyā vastvantarāvagatau sahokteḥ sahabhāvābhāvādarthānyeparihāṇiḥ prasajyate, naitadasti /
yasmāt sahoktirityuktam, na punaḥ sahapratipattiriti /
tenātyantasahabhāvābhidhānameva (saṃ) pratipannamutkarṣāvagateriti na kiñcidasaṃbaddham /
children.translated_text: Here, for the charm of nourishing the <s>vipralambhaśṛṅgāra</s> (love-in-separation) <s>rasa</s>, which is the primary [element], a double sentence-meaning is composed. Now, if the objection is raised: 'When multiple meanings are possible, how does <s>śleṣa</s> (double meaning) not enter here?' — [the author] responds. Since <s>śleṣa</s> exists when both [meanings] or either one is primary, but here such primacy is absent — all the many or the two [meanings] are in a subordinate role, because they terminate in service to the primary meaning. Furthermore, in <s>śleṣa</s>, through a single word, the illumination of two meanings simultaneously — like a lamp's light — the general word-meaning shines forth there as either meaning-duality or word-meaning-duality. In <s>sahokti</s>, however, since such [simultaneity] is subordinate, through a single sentence recurring repeatedly, the illumination of another thing is accomplished — therefore repetition here attains the primacy of the word. If it is said that in 'O lord of all kings' there can be an entry of <s>śleṣa</s> in a portion of the sentence, even so there is no fault, since one figure sometimes assumes a subordinate role to another figure. Here <s>śleṣa</s> is subordinate in a portion of the sentence, while the primary status belongs to <s>sahokti</s> alone. Now, if [the objection is raised that] since through repetition another thing is apprehended, <s>sahokti</s> lacks simultaneous co-existence and thus there would be a deficiency in meaning — this is not so. Because it is called '<s>sahokti</s>' (co-expression), not '<s>sahapratipatti</s>' (co-apprehension). Therefore, the expression of utter simultaneity alone is accepted, and the apprehension of excellence [follows] — thus nothing is incongruous.
"Some call this <s>samāsokti</s> (condensed expression), some call it <s>sahokti</s> (co-expression);
Based on the connection of meaning, the learned [recognize] their distinctness." // <s>Vjīv</s>C 3.199 //

children.text:
ityantaraślokaḥ /
evaṃ guṇabhūtādapi svarūpotkarṣamāhātmyādalaṅkārasāmānyasvabhāvāt /
kāṃścidalaṅkārānamidhāyedānīṃ vibhūṣaṇatvādeva tathavidhān guṇabhūtānupakramate /
tatra dṛṣṭāntaṃ tāvadabhidhatte---
children.translated_text: This is an interpolated verse. Thus, even from [a figure] in a subordinate role, due to the greatness of its inherent excellence, because of the general nature of figuration — having described some figures, [the author] now introduces those which are subordinate as [genuine] embellishments. Among these, he first describes <s>dṛṣṭānta</s> (illustrative example):
Where, based on the similarity of things, there is a presentation of something else,
And where words like '<s>iva</s>' (like) etc. are impossible — that is called <s>dṛṣṭānta</s> (illustrative example). // <s>Vjīv</s> 3.53 //

children.text:
vastusāmyetyādi /
"yadanyasya" ("yasmāt") varṇyāt prastutāt "anyasya" vyatiriktavṛtteḥ padārthāntarasya "upadarśanam" = upanibandhanaṃ sa dṛṣṭāntanāmālaṅkāro 'bhidhīyate /
kathaṃ "vastusāmyaṃ samāśritya" "vastunoḥ" padārthayoḥ dṛṣṭāntadārṣṭāntikayoḥ "sāmyaṃ" sādṛśyaṃ "samāśritāya" nimittīkṛtya /
liṅgasaṃkhyāvibhaktisvarūpalakṣaṇasāmyavarjitamiti (bodhanārthaṃ) vastugrahaṇam /
"tatra" upante "ivādyasaṃbhave" sādṛśyābhidhāyināmivaprabhṛtīnāṃ virahe /
tadevamupamāyāḥ vācakamagre vyatiricyate /
yathā---
children.translated_text: 'Similarity of things' etc. 'Of something else' — 'other than' the thing to be described, i.e., the contextual [subject]; 'other' means belonging to a different domain; 'presentation' = composition — that figure named <s>dṛṣṭānta</s> is so called. How? — 'Based on the similarity of things' — 'of things' means of the two entities, namely the illustrative example and the thing to be illustrated; 'similarity' = resemblance; 'based on' = having as its cause. The word 'thing' (<s>vastu</s>) is used to exclude similarity of gender, number, case-ending, and form-characteristics. 'There' = in proximity; 'where <s>iva</s> etc. are impossible' = in the absence of words like <s>iva</s> that express resemblance. Thus, the marker of <s>upamā</s> (simile) is first distinguished. For example:

children.text: sarasijamanuviddhaṃ śaivalenāpi ramyaṃ malinamapi himāṃśorlakṣma lakṣmīṃ tanoti /
children.translated_text: "A lotus, even when pierced by <s>śaivāla</s> (moss), is lovely; even the stained mark of the cool-rayed [moon] bestows beauty.

children.text: iyamadhikamanojñā valkalenāpi tanvī kimiva hi madhurāṇāṃ maṇḍanaṃ nākṛtīnām // VjivC_3.200 //
children.translated_text: This slender woman is all the more charming even in bark-garments — for what indeed is not an adornment of beautiful forms?" // <s>Vjīv</s>C 3.200 //

children.text:
(atra) pādatrayamevodāharaṇaṃ, caturthe bhūṣaṇāntarasaṃbhavāt /
dṛṣṭāntamabhidhāya tatsaṃbhaddhavibhūṣaṇaprastāvāt samānacchāyamarthāntaranyāsamabhidhatte /
children.translated_text: Here, only the first three quarters serve as the illustration; in the fourth, another figure is possible. Having described <s>dṛṣṭānta</s>, from the occasion of a related figure with a similar character, he describes <s>arthāntaranyāsa</s> (corroborative statement):
The placement of another sentence-meaning, on account of similarity of primary purport,
Should be known as <s>arthāntaranyāsa</s> — that which is employed in a corroborative capacity. // <s>Vjīv</s> 3.54 //

children.text:
vākyārthetyādi /
"jñeyaḥ sor'thāntaranyāsaḥ" = (arthāntaranyāsa) nāmālaṅkāro "jñeyaḥ" = parijñātavyaḥ /
kīdṛśaḥ---"vākyārthāntaravinyāsaḥ"---parasparānvitapadasamudāyābhidheyaṃ vastu vākyārthaḥ tasmādanyasmāt = aprakṛtatvāt prastutavyatireki vākyārthāntaraṃ, tasya "vinyāsaḥ" = viśiṣṭaṃ nyasanaṃ = tadvidāhlādakāritayopanibandhaḥ /
kasmāt kāraṇāt "mukhyatātparyasāmyataḥ"," mukhyaṃ" = prastāvādhikṛtatvāt pradhānabhūtaṃ vastu, tasya "tātparyaṃ" = yatparatvena tatsaṃmataṃ, tasya "sāmyataḥ" = sādṛśyāt /
kathaṃ "samar(pakata) yāhitaḥ" = samarpakatvenopanibaddhaḥ, tadupapattiyojaneneti yāvat /
atra sāmānye samarthanīye viśeṣaḥ samarthako, viśeṣe vā sāmānyaṃ, (ta) yoḥ parasparāvyabhicārāt /
yathā---
children.translated_text: 'Sentence-meaning' etc. 'Should be known as <s>arthāntaranyāsa</s>' = the figure named <s>arthāntaranyāsa</s> should be recognized. Of what kind? — 'The placement of another sentence-meaning' — the 'sentence-meaning' is the thing expressible by a group of mutually connected words; 'another' than that, i.e., non-contextual, different from the contextual; 'of another sentence-meaning'; its 'placement' = distinguished composition = a binding that produces delight in the learned. For what reason? — 'On account of similarity of primary purport' — 'primary' = the thing that is chief due to being the topic of the occasion; its 'purport' = that toward which it is directed, which is approved; 'on account of its similarity' = because of its resemblance. How? — 'Employed in a corroborative capacity' = composed as corroborative, i.e., through the application of its proof. Here, when a general [statement] is to be established, the particular serves as corroboration; or when a particular [is to be established], the general [serves as corroboration] — because of the non-deviation between the two. For example:
"Without doubt, she is worthy of a <s>Kṣatriya</s>'s hand — for my mind desires noble things in her.

children.text: satāṃ hi sandehapadeṣu vastuṣu pramāṇamantaḥ karaṇapravṛttayaḥ // VjivC_3.201 //
children.translated_text: For, of the wise, in matters of doubt, the inclinations of the inner faculty are the authority." // <s>Vjīv</s>C 3.201 //
Or for example:
"For what indeed is not an adornment of beautiful forms?" // <s>Vjīv</s>C 3.202 //

Having thus described <s>arthāntaranyāsa</s>, from the occasion of a related figure with a similar character — through the connection of sentences pertaining to a particular subject — he describes <s>ākṣepa</s> (repudiation):
An <s>ākṣepa</s> (repudiation), with the semblance of a prohibition, [employed] to manifest a supreme beauty

children.text: ākṣepa iti sa jñeyaḥ prastutasyaiva vastunaḥ // Vjiv_3.55 //
children.translated_text: Of the very contextual thing — that should be known as <s>ākṣepa</s>. // <s>Vjīv</s> 3.55 //

children.text:
niṣedhacchāyayetyādi /
"ākṣepa iti sa jñeyaḥ" = so 'pyamākṣepālaṅkārojñātavyaḥ /
sa kīdṛśaḥ---"prastutasyaiva vastunaḥ ākṣepaḥ" = prakṛtasyaivārthasya ākṣepaḥ = apākaraṇam = abhipretasyārthasyāpi nivartanamiti (yāvat) /
kayā ? "niṣedhacchāyayā" = pratiṣedhavicchittyā /
kimartham ? "kāntiṃ prathayituṃ parāṃ" = prakṛṣṭāmupaśobhāṃ prakaṭayitum /
yathā---
children.translated_text: 'With the semblance of a prohibition' etc. 'That should be known as <s>ākṣepa</s>' = that figure named <s>ākṣepa</s> should be recognized. Of what kind? — '<s>Ākṣepa</s> of the very contextual thing' = the repudiation = removal = the turning away even of the intended meaning of the very contextual [subject]. By what means? — 'With the semblance of a prohibition' = with the charm of a negation. For what purpose? — 'To manifest a supreme beauty' = to make evident an excellent adornment. For example:

children.text: suhaa vilaṃvasu thoaṃ jāva imaṃ virahakāaraṃ hiaaṃ /
children.translated_text: "O handsome one, delay a little while, until this heart, trembling with separation,

children.text: saṃṭhaviūṇa bhaṇissaṃ ahavā volesu kiṃ bhaṇimo // VjivC_3.203 //
children.translated_text: Is steadied — then I shall speak. Or rather, depart — what shall we say to the heartless?" // <s>Vjīv</s>C 3.203 //

children.text:
subhaga vilambasva stokaṃ yāvadidaṃ virahakātaraṃ hṛdayam /
saṃsthāpya bhaṇiṣyāmyathavāpakrama kiṃ bhaṇāmaḥ /
(iti chāyā)
children.translated_text: (Sanskrit reconstruction:) "O handsome one, delay a little while, until this heart, trembling with separation, is steadied — then I shall speak. Or rather, depart — what shall we say?"

children.text:
atra vākyārthaḥ--- subhageti bahuvallabhatāpratipādanaparamāmantraṇapadam /
(nāyikāprativacanaṃ) nāsūtritam, (taddhi) sākṣādabhidhīyamānatayā na tathā cetanacamatkāritāṃ pratipadyate, yathaitadākṣepamātraṃ bhaṇitivaicitryeṇa pratīyamānatayā niyamāt tadvidāhlādavidhāyitvaṃ puṣṇāti /
tadevamākṣepasvarūpamabhidhāya sādhāraṇavaktavyaśeṣameteṣāmabhidhatte---
children.translated_text: Here the sentence-meaning is: '<s>Subhaga</s>' (O handsome one) — this is an address whose purpose is to convey [his] being beloved by many. The heroine's response is not explicitly stated, for if directly expressed, it would not produce the same delight of consciousness as this mere <s>ākṣepa</s> (repudiation) does, which — being apprehended through the charm of varied expression — necessarily nourishes the capacity to produce delight in the learned. Having thus described the nature of <s>ākṣepa</s>, [the author] states what remains to be said in common about these [figures]:
These three — <s>dṛṣṭānta</s> and the rest — arise according to the speaker's intention, with reference to what is yet to be said or already stated,
Whether or not a [logical] reason is present. // <s>Vjīv</s> 3.56 //

children.text:
vakṣyamāṇetyādi /
vakṣyamāṇoktau viṣayau yeṣāṃ te vakṣyamāṇoktaviṣayāḥ, "dṛṣṭāntaprabhṛtayaśca "trayo 'pyete" abhidhāsyamānābhihitagocarāḥ saṃbhavantīti saṃbandhaḥ /
kena hetunā"vivakṣayā" = vaktumicchayā = kaveryathāpratibhāsamabhidhātuṃ vāñchayā /
tadidamatra tātparyam---yadā saṃniveśavaicitryamātrametanna punaratra lakṣaṇātirekaḥ kaścidasti /
madhyamasya viśeṣāntaramabhidhātumāha--- "hetau satyathavāsati" hetāviti /
"hetau" hetuvācini hiśabdādau "sati" saṃbhavati = pramujyamāne, "athavā" kadācit, "asati" asabhavati---aprayujyamāne /
evaṃ (hetorabhidhānenānabhidhānena) vārthāntaranyāsaḥ prakāradvayena vidyate /
arthāntaranyāsamātramabhibhūṣaṇamityarthaḥ /
nidarśanajātamatra pūrvoktavyatireki na pradarśitam, tasmātsvayamevotprekṣaṇīyam /
evaṃ svarūpaviśeṣapratiṣedhabodhitachāyātiśayamalaṅkaraṇamabhidhāya kāraṇapratiṣedhottejita(chāyā)tiśayamabhidhatte---
children.translated_text: 'About to be stated' and so forth. Those whose subjects are about to be stated — 'these three too, beginning with <s>dṛṣṭānta</s> (example)' — [the author] will describe...
For the nourishment of beauty, through the prior abandonment of one's own cause,
the vivification of the meaning to be expressed by some particular [quality] — this is <s>vibhāvanā</s> (poetic causation). // Vjiv_3.57 //

children.text:
svakāraṇetyādi /
"arthasya" varṇanīyasya = prastutasya, "viśeṣeṇa kenāpi" alaukikena rūpāntareṇa "bhāvanā" = "vibhāvanā" vibhāvanetyalaṅkṛtirabhidhīyate /
tadayamatrārthaḥ---yā vinā bhāvyate, kā sā ? tatsamarthakāraṇarūpaprayojakavyāpāralakṣaṇāṃ kriyāṃ (vinā bhāvyate sā) vibhāvanā /
"svakāraṇaparityagapūrvakam" = tasya viśeṣasya svamātmīyaṃ kāraṇaṃ yannimittaṃ tasya parityāgaḥ prihāṇaṃ pūrvaṃ prathamaṃ yatra tatkṛtetyarthaḥ /
kimarthaṃ "kāntipuṣṭaye" śobhā(vṛddhaye) /
tadidamuktaṃ bhavati---yathā lokottaraviśiṣṭatāṃ varṇanīyaṃ nīyate iti /
yathā---
children.translated_text: 'Of one's own cause' and so forth. 'Of the meaning' — of the thing being described, the subject at hand; 'by some particular' — by some extraordinary, unprecedented form; 'vivification' (<s>bhāvanā</s>) is '<s>vibhāvanā</s>'...
Her body's ornament was not artificially gathered, O beauty; the instrument of her intoxication was not called a drink;

children.text: kāmasya puṣpavyatiriktamastraṃ bālyātparaṃ sātha vayaḥ prapede // VjivC_3.204 //
children.translated_text: the weapon of <s>Kāma</s> (Love) was other than flowers — beyond childhood she attained the next age. // VjivC_3.204 //

children.text:
atra kṛtrimakāraṇaparityāgapūrvakaṃ lokottarasahajaviśeṣaviśiṣṭatā varṇanīyasya kaverabhipretā /
tadevamasaṃbhāvyakāraṇatvādavibhāvyamānasvabhāvāṃ vibhāvanāṃ vicārya vicāragocarasvarūpatayā svarūpasandehasamarpitātiśayaṃ sasandehamabhidhatte---
children.translated_text: Here, the poet intends to describe the subject as distinguished by an extraordinary innate particularity, preceded by the abandonment of the artificial cause. Thus, through the cause that is inconceivable...
In which the imagined form, due to the possibility of another <s>utprekṣā</s> (imaginative fancy),

children.text: sandehamete vicchittyai sasandehaṃ vadanti tam // Vjiv_3.58 //
children.translated_text: [produces] doubt — those [critics] call that, for the sake of beauty, '<s>sasandeha</s>' (the doubtful). // Vjiv_3.58 //

children.text:
yasminnityādi /
"yasmin" = alakāre, "utprekṣitaṃ" saṃbhāvanānumānāt sāmyasamanvayācca svarūpāntarasamāropadvāreṇa pratibhollekhitaṃ "rūpaṃ" padārthaparispandalakṣaṇaṃ "sandehameti" saṃśayaṃ samārohati /
kasmāt kāraṇāt---"utprekṣāntarasaṃbhavāt" = utprekṣāprakarṣaparasyāparasyāpitadviṣayasya sadbhāvāt /
kimarthaṃ---"vicchittyai" = śobhāyai /
tadevamabhidhāvaicitryaṃ sasandehābhidhānaṃ vadanti /
yathā---
children.translated_text: 'In which' and so forth. 'In which' — in that ornament; 'imagined' — through conjectural inference and through the correlation of similarity, presented through the door of superimposing another form...

children.text: rañjitā nu vividhāstaruśailāḥ nāmitaṃ nu gaganaṃ sthāgitaṃ nu /
children.translated_text: Are the varied trees and mountains colored, or is the sky bent down, or is it covered?

children.text: pūritā nu viṣameṣu dharitrī saṃhṛtā nu kakubhastimireṇa // VjivC_3.205 //
children.translated_text: Is the earth filled in the uneven places, or are the quarters gathered up — by darkness? // VjivC_3.205 //
Or for example:
With half-closed, one-eyed, rolling glances, their bodies trembling as they approached their beloved,

children.text: nimajjatīnāṃ śvasitoddhatastanaḥ śramo nu tāsāṃ madano nu paprathe // VjivC_3.206 //
children.translated_text: their breasts heaving with sighing, sinking [in the water] — was it fatigue of those [women], or was it <s>Madana</s> (Love) that spread? // VjivC_3.206 //
Or for example:
[Prakrit:] 'With the arrow-bearing [god of love] whose form is imperceptible, [the season] slowly [works upon] the people...

children.text: bhisvai śiśāve guṇaā muhā sarvayanti ahaṇarai tam // VjivC_3.207 //
children.translated_text: for frightening the young maidens, virtues, the faces — all are put on display by the shafts.' // VjivC_3.207 //
(<s>Chāyā</s>?) Or for example:

Is it the sole jewel in the treasury of the world amassed with the great wealth of beauty by the Creator? Is it this lotus of the lake of <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic sentiment)? Is it the limit of delicacy?

children.text: kiṃ lāvaṇyapayonidherabhinavaṃ bimbaṃ sudhādīdhiter- vaktuṃ kāntatatamānanaṃ tava mayā sāmyaṃ na niścīyate // VjivC_3.208 //
children.translated_text: Is it the new disc of the nectar-moon of the ocean of charm? — To describe the beauty of your face, O beloved, no likeness can be determined by me. // VjivC_3.208 //

The <s>sasandeha</s> (doubtful) is of a single type, because it is rooted in <s>utprekṣā</s>. Having thus described the <s>sasandeha</s>, beautiful through the doubt about its essential nature, he describes the <s>apahṇuti</s> (denial), charming through the concealment of its essential nature:
In order to exhibit another form of the thing being described,
in which there is a denial of its own nature — that is regarded as <s>apahṇuti</s> (denial). // Vjiv_3.59 //

children.text:
anyādityādi /
pūrvavadutprekṣāmūlatvamevāsyāḥ /
saṃbhāvanānumānāt sādṛśyasamanvayācca "varṇanīyasya vastunaḥ" = prastutasyārthasya, "anyat" = kimapyapūrvaṃ, "rūpamarpayitum" = rūpāntaraṃ samāropayituṃ, "svarūpāpahnavaḥ" = svabhāvāpalāpaḥ saṃbhavati, "yasyām" "asau" = eṣā evaṃvidhabhaṇitireva, "apahnatiḥ" "matā" = pratibhātā tadvidām /
yathā--
children.translated_text: 'Another' and so forth. As before, this too is rooted in <s>utprekṣā</s>. Through conjectural inference and through the correlation of similarity, 'of the thing being described' — the subject at hand...
This radiant one is the eye of the whole world, the foremost among the luminous — it is not the most beautiful moon with its pleasing eye-festival borrowed from a lovely face.

children.text: paryāyeṇa manobhuvā virahiṇāṃ veddhuṃ mano nirdayaṃ puṣpeṣūnniśitāgratāṃ vijayinī netuṃ niyakto mama // VjivC_3.209 //
children.translated_text: It is appointed by <s>Manobhū</s> (Love) to pierce mercilessly the minds of those separated [from their beloved], in turn — my victorious one, to bring the arrow-tips of his flower-shafts to sharpness! // VjivC_3.209 //
Where, with the property-bearer remaining in its own form, only the property is denied — an example:

children.text: tava kusumaśaratvaṃ śītaraśmitvamindoḥ dvayamidamayathārthaṃ dṛśyate madvidheṣu /
children.translated_text: Your being the flower-arrowed one, and the moon's being the cool-rayed one — both of these appear untrue to people like me;
for the moon shoots fire with its frost-bearing rays, and you too make your flower-arrows hard as diamond! // VjivC_3.210 //

children.text:
atra bhaṇitivaicitryavaśādaśābdam apahnavapratipādanaṃ vihitam, yasmāddharmasya kusumaśaratvādeḥ svabhāvasamucitaṃ sukumārakāryakāritvamapasārya tadviruddhamatikarālakāryakāritvamupanibaddham /
kvacicca sādṛśyasamanvayādapahnatiryathā---
children.translated_text: Here, through the force of the variety of expression, the conveyance of denial is accomplished without [using the word 'not'], since the natural delicacy appropriate to the nature of the property — the flower-arrowed-ness and the like...

children.text: pūrṇendoḥ paripoṣakāntavapuṣaḥ sphāraprabhābhāsuraṃ nedaṃ maṇḍalamabhuyudeti gaganābhoge jigīṣorjagat /
children.translated_text: This disc, blazing with expansive radiance, of the full moon whose body is beautified by the nourishment of fullness, does not rise again in the expanse of the sky of one who desires to conquer the world.

It is the fitting parasol of <s>Māra</s> (Love), now pale with the beauty of twilight — [the parasol] of the sole war-elephant exerting himself to crush the pride of those haughty with self-esteem. // VjivC_3.211 //

children.text: evamalaṅkārāṇāṃ tantratayā pratyekamalaṅkāryaṃ prati vicchittividhāyitvamabhidhāyedānīṃ samuditānāṃ tadevābhidhatte---
children.translated_text: Having thus described the capacity of individual ornaments to produce beauty with respect to the ornamentable, each in its own thread, he now describes the same for combined [ornaments]:
Where ornaments shine forth with their operations mutually intertwined,

children.text: yathā padārthā vākyārthe saṃsṛṣṭiḥ sābhidīyate // Vjiv_3.60 //
children.translated_text: just as words [shine] in the sentence-meaning — that is called <s>saṃsṛṣṭi</s> (confluence). // Vjiv_3.60 //

children.text:
rājantītyādi /
"yatra" = yasyām,"alaṅkārāḥ" = prastutasaṃpadupetāḥ santaḥ "rājanti" śobhante, "saṃsṛṣṭiḥ sābhidhīyate" saṃsṛṣṭisaṃjñālaṅkṛtiḥ socyate /
kathaṃ rājantītyāha---"yatā padārthā vākyārthe" = tātparyalakṣaṇe vastuni "yathā" = yena prikāreṇa "padārthāḥ" pravibhaktasvarūpāḥ vākyaikadeśabhūtapadābhidheyāḥ santovā svātmanā sphuranto 'pi parasparānvayalakṣaṇasaṃbandhanibandhanasvabhāvāḥ pradhāne hi pāratantryamanubhavantastadeva samudāyātmakamekavākyārthatātparyaṃ pratipādayanti, yathā tena prakāreṇa yadetayoravisaṃvādisamavāye saṃbandhitayā saṃsṛṣṭāvanyonyānvitavṛttayaḥ parasparasaṃbandhāvagatasāmarthyāt pṛthagbhūtavākyārthāvayavaikadeśavartino 'pyalaṅkārāḥ kāmapi sahṛdayasaṃvedyaparasparasaṃsargātmatāmevaṃ (va) sakalavākyārthaviṣayāṃ vicchittimupapādayantaḥ paratantrāḥ parisphuranti ityabhiprāyaḥ /
yathā---
children.translated_text: 'They shine forth' and so forth. 'Where' — in which [expression]; 'ornaments,' being endowed with the fitness of the subject, 'shine forth' — look beautiful; 'that is called <s>saṃsṛṣṭi</s>' — this is spoken of as <s>saṃsṛṣṭi</s>...

children.text: āśliṣṭo navakuṅkumāruṇaravivyālokitairvistṛto lambāntāmbarayā sametya bhuvane dhyānāntare sandhyayā /
children.translated_text: Embraced, expanded by the glances of the freshly-saffron-reddened sun, having met with twilight — of trailing garments, in the interval of meditation — upon the earth;

now the onset of evening, with bees [of] falling darkness swarming around the budding ray-tips of moonbeams, appears like a <s>kuravaka</s> tree whose <s>dohada</s> (longing) has been fulfilled by the goddess. // VjivC_3.212 //

children.text:
atra rūpakādinā svātmanā pṛthakkṛtakṛtyena parasparasaṃsargasaṃpadupārjitā vākyārthavakratāvicchittiḥ kācideva parisphurati /
yathā vā---
children.translated_text: Here, with <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor) and the like, each having separately accomplished its own function, a certain design of sentence-meaning obliquity, acquired through the wealth of mutual conjunction, shines forth...

children.text: mlāniṃ vāntaviṣānalena nayanavyāpāralabdhātmanā nītā rājabhujaṅga pallavamṛdū rambhā tatheyaṃ tvayā /
children.translated_text: O royal serpent, this <s>rambhā</s> (plantain), whose sprouts are tender, has been led to withering by you — by the fire of your venom-glance, which takes its form through the operation of the eye.

children.text: adyāpīśvaraśekharendukiraṇasmerasthalīlāñchite kailāsopavane yathā sugahane naiti prarohaṃ punaḥ // VjivC_3.213 //
children.translated_text: Even now, in the garden of <s>Kailāsa</s>, densely beautiful, adorned with the smiling moonbeam-meadows of the Lord's crest-moon, it does not sprout again. // VjivC_3.213 //

children.text:
atra pūrvavadeva rūpakādīnāṃ parasparasaṃsargasaṃpadupārjitā vakratāvicchittiḥ vibhāvyate /
evaṃ saṃsṛṣṭimabhidhāya tathāvidhacchāyāvicchittividhāyinaṃ saṃkarālaṅkāramabhidhatte---
children.translated_text: Here, as before, the design of obliquity acquired through the wealth of the mutual conjunction of <s>rūpaka</s> and the like is perceived. Having thus described <s>saṃsṛṣṭi</s> (confluence), he now describes its counterpart [<s>saṃkara</s>]:
This complex of ornaments, having become mixed (<s>saṃkīrṇa</s>) by [the intervention of] others,
flashing forth in manifold ways in the sentence — that is called <s>saṃkara</s> (mixture). // Vjiv_3.61 //

children.text:
alaṅkāretyādi /
pūrvoktalakṣaṇamākrāntavṛttiḥ "alakārakalāpo 'yaṃ" rasavadādyalaṅkāranikurambaḥ "saṃkarākhyo 'bhidhīyate" saṃkaranāmā nigadyate /
kīdṛśaḥ---"saṃkīrṇatāṃ gataḥ" = saṃmiśratāṃ prāptaḥ, sabalatvena pratibhāsatvamadhirūḍhaḥ /
kiṃ kurvan---"sphuran" = ātmanaḥ sphuritaṃ samupadarśayan---pratibhāsamānatāmupasaran,"vākye" saṃkīrṇatāmupapadyate /
tatsaṃveśanaviśeṣasyānupapatteḥ bhaṇitāntarvarto yaḥ kaścidalaṅkāro yathopapatti vibhūṣaṇāntareṇa saṃkīrṇaḥ saṃkara saṃjñāviṣayatāṃ pratipadyate /
tena sakalasyāpyalaṅkārakalāpasya (saṃkara ityabhidhānaṃ saṃpadyate) /
yathā---
children.translated_text: 'The complex of ornaments' and so forth. This complex of ornaments — this cluster of ornaments beginning with <s>rasavat</s> — whose operation conforms to the previously stated characteristic — 'is called <s>saṃkara</s>'...

children.text: rohanmūlātigaurairuragapatiphaṇaistatra pātālakukṣau prodyadvālaṅkuraśrīḥ diśi diśi daśanairebhirāśāgajānām /
children.translated_text: With the exceedingly white hoods of the serpent-king rising from the root in the cavity of the netherworld, with the beauty of rising young-sprout-splendor, in direction after direction, upon the tusks of the elephants of the quarters,

children.text: asminnākāśadeśe vikasitakusumā rāśibhistārakāṇaāṃ nātha tvatkīrtivallī phalati phalamidaṃ bimbamindoḥ sudhārdram // VjivC_3.214 //
children.translated_text: in this expanse of the sky, with clusters of blossoming flower-stars — O Lord, your fame-creeper bears this fruit: the moist-with-nectar disc of the moon. // VjivC_3... //

children.text:
atra kīrtivallīti rūpakālaṅkāraḥ siddhabaddhatatsāmyāśaṅkāṃ vinā na yuktayuktatāṃ pratipadyate /
tena tadāśaṅkānibandhanatathāvidhaparispandakīrtisandarśitasamudbhutatasaṃbhāvanānumānamāhātmyāt pratīyamānavṛttirutprekṣātra kaverabhipretā /
yasmādetayordvayorapi parasparasaṃbhāvanāṃ vinā svarūpalabdhireva na (parya) vasyatīti, saṃkīrṇayoratha saṃvādādevaṃvidhaviṣaye saṃkaroktiḥ pravartate /
vākyaikadeśe yathā "nirmokamuktiriva gaganoragasya" iti niṣkampatayā vyavahartumaśakyatvāt, nirmokamuktirivetyutprekṣayā rūpakālaṅkārasya svarūpalābhāvakāśaḥ (samarpyate) /
tathaivotprekṣāyāḥ, yasmādatrāpi saṃkarālaṅkāravyavahāraḥ /
nanu cānenanyāyena "asyāḥ sargavidhau" iti "kiṃ tāruṇyataroḥ" ityādeḥ saṃkarālaṅkāroktiḥ pravartatām ? na pravartate, yasmādatrār (thasāmarthyāvagato) tprekṣāyāḥ sasandehaṃ vinānupapatteḥ, parasmiṃśca tathaiva rūpakasyeti dvayorapyetayoḥ tattvaṃ tulyam /
sasandehasya punastadvibhūṣaṇatvenāntarvidhāne maṇimayapadakabandhabandhurahārādiramaṇīyatvamityuktameva /
saṃsṛṣṭernānāvidhacchāyamaṇimālāmanoharatā, saṃṅkarālaṅkārasya vividhakāntiratnavinyāsavictrabahulātulakāntikalpatvamiti sarvameva vibhaktam /
evaṃ yathopapattyalaṅkārān lakṣayitvā keṣāñcidalakṣitatvāt lakṣaṇāvyāptidoṣaṃ parihartumupakramate /
children.translated_text: Here, the <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor) figure in 'fame-creeper' does not attain the quality of being well-reasoned without the suspicion of resemblance with something already established. Therefore, from the greatness of the probable inference arising from the imagined possibility that is generated by the contemplation of such an activity — this <s>utprekṣā</s> (poetic fancy), whose function is suggested, is what the poet intends here. Because without the mutual imagined possibility of both [rūpaka and utprekṣā], the acquisition of their essential nature itself does not come to completion; therefore, when the two are intermixed, in such a domain, the designation '<s>saṃkara</s> (confusion) of figures' applies — from their concordance. In one part of a sentence, as in 'like the shedding of the slough of the serpent of the sky' — because one cannot proceed confidently — through the <s>utprekṣā</s> 'as if a shedding of the slough,' scope is provided for the acquisition of the essential nature of the <s>rūpaka</s> figure. Similarly for the <s>utprekṣā</s>, because here too the designation '<s>saṃkara</s> of figures' applies. Now, 'should the designation of <s>saṃkara</s> of figures be applied to verses like 'asyāḥ sargavidhau' and 'kiṃ tāruṇyataroḥ' by this same reasoning?' — It should not, because there <s>utprekṣā</s>, understood from the power of meaning, is impossible without the element of doubt (<s>sasandeha</s>), and in the other case likewise for <s>rūpaka</s> — thus the reality of both is the same. And regarding <s>sasandeha</s> (doubt), its internal placement as an ornament of those [figures] produces a beauty like that of a necklace bound with settings of jewel-studded medallions — this has already been stated. Of <s>saṃsṛṣṭi</s> (conjunction), the charm is like that of a garland of diverse-hued jewels; of the <s>saṃkara</s> figure, the beauty is like an incomparable, brilliant [ornament] with the arrangement of jewels of varied lustre — thus everything has been distinguished. Having thus characterized ornaments as appropriate, [the author] now undertakes to remove the defect of under-extension of the definition, since some [putative ornaments] have not been characterized —
Because of their being [identical to] another ornament, and because of their being devoid of beauty —
certain [so-called] ornaments are not considered ornaments in the least. // <s>Vjīv</s> 3.62 //

children.text:
bhūṣaṇetyādi /
"ye" = pūrvoktavyatiriktāḥ"kecidalaṅkārāḥ" te "nālaṅkāratayā manāk" na vibhūṣaṇatvenābhyupagatāḥ /
kena hetunā "bhūṣaṇāntarabhāvena" = anyadbhūṣaṇaṃ "bhūṣaṇāntaraṃ", tebhyo vyatiriktam; "tadbhāvena" = tatsvabhāvatvena tadananyatvena pūrvoktānāmevānyatamatvenetyarthaḥ /
"śobhāśūnyatayā tathā" = śobhā kānatiḥ tayā śūnyaṃ rahitaṃ śobhāśūnya tasya bhāvaḥ śobhāśūnyatā tayā hetubhūtayā /
na kevalaṃ tābhyāmeva, yāvadalaṅkāryatayā vibhūṣyatvenāpi teṣāmalaṅkaraṇatvamanupapannam /
evaṃ ca---
children.translated_text: 'Because of their being' and so forth. 'Certain ornaments' — different from those stated before — 'are not considered ornaments in the least' — are not accepted as adornments. For what reason? — 'Because of their being another ornament' — because of their identity with another ornament, with those different [ornaments stated before], meaning: because of their being just one of the previously stated [figures]. 'Because of their being devoid of beauty likewise' — 'beauty' is lustre; 'devoid of that' means lacking it; 'the state of being devoid of beauty' — by that, as the cause. Not only by those two [reasons], but also because of their being the thing adorned (<s>alaṅkārya</s>) — i.e., the thing to be adorned — their status as ornament is untenable. And thus —
<s>Yathāsaṃkhya</s> (enumeration-in-order), the ornament that was proclaimed by earlier [masters] —
by both causes, that is not considered an ornament. // <s>Vjīv</s> 3.63 //

children.text:
"yathāsaṃkhyamalaṅkāraḥ pūrvairāmnātaḥ" tulya (kramaṃ) kaiścitsvaśabdenābhihitaḥ svanāmnā "sa nālaṅkāraḥ,kāraṇadvitayenāpi" bhūṣaṇāntarabhāvena śobhāśūnyatayā ca /
tathā ca tasyodāharaṇam---
children.translated_text: '<s>Yathāsaṃkhya</s> (enumeration-in-order), proclaimed by the earlier [masters]' — equal-sequence, named by some with its own name — 'that is not an ornament, by both causes' — by being [identical to] another ornament, and by being devoid of beauty. And thus an example of it —
Lotus, moon, bee, elephant, male cuckoo, peacock —
by your face, beauty, eye, gait, voice, and hair, they are conquered. // <s>Vjīv</s>C 3.215 //

children.text:
atrātmakṛtalakṣye bhaṇitivaicitryavirahāt na kācit kāntirvidyate /
satyāmapyetasyāṃ sāmyaṃ vyatireko vā jīvitamāmnātaṃ na punaḥ samānasaṃkhyātvam /
(kevala) samānasaṃkhyātve "yathāsaṃkhyamanudeśaḥ samānām" iti sūtrodāharaṇanyāyāt saṃkhyātānudeśāt na kiñcidatiricyate /
keṣāñcidāśīḥ prabhṛtīnāmalaṅkāratayā matānāṃ bhūṣaṇatvānupapatteḥ /
āsiṣastu lakṣaṇodāharaṇāni neha paṭhyante /
teṣu cāśaṃsanīyasyaivārthasya mukhyatayā varṇanīyatvādalaṅkāryatvamiti preyolaṅkāroktāni dūṣaṇānyāpatanti /
children.translated_text: Here, in what is [supposedly] a self-made criterion, there is no beauty whatsoever due to the absence of variety of expression. And even granting [the figure], the life of the matter is claimed to be resemblance or dissimilarity, not equal-numberedness. Mere equal-numberedness, by the maxim of the grammatical rule 'yathāsaṃkhyam anudeśaḥ samānām' — through the mere enumeration of counted items — adds nothing. Because certain [supposed figures] like <s>āśīḥ</s> (benediction) and the rest, accepted as ornaments [by some], are untenable as adornments. Definitions and examples of <s>āśīḥ</s> are not read here. And in those, since the desirable content is principally what is to be depicted, they have the status of being the thing adorned (<s>alaṅkārya</s>) — hence the objections stated regarding the <s>preyas</s> ornament apply —
There would be no contradiction with <s>preyas</s> when another ornament is present;
even from the non-observation elsewhere, <s>saṃsṛṣṭi</s> (conjunction) and <s>saṃkara</s> (confusion) would result. // <s>Vjīv</s>C 3.216 //

(Interpolated verse.) Also for <s>viśeṣokti</s> (special statement), because of its subsumption under the previously stated ornament, and because of its being the thing adorned — the status of being an ornament is untenable. And thus an example of it —
He alone, <s>Kusumāyudha</s> (the Flower-armed Love-god), conquers the three worlds;

children.text: haratāpi tanuṃ yasya śambhunā na hṛtaṃ balam // VjivC_3.217 //
children.translated_text: even though <s>Śambhu</s> (<s>Śiva</s>) destroyed his body, his power was not taken away. // <s>Vjīv</s>C 3.217 //

children.text:
atra sakalalokaprasiddhajayitvavyatirekikandarpasvabhāvamātraṃ lokottaratvena vākyārthaḥ /
(evaṃ) sūkṣmaleśahetavaḥ (nālaṅkārāḥ /
tathā ca) bhāmahaḥ---
children.translated_text: Here, the sentence-meaning is merely the well-known-to-all-the-world nature of <s>Kandarpa</s> — his being victorious to an extraordinary degree. Similarly, <s>sūkṣma</s> (the subtle), <s>leśa</s> (the trace), and <s>hetu</s> (the reason) are not ornaments. And thus <s>Bhāmaha</s> —
'<s>Hetu</s> (reason), <s>sūkṣma</s> (the subtle), and <s>leśa</s> (the trace) are not considered ornaments,'
'because they fail to express <s>vakrokti</s> (oblique expression) of the collective meaning.' // <s>Vjīv</s>C 3.218 //
And thus an example of <s>sūkṣma</s> (the subtle) —
Knowing the rogue to be absent at the appointed time, the clever woman,
with a hint cast through her laughing eyes, closed the play-lotus. // <s>Vjīv</s>C 3.219 //

children.text:
atra varṇanīyātmā sūkṣmo na punaralaṅkāraṇam, kasmāt---sākṣādabhidhayā vaktavyārthastathāvidhayā yuktyā pratipādyate /
leśasyodāharaṇaṃ yathā---
children.translated_text: Here, <s>sūkṣma</s> is of the nature of the thing to be described, not an ornament. Why? — The content to be expressed is conveyed through direct statement, by such a device. An example of <s>leśa</s> (the trace) —
'Let the guards recognize me as enamored of the princess by the horripilation [on my body] —'
'Known [only to me] — alas, the forest is [indeed] cold and windy!' // <s>Vjīv</s>C 3.220 //

children.text:
atrāpyetadeva vaktavyaṃ vastu kathaṃ vibhūṣaṇatāmarhati ? /
"yatparaḥ śabdaḥ sa śabdārthaḥ" iti nyāyāt /
hetorudāharaṇam---
children.translated_text: Here too, the same must be said: how can this content deserve the status of ornament? — By the maxim 'the word that follows [in syntactic connection] is the word-meaning.' An example of <s>hetu</s> (the reason) —
This breeze from the <s>Malaya</s> [mountain], swaying the shoots of fragrant sandal-trees,
generates delight in everyone. // <s>Vjīv</s>C 3.221 //
Thus, <s>upamārūpaka</s> (simile-metaphor) too is not an ornament.
The measuring-rod of the entire expanse of the sky, [and also] the foot of the Sun-bird [<s>Viṣṇu</s>] —
victorious is [that foot], a fresh mirror for the moon-faces of <s>Siddha</s>-women! // <s>Vjīv</s>C 3.222 //

children.text:
atra rasavadalaṅkāra (vat) vācyavācakayoḥ saṃgatireva nāsti /
tathā ca upamā ca rūpakaṃ ceti vigrahe dvandvo vā vivakṣitaḥ syāt, viśeṣaṇasamāso vā /
tatra dvandvapakṣe kvacidvākyaikadeśe rūpakaṃ kvacidupameti (dvitiya) praṇibandhanaṃ na kiñcidekasmin /
tatrāpi pratyekaṃ parispandatayā svasthāne samaṃ vibhātīti parasparāpekṣāṃ vinā samudāyātmakasya viśeṣyasyāsaṃbhavāt dvandvapakṣo 'nupapannaḥ /
viśeṣaṇasamāse 'pi sarvasmin vākye, ekadeśe vā dvitayamapīti dvayorekasmin vastuni yugapat parasparaviruddhayośchāyātapayoriva samāveśānupapattiḥ /
ekatarapakṣāvalambinyā vācā pratyekaṃ vācyavācakasvarūpaniścitāvaparasyāvakāśabhaṅgo 'pi na sambhavatīti parasparāpekṣāṃ vinā samudāyātmakaviśeṣaṇasamāso 'pyakicitkaraḥ /
kathañcittatraikataraniścaye pramāṇābhāvādanyatarakalpanena doṣāyogātsaṃkaravyavahāraḥ /
prastute punarevaṃvidhasvarūpaniṣpattāvapi saṃsiddhivivakṣayā yasyātmasiddhaāvapi sandehadolādhirūḍhistatrāpyasambhūtādvastuto 'vyavasthitaiva kadācidastīti yatkiñcideva vākyasāmarthyādavaseyaḥ /
pratīyamānaprakārāttṛtīyaṃ ramaṇīyamalaṅkaraṇakalāpamiti vākyavakratāsarvasvaṃ samākhyeyam /
samudāyātmakavākyavakratāsvarūpamāsūtrayati---
children.translated_text: Here, as with the <s>rasavadalaṅkāra</s>, there is simply no conjunction of the expressed and the expressor. And thus, in the analysis 'upamā ca rūpakaṃ ca' (simile and metaphor), either a <s>dvandva</s> (copulative) compound or a <s>viśeṣaṇasamāsa</s> (determinative) compound may be intended. In the <s>dvandva</s> case — sometimes <s>rūpaka</s> in one part of the sentence, sometimes <s>upamā</s> in [another] — there is no single basis for both. Moreover, since each shines equally through its own individual activity in its own place — without mutual dependence, the collective whole as a qualified entity is impossible — therefore the <s>dvandva</s> interpretation is untenable. Even in the determinative compound — whether both [figures apply] to the entire sentence or to one part — the impossibility of two [figures], mutually contradictory like shade and sunlight, simultaneously inhabiting one subject — and since speech, which supports only one interpretation, while determining the expressed-expressor nature of each individually, cannot also break the scope of the other — without mutual dependence, the collective-natured determinative compound too is fruitless. If somehow one interpretation is fixed, from the lack of evidence for the other and the fault of artificial attribution, the designation '<s>saṃkara</s>' (confusion of figures) applies. Regarding the present [discussion], however, even when such a nature is established, the claim of <s>saṃsiddhi</s> (mutual accomplishment) — even for one whose nature is self-established yet whose state ascends the swing of doubt — even there, what has not actually arisen is simply indeterminate and may sometimes exist — this much can only be inferred from the power of the sentence. The third, beautiful cluster of ornamental arts — those of the suggested type — should be declared as the very essence of sentence-obliqueness. [The author] now formulates the essential nature of sentence-obliqueness as an aggregate —
Radiant with qualities such as <s>lāvaṇya</s> (gracefulness), graced with coquetry by the placement of each step, captivating to the mind with few ornaments fashioned with charm,

children.text: atyarthaṃ rasavattayārdrahṛdayā (śaknotyudārābhidhā vāgvakrā sukavestathaiva ca) mano hartuṃ yathā nāyikā // Vjiv_3.64 //
children.translated_text: exceedingly tender-hearted through its quality of having <s>rasa</s>, noble in expression — oblique speech can steal the mind just like a heroine. // <s>Vjīv</s> 3.64 //

children.text:
lāvaṇyādītyādi /
āsāmevaṃvidhavākyasvarūpāyattāvagamanodāharaṇaṃ pravakṣyati /
tatsamudāyātmakasya (vākyasya) rasavattayā (manaḥ cetaḥ) hartuṃ ca saknoti yatā nāyikā tathā /
kīdṛśī---"lāvaṇyādiguṇojjvalā" (lāvaṇyādibhiḥ) lāvaṇyaprabhṛtibhiḥ "guṇaiḥ" prathamollekhalakṣaṇairguṇaiḥ "ujjvalā" bhrājiṣṇuḥ "pratipadanyāsaiḥ" "pratipadanyāsaḥ" pratisuptiṅantopanibandhānāni, taiḥ "vilāsāñcitā" śobhātiśayenābhyañcitā "vicchittyā" vaidagdhyabhaṅgyā kayācit "racitaiḥ" upanibaddhaiḥ "alpaiḥ" parimitaiḥ (vibhūṣaṇabharaiḥ) alaṅkaraṇairupamādibhiḥ, "manohāriṇī" hṛyaparañjikā vāk vicchittivihitaparimitālaṅkāraṇavinmayāsā śobhātiśayanidhānatāṃ pratipadyate /
kīdṛśī vāk---"udārābhidhā" audāryaguṇayuktābhihitā /
"atyarthaṃ rasavattayā" rāgādimattvena "ārdrahṛdayā" sarasābhiprāyā kāntāpi tathāvidhavilāsāñcitā bhavati /
nāyikāpakṣe lāvaṇyādayaḥ saundaryaprabhṛtayaḥ, padanyāsaḥ pādavikṣepaḥ, vilāsaḥ ceṣṭāviśeṣaḥ (vākpakṣe) vicchittiḥ vaidagdhyam, vāk vākyam, bhūṣaṇāni alaṅkārāḥ, kavyabhidhā vacanam /
prabandhasāmarthyamiti /
iti śrīrājānakakuntakaviricite vakroktijīvite kāvyālaṅkāre tṛtīya unmeṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Radiant with gracefulness' and so forth. [The author] will give examples illustrating how understanding depends on the nature of such sentences. Of the aggregate-natured sentence, through its quality of having <s>rasa</s>, it 'can steal the mind' — just as a heroine. Of what kind? — 'Radiant with qualities such as <s>lāvaṇya</s>' — by <s>lāvaṇya</s> and the rest, the qualities characterized as the first delineation, 'radiant' — resplendent. 'By the placement of each step' — by each nominal and verbal composition — 'graced with coquetry' — anointed with a superabundance of beauty. 'By charm' — by some turn of ingenuity. 'Fashioned' — composed. 'By few' — by a limited [number of] 'ornaments' — ornaments such as <s>upamā</s> (simile) and the rest. 'Captivating to the mind' — pleasing to the heart: speech endowed with limited ornaments fashioned through charm attains the status of being the repository of superabundant beauty. Of what kind is the speech? — 'Noble in expression' — endowed with the quality of nobility. 'Exceedingly tender-hearted through its quality of having <s>rasa</s>' — through possessing passion and the like — 'of tender intention' — the beloved too becomes thus graced with coquetry. In the heroine-interpretation: <s>lāvaṇya</s> and the rest are beauty and so forth; 'step-placement' is the movement of feet; 'coquetry' is a particular gesture; in the speech-interpretation: 'charm' is ingenuity; 'speech' is the sentence; 'ornaments' are <s>alaṅkāras</s>; 'expression' is utterance. This is the power of the composition. Thus ends the third <s>unmeṣa</s> (flash) of the <s>Vakroktijīvita</s>, the ornament of poetry, composed by the royal preceptor <s>Kuntaka</s>.

<s>Vakroktijīvita</s>, Fourth <s>Unmeṣa</s>. Having thus illuminated sentence-obliqueness, which is like the entire treasure of all literary art, [the author] now introduces section-obliqueness (<s>prakaraṇavakratā</s>), whose occasion has arrived —
Where the activity of the characters, adorned by the beauty of the unrestrained enthusiasm of their exertion,
bearing the delineation of their own intent, // <s>Vjīv</s> 4.1 //
— even in a desire whose arising is inconceivable from the root up —
a certain boundless [obliqueness] unfolds: that is section-and-work-obliqueness (<s>prabandhāṃśavakratā</s>). // <s>Vjīv</s> 4.2 //

children.text:
yatretyādi /
---"prabandhāṃśavakratā" (prakaraṇa) vakrabhāvo bhavatīti sambandhaḥ /
kīdṛśī---"niḥsīmā"---niravadhiḥ, "yatra"---yasyāṃ "vyavahartṝṇāṃ"---tattadvyāpāraparigrahavyagrāṇāṃ pravṛttiḥ "kāpi"---alaukikī "unmīlati"---udbhidyate /
kiṃviśiṣṭā---"niryantraṇotsāhaparispandopaśobhinī"---nirargalavyavasāyasphuritasphāravicchittiḥ, ata eva "svāśayollekhaśālinī" nirupamani (ja) hṛdayollāsitālaṅkṛtiḥ, kasmin sati---"apyāmūlādanāśaṅkyasamutthāne manorathe"---kandāt prabhṛtyasaṃbhāvyasamudbhede samīhite /
tadayamamatrārthaḥ---yatra manāṅmātramapyanunmīlitamanorathe kathāmadhye nirupadhimānadhanānāmadhyavasāyapaddhatiḥ nirantaravyavasāyātisphārā cetanacamatkāriṇī tadvihitavakratāvicchittiḥ prikaraṇasyālaṅkaraṇāyate, prabandhasya ca /
yathā abhijñānajānakīnāmni nāṭaketṛtīye 'ṅke setubandhe 'nākalitavidyābalānāmaviditavaidehīdayitadivyāstra prabhāvasaṃpadāṃ vānarapravīrāṇāṃ prathamameva makarākaramālokayatāṃ bandhādhyavasāyaḥ /
tathāhi---tatra nīlasya senāpatervacanam---
children.translated_text: 'Where' and so forth. 'Section-and-work-obliqueness' — the oblique character of the section — this is the syntactical connection. Of what kind? — 'Boundless' — unlimited. 'Where' — in which — 'of the characters' — of those who are occupied with the adoption of their respective activities, 'a certain' — extraordinary 'activity unfolds' — emerges. Of what kind? — 'Adorned by the beauty of the unrestrained enthusiasm of their exertion' — [having] a charm bursting with an unfettered determination and wide-open brilliance; and therefore 'bearing the delineation of their own intent' — [having] an ornamental beauty that radiates from the incomparable efflorescence of the heart. In what condition? — 'Even in a desire whose arising is inconceivable from the root up' — in a wish whose emergence, from the very beginning, is unimaginable. This then is the purport: where, in the midst of a narrative in which a desire has not opened even slightly, the course of determination of those who possess wealth of unfeigned pride — continuously overflowing with the exuberance of resolve, producing wonder in consciousness — the charm of obliqueness fashioned by that [resolve] serves as the ornament of the section, and of the work. For example, in the drama called <s>Abhijñāna-Jānakī</s>, in the third act, during the building of the bridge [to Laṅkā] — the determination to build [the bridge] of the monkey-heroes, who had not assessed the power of supernatural weapons, who were unaware of the divine missile-powers of <s>Vaidehī</s>'s (<s>Sītā</s>'s) beloved — upon first seeing the ocean with its crocodiles. And thus, the words of the general <s>Nīla</s> there —

children.text: śailāḥ santi sahastraśaḥ pratidiśaṃ valmīkakalpā ime dordaṇḍāśca kaṭhoravikramarasakrīḍhāsamutkaṇṭhitāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Boulders exist in thousands, in every direction, these anthills — and [our] staff-like arms, eager for the play of fierce valor's savour —'

children.text: karṇāsvāditakumbhasaṃbhavakathāḥ kiṃ nāma kallolinī- kānte goṣpadapūraṇe 'pi kapayaḥ kautūhalaṃ nāsti vaḥ // VjivC_4.1 //
children.translated_text: "You monkeys, who have heard the story of <s>Kumbhasaṃbhava</s> (Agastya, born from a pot) — is there truly no curiosity among you even about filling a puddle in the bed of a lovely river?" // VjivC_4.1 //
The reply of the monkeys, spoken offstage after commotion —

children.text: āndolyante kati na girayaḥ kandukānandamudrāṃ vyātanvānāḥ kapiparisare kautukotkarṣatarṣāt /
children.translated_text: "How many mountains are not tossed about, displaying the joyful gesture of ball-play, in the company of monkeys, out of eagerness for the height of sport!

children.text: lopāmudrāparivṛḍhakathābhijñatāpyasti kiṃ tu vrīḍāveśaḥ pavanatanayocchiṣṭasaṃsparśanena // VjivC_4.2 //
children.translated_text: There is also familiarity with the story elaborated by <s>Lopāmudrā</s>, but there is bashfulness due to contact with what was left over by <s>Pavanatanaya</s> (the son of the Wind, i.e. <s>Hanumān</s>)." // VjivC_4.2 //

children.text:
atraiva pavanatanayocchiṣṭe adhivācini paryāyavakratāprikāraḥ smartavyaḥ /
ārya, duṣkaro 'yamebhirmakarākarabandhādhyavasāya iti rāmeṇa paryanuyuktasya jāmbavato 'pi vākyam---
children.translated_text:
Here itself, regarding the word '<s>pavanatanayocchiṣṭa</s>' (left over by the son of the Wind) used in a transferred sense, the type of <s>paryāyavakratā</s> (obliqueness of synonyms) should be recalled.
The speech of <s>Jāmbavān</s>, when questioned by <s>Rāma</s> saying "Noble one, the resolve of these ones to bind the ocean is difficult" —
"Even on paths of desire that have sprouted without limit,
the skilled undertake the exertion of duty and are victorious." // VjivC_4.3 //

children.text:
evaṃvidhamaparamapi tata eva vibhāvanīyamabhinavādbhutābhogabhaṅgīsubhagaṃ subhāṣitasarvasvam /
yathā vā raghuvaṃśe pañcame sarge caturu (da) dhikāñcīkalāpālaṅkaraṇakāśyapīparivṛḍhasya viśvajidākhyamakhadīkṣādakṣiṇīkṛtasamastasaṃpadaḥ sahajaudāryarahasyodāharaṇasya raghorarghasaṃpāditamṛṇmayapātrasamālokanasamunmūlitamanorathāḍambare varatantorantevāsini niṣiddhagamane munau
children.translated_text:
Other such brilliant sayings (<s>subhāṣita</s>), beautiful with the grace of novel and wondrous amplitude, are also to be appreciated from the same source.
As for example, in the fifth canto of the <s>Raghuvaṃśa</s>, when the sage — the pupil of <s>Kāśyapa</s>, adorned with a girdle of four (teen) strands, who had been nurtured [in learning], whose student <s>Varatantu</s> had been forbidden to depart — [addressed] <s>Raghu</s>, who had given away all his wealth as <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (sacrificial fees) at the consecration of the sacrifice called <s>Viśvajit</s>, and who was an illustration of the secret of innate generosity, and whose extravagance of desire had been uprooted by the sight of the earthen vessels acquired in exchange for his wealth,

children.text: "kiṃ vastu vidvan gurave pradeyaṃ tvayā kiyadveti" // VjivC_4.4 //
children.translated_text: "'What thing, O learned one, is to be given to the teacher, and how much?' —" // VjivC_4.4 //
Immediately after this question, having calculated the teacher's fee of fourteen <s>koṭi</s> (crores) of gold that had been specified,

children.text: dvitrāṇyahānyarhasi soḍhumarhan yāvadyate sādhayituṃ tvadartham // VjivC_4.5 //
children.translated_text: "'You who are worthy, please endure for two or three days, while what is needed is procured for your sake.'" // VjivC_4.5 //

children.text:
iti nirargalagambhīrato dāragarimāgopāyitāntargatayā giragnyagāramalaṅkurvati kuberaṃ prati sāmantasaṃbhāvanayā jayādhyavasāyaḥ kāmapi sahṛdayahṛdayāhlādakāritāṃ pratipadyate /
sūktisudhāvīcayo 'pyatra tata (evā) svādanīyāḥ /
etatprakaraṇaprāṇaparispandasundaraṃ ca kiñcidudāhriyate /
yathā---
children.translated_text:
