Thus, with unobstructed depth, his speech, whose inner intention was concealed by the gravity of the undertaking, adorns his household, and his resolve of victory — through the respectful treatment of <s>Kubera</s> as a feudatory lord — attains an indescribable capacity to delight the hearts of <s>sahṛdayas</s> (sensitive readers).
The waves of nectar-like <s>sūktis</s> (felicitous expressions) here too are to be savored from the same [source].
And something that is beautiful with the vital pulsation (<s>prāṇaparispanda</s>) of this <s>prakaraṇa</s> (episode) is cited as example.
As follows —
"That resplendent heap of gold obtained from <s>Kubera</s>, who was about to be attacked,

children.text: dideśa kautsāya samastameva pādaṃ sumeroriva vajrabhinnam // VjivC_4.6 //
children.translated_text: the king bestowed upon <s>Kautsa</s> in its entirety, like a portion of <s>Sumeru</s> split by the thunderbolt." // VjivC_4.6 //

children.text:
atra dambholidalitakāñcanācalapādasādṛśyapratīyamānāparimitasya tapanīyakūṭasya sarvasyāpi (viśrā)ṇanāt, anya eva tādṛśadraviṇavyasanavartino dilīpanandanasya, kalpanākalaṅkakadarthitārthavitaraṇānuccatarān kalpatarūpanapi tiraskurvāṇaḥ sa koṣyaudāryasīmāviśeṣaḥ samujjṛmbhate, yena garbhokṛtagarvagarimagranthīśithilādvitīyayaśassandohadohadasya dātrantarāsahiṣṇoḥ "gurvartham" ityādeḥ prathamoditavākyaprakāṇḍasya prāṇaparispandaparipoṣaṇamevādhīyate /
anyacca---
children.translated_text:
Here, because all of the immense mass of gold — whose limitlessness is perceived through the simile of the golden mountain-peak shattered by the thunderbolt — is given away entirely, a certain extraordinary limit of munificence belonging to the son of <s>Dilīpa</s>, who was devoted to such lavish spending, manifests itself, surpassing even the wish-fulfilling trees (<s>kalpataru</s>) which are diminished by the blemish of being merely imaginary in their gift-giving; and through this, what is achieved is nothing but the nourishment of the vital pulsation (<s>prāṇaparispanda</s>) of the grand statement beginning with "for the teacher's sake," which was uttered first — [the statement] of one whose unrivaled glory-yielding desire had its knots of swelling pride loosened from within.
And another [verse] —
"Those two, dwelling in <s>Sāketa</s> (Ayodhyā), were both of praiseworthy character among the people:
the king, more desireless than what was to be given to the teacher in value, and also more generous than [what] the supplicant desired." // VjivC_4.7 //

children.text:
ityādi /
atrāpi gurupradeyadakṣiṇātiriktaṃ kārtasvaramapratigṛhṇataḥ kautsasya, raghorapi prāthitāt śataguṇaṃ sahastraguṇaṃ vā prayacchataḥ (parasparaṃ kalahāyamānayo) rniravadhi(ni) spṛhatvaudāryasaṃpat sāketanivāsinām aśrutapūrvāṃ kāmapi mahotsavamudrāmātatāna /
evameṣā mahākaviprabandheṣu prakaraṇavakratāvicchittiḥ rasaniṣyandinī sahṛdayaiḥ svayamutprekṣaṇīyā /
imāmeva prakārāntareṇa prakāśayati---
children.translated_text:
And so forth.
Here too, the wealth of desirelessness and generosity — of <s>Kautsa</s> who would not accept the gold exceeding the teacher's fee, and of <s>Raghu</s> who gave a hundredfold or thousandfold more than what was requested — the two vying with each other endlessly, spread among the inhabitants of <s>Sāketa</s> a certain unprecedented festival of celebration.
Thus this appreciation of <s>prakaraṇavakratā</s> (obliqueness of episodes) in the compositions of great poets (<s>mahākavi</s>), overflowing with <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic emotion), is to be imagined by the <s>sahṛdayas</s> (sensitive readers) on their own.
He reveals this same [concept] through another mode —
"Even on the path of narrative variety that is based on inherited plot (<s>itivṛtta</s>),
a different <s>vakratā</s> (obliqueness) shines forth, through the charm of what is newly created." // Vjiv_4.3 //
"In such a way that the <s>prakaraṇa</s> (episode), which is the very life of the entire composition (<s>prabandha</s>),
shines, brimming with <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic emotion) that has reached its highest pitch." // Vjiv_4.4 //

children.text:
itivṛtteti /
---"tathā utpādyalavalāvaṇyādanyā bhavati vakratā" = tena prakāreṇa kṛtrisaṃvidhānakāmanīyakādalaukikī vakrabhāvabhaṅgī samujjṛmbhate sahṛdayānāvarjayatīti yāvat /
(kasmin--) "kathāvaicitryavartmani"---kāvyasya kathāvicitrabhāvamārge /
kiṃviśiṣṭe "itivṛttaprayukte 'pi"---itihāsaparigrahe 'pi /
tatheti tathāprayogamapekṣata ata āha---"yathā prabandhasya sakalasyāpi jīvitam /
bhāti prakaraṇaṃ" yena prakāreṇa sargabandhādeḥ samagrasyāpi prāṇapradaṃ bhāsate 'ṅgam /
kīdṛgbhūtaṃ---"kāṣṭhādhirūḍharasanirbhara (m) = prathamadhārodbhāsitaśṛṅgārādiparipūrṇam /
tadayamatra paramārthaḥ = vikhyātavicitrarucirakathākaraṇḍakāyamā(ne)mahābhāratādau rasasamudramudritāyāmapi kathāyāṃ kasyaciduttarādharavicchittikāraṇavikalpakābhāvāt, savi(śeṣa)rasabhāvajanakāścaryajananakāryajātāni atibandhuranijapratibhāsamunmīlitasamucitanirupamānanimittāni nibandhanīyānīti /
tadatiśayavakratāprakāreṇa prakaraṇena vyavaharan kaviḥ sakalakavirasikapariṣatparitoṣaṇamāvahati /
prabandhe 'pi pravaranavasaṃskārakāraṇaramaṇīyakāntiparipoṣaḥ rekhārājamānapurātanatruṭitacitradaśāspadasaubhāgyamanubhavati /
abhijñānaśākuntale nāṭake itarataruṇītiraskārakāraṇāvirodhakatvenekṣaṇakṣaṇākalitalalitalāvaṇyalakṣmīlalāmanirupamarūparekhā sukhapratyabhijñā samujjṛmbhate /
vistrambhasaṃbhāvanāsanāthakathārahasyaramyaparasparānurūpapremaprakarṣapravartitacirataravicitraviharaṇavyāpārasuprāptapratyabhijñāṃ tāṃśakuntalāṃ prati duṣyantasya vismaraṇakāraṇamitivṛttāgaditamapi alpamātrāparādhapravartamānakrūrakrudhaḥ karuṇāparāṅmukhasyamunerduvāsasaḥ śāpamutpāditavān kaviḥ /
tatra hi prakaraṇaprakāṇḍe śakuntalā kila prathamapriyapravāsavāsaravitīrṇavirahaduḥsahaduḥkhāveśavivaśāntaḥkaraṇavṛttiruṭaja(saṃnihitā) paryākulena prāṅgaṇaprānte sthite (na) maharṣiṇā manyusaṅgāt---
children.translated_text:
Regarding '<s>itivṛtta</s>' (inherited narrative) —
"Thus, through the charm of what is newly created, a different <s>vakratā</s> (obliqueness) comes into being" — that is to say, by that method, an extraordinary manner of oblique expression, beautiful through the artful arrangement of artificially devised elements, blossoms forth and captivates the <s>sahṛdayas</s> (sensitive readers).
(In what context?) — "on the path of narrative variety" — on the path where the story of a <s>kāvya</s> (literary work) becomes varied.
Of what kind? — "even when based on inherited plot (<s>itivṛtta</s>)" — even when drawing upon traditional history (<s>itihāsa</s>).
The word 'thus' (<s>tathā</s>) requires a correlative, hence he says: "In such a way that the <s>prakaraṇa</s> (episode), which is the very life of the entire composition (<s>prabandha</s>), shines" — that is, the component that bestows life upon the whole, including <s>sargabandha</s> (canto-composition) and so forth, becomes radiant.
Of what nature? — "brimming with <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic emotion) that has reached its highest pitch" — filled to the brim with <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (the erotic sentiment) and other <s>rasas</s> that are illuminated at their highest level.
The ultimate meaning here is this: even when the story is stamped with an ocean of <s>rasa</s> in a great work like the <s>Mahābhārata</s>, which measures out a casket of famous, varied, and beautiful narratives, since there is no one to devise the particular distinctions of higher and lower [elements], things that generate wonder and produce extraordinary effects — born of <s>rasa</s> endowed with special qualities — must be composed through unique and incomparable means awakened by the poet's own supremely graceful genius.
The poet who operates through the <s>prakaraṇa</s> (episode) by means of such surpassing <s>vakratā</s> (obliqueness) brings about the satisfaction of the entire assembly of connoisseurs among poets.
Even within the <s>prabandha</s> (composition), the nourishment of beauty through excellent and novel refinement experiences the good fortune of an ancient painted canvas whose faded condition is being restored along its outlines.
In the play <s>Abhijñānaśākuntala</s>, an incomparable outline of beauty — the lovely crest-jewel of charm perceived in a single glance as not contradicting the cause of surpassing other young women — shines forth, easily recognizable.
Regarding that <s>Śakuntalā</s>, who had attained recognition through the well-achieved activities of long and varied dalliance prompted by the excellence of mutual love befitting each other, delightful with the secret narrative sanctioned by trustful intimacy — the poet devised the curse of the sage <s>Durvāsas</s>, who was cruel due to a trifling offense and averse to compassion, as the cause of <s>Duṣyanta</s>'s forgetting, even though the inherited narrative (<s>itivṛtta</s>) had told it [differently].
For in that grand episode (<s>prakaraṇa</s>), <s>Śakuntalā</s>, whose mental state was overcome by the unbearable grief of separation endured during the first days of her beloved's absence, was stationed in the hermitage; and by the great sage, who stood at the edge of the courtyard, agitated with anger —

children.text: vicintayantī yamananyamānasā taponidhiṃ vetsi na māmupasthitam /
children.translated_text: "You who are thinking of him alone, with mind fixed on no other — you do not notice me, a treasury of <s>tapas</s> (austerity), who have arrived.

children.text: smariṣyati tvāṃ sa na bodhito 'pi san kathāṃ pramattaḥ prathamaṃ kṛtāmiva // VjivC_4.8 //
children.translated_text: He shall not remember you even when reminded, like a drunkard [who forgets] a tale told earlier." // VjivC_4.8 //

children.text:
itthaṃ śaptā /
tacchravaṇaparyākulābhyāṃ sakhībhyāṃ (anunītaḥ) pravāsyamāno 'pi munipravaraḥ priyatamanyāsāṅgulīyakavilokanaṃ (śāpā) vasānā (vadhi) makārṣot /
priyaṃ prati yāntyāśca muniduhituralaṅkṛtāṅgulīkisalayasyāṅgalīyakasya kutracit kuṭilatarataraṅgiṇīpayovatārādantarjalamalakṣitaṃ paribhraṣṭasya sasaṃbhramamadabhramarīcimaṇḍalamāṇikyasamullasitasarasāmiṣaviśaṅkākulaśakalīkavalitasya kālāntare tadantakāriṇā kaivartanena punarapi (samarpaṇam) /
evaṃvidhasya saṃvidhānakasya rasanidhānakalaśāyamānasya māhātmyādikhilasyāpi nāṭakasya kāpi (vicchittiḥ) samaye cañcarīkopālambhagarbhagītyavagamanāt muniśāpāpasāritapreyasīsmṛterapi tadadhivāsavāsanāpi ca parisphurantī pauravasya pāravaśyaṃ niścayāmāsa /
tathā ca
children.translated_text:
Thus was she cursed.
The best of sages, though propitiated by her two companions who were distressed at hearing that [curse], and though about to depart, made the beholding of the beloved's ring upon her finger the terminus of the curse's effect.
And as the sage's daughter was departing toward her beloved, the ring upon her finger — that sprout-like adorned digit — fell off unnoticed somewhere into the water at the descent of a sinuous river's current; it was swallowed by a fish confused by the suspicion that the sapphire, glittering with an abundant circle of rays, was a juicy morsel of food; and in due course of time, it was restored again by a fisherman who was the slayer of that [fish].
Of such a narrative arrangement (<s>saṃvidhānaka</s>), which serves as a treasure-vessel of <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic emotion) — an indescribable aesthetic charm pervades the entire play from its beginning to end; at the right moment, from understanding the song containing the reproach of the bee (<s>cañcarīka</s>), the memory of the beloved who had been displaced by the sage's curse, and also the lingering fragrance of its impression — all this determined the helpless state of the descendant of <s>Puru</s> (<s>Duṣyanta</s>).
And thus —

children.text: ramyāṇi vīkṣya madhurāṃśca niśamya śabdān paryutsukībhavati yatsukhito 'pi jantuḥ /
children.translated_text: "When a creature, though happy, becomes deeply agitated upon seeing beautiful things and hearing sweet sounds,

children.text: taccetasā smarati nūnamabodhapūrvaṃ bhāvasthirāṇi jananāntarasauhṛdāni // VjivC_4.9 //
children.translated_text: surely his heart remembers, without conscious awareness, the enduring affections of former births." // VjivC_4.9 //

children.text:
atra saṃmugdhasubhagamenakānandinīsmaraṇalekhālāvaṇyamanyadeva camatkārakāraṇaṃ sahṛdayānāṃ samudyotate /
aparaṃ ca parāvartitāyāmapi vyalīkamabhijñakaṃ ca, maharṣiśiṣyasamākhyātakaragrahaṇagarbhādhānāyāṃ mahāmanyusamunmeṣaḥ /
manāgullaṅghitasahajalajjāvatāratāpasaśīghrāpanītāvaguṇṭhanena (parāṅganāracita)tathāvidhasakalalalanālāvaṇyāvalepasaṃpadi saṃpāditavipañciṭaṅkāravalguvāgvilāsavyāhṛtavanaviharaṇarahasyābhi jñāyāṃ bharatamātari tathārūpaṃ pratyākhyānapāruṣyamapi rājñaḥ śāpasya saṃpatsyamānānutāpaṃ parasparaṃ prakāśībhavadanargalānurāgapragbhārasaṅgādatīva sahṛdayāhlādakāri /
śāpāvasānasamutpattaye prasiddhasyaraṇasamullāsiduḥsahavirahajvarapātāvegavikalatvaṃ ca samanantaramevāṅgulīyasaṅgamādatīva sahṛdayānāhlādayati /
narapatestatra kañcukino vacanam---
children.translated_text:
Here, the charm of the sketch-like remembrance of the charmingly beautiful <s>Menakā</s>'s daughter shines forth as an altogether different cause of <s>camatkāra</s> (aesthetic wonder) for the <s>sahṛdayas</s> (sensitive readers).
And furthermore, even when she was brought back, the false denial of recognition, and then the great eruption of wrath when the marriage and conception were narrated by the great sage's disciple —
when, with the veil quickly removed by the ascetic woman whose natural modesty was slightly transgressed, in the presence of the full splendor of all feminine beauty that [appeared to be] fashioned by another woman, and when the secret of the forest dalliance was recognized through the charming speech-play that produced the sound of the <s>vīṇā</s> (lute) — even such harsh rejection by the king toward the mother of <s>Bharata</s> is supremely delightful to the <s>sahṛdayas</s> (sensitive readers), because the impending remorse of the curse and the flood of unbridled mutual love becoming manifest to each other [create aesthetic pleasure].
And the state of being overcome by the unbearable fever of separation, blazing in the well-known forest, for the purpose of the eventual conclusion of the curse, delights the <s>sahṛdayas</s> greatly, immediately upon the reunion through the ring.
The speech of the chamberlain (<s>kañcukin</s>) to the king at that point —
"Having rejected the prescribed rites of special adornment, wearing only a single golden bracelet placed on his left forearm, his lip discolored by sighing,

his eyes wearied by sleepless nights of anxious brooding — though diminished like a great gem whose luster has been effaced by a scratch, he is not unnoticed due to his innate radiance." // VjivC_4.10 //

children.text: ramyaṃ dveṣṭi yathā purā prakṛtibhirna pratyahaṃ sevyate śayyāprāntavivartanairvigamayatyunnidra eva kṣapāḥ /
children.translated_text: "He avoids pleasant things as before; he is not attended daily by his retinue; he spends his nights, though wide awake, turning from side to side upon the edge of his bed;

children.text: dākṣiṇyena dadāti vācamucitāmantaḥ purebhyo yadā gotreṣu skhalitastadā bhavati ca vrīḍāvilakṣaściram // VjivC_4.11 //
children.translated_text: when out of courtesy he gives appropriate speech to the ladies of the inner apartments, he stumbles over their names and remains ashamed and abashed for a long time." // VjivC_4.11 //

children.text:
atra rājño viśeṣaṇavakratā, gotreṣviti vacanavakratvaṃ ca kimapi cittacamatkārakāri /
rājño 'pi svayaṃlikhitālekhyālokamānavilocanasya smaraṇātmaka dayitātmamudrāmudritaṃ sahṛdayavacanam /
children.translated_text:
Here, the <s>vakratā</s> (obliqueness) in the characterization of the king, and the <s>vacanavakratva</s> (obliqueness of expression) in the phrase 'over their names' (<s>gotreṣu</s>), produce an indescribable <s>camatkāra</s> (aesthetic wonder) in the mind.
The speech of the <s>sahṛdaya</s> (sensitive reader), stamped with the seal of the beloved's own image, as the king gazes at a portrait drawn by his own hand, immersed in remembrance —
"O bee, if you touch the <s>bimba</s>-fruit lip of my beloved — lovely as the tender shoot of an untroubled young tree — which I drank with tenderness during the festivals of love,

children.text: bimbādharaṃ spṛśasi cet bhramara priyāyāḥ tvāṃ kārayāmi kamalodarabandhanastham // VjivC_4.12 //
children.translated_text: I shall confine you within the hollow of a lotus." // VjivC_4.12 //

children.text:
ityudita evāsvādanīyaḥ /
avidyamāne punaretasmin tatpādyalavalāvaṇyallāmni prakaraṇe niṣkāraṇavismaraṇavairasyamitihāsāṃsyeva rūpakasyāpi virūpakatāpattinimittatāmavagāhate /
utpādyalavalāvaṇyāditi dvidhā vyākhyeyam = yathā kvacidasadevotpādyam, kvacidaucityatyaktaṃ sadapyanyathāsaṃpādyam sahṛdayahṛdayāhlādanāya /
yathādāttarāghave mārīcavadhaḥ /
tacca prāgeva vyākhyātam /
evamanyadapyasyā vakratāvicchitterudāharaṇaṃ mahākaviprabandheṣu svayamutprekṣaṇīyam /
children.translated_text:
This is to be savored just as it has been stated.
Moreover, in the absence of this <s>prakaraṇa</s> (episode), which is the crest-jewel of the charm of what is newly created, the unpleasantness of a causeless forgetting would cause the dramatic work (<s>rūpaka</s>) too, just like the bare inherited narrative (<s>itihāsa</s>), to fall into disfigurement.
The phrase 'through the charm of what is newly created' (<s>utpādyalavalāvaṇyāt</s>) is to be explained in two ways: in some cases what is to be created is entirely new, and in other cases, even what exists [in the source] is to be reconstituted differently, for the delight of the <s>sahṛdayas</s>' (sensitive readers') hearts.
As for example, the killing of <s>Mārīca</s> in the <s>Uttararāghava</s>.
That has been explained previously.
Thus other examples of this type of <s>vakratāvicchitti</s> (appreciation of obliqueness) in the compositions of great poets are also to be imagined by oneself.
"The words of poets live on, dense with compositions pregnant with uninterrupted outpourings of <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic emotion),

children.text: giraḥ kavīnāṃ jīvanti na kathāmātramāśritāḥ // VjivC_4.13 //
children.translated_text: not those that depend merely on the bare narrative." // VjivC_4.13 //

(This is an intervening verse.)
He brings to light yet another mode of <s>prakaraṇavakratā</s> (obliqueness of episodes) —
"The vital pulsation of the mutual relationship of helper and helped among the individual parts of a composition (<s>prabandha</s>),
which is connected with the binding of the fruit [of the narrative], shining forth —" // Vjiv_4.5 //
Manifesting through the creative intuition that shines with extraordinary depiction,
[the composition] gives birth to the secret of a new obliquity of some poet. // Vjiv_4.6 //

children.text:
"sūte"---samunmīlayati /
(kiṃ) "nūtanakratvarahasyaṃ"---abhinavavakrabhāvopaniṣadaṃ /
"kasyācit"---(na) sarvasya /
"kaveḥ"---kavayituḥ, prastutau (citya) cāruracanāvicakṣaṇasyeti yāvat /
kaḥ "upakāryopakartṛtvaparispandaḥ"---anugrāhyanugrahakatvamahimā /
kiṃ kurvan "parisphuran"---samunmīlayan /
kiṃviśiṣṭaḥ---"phalabandhānubandhavān" = pradhānakāryānusandhānavān kāryānusandhānanipuṇa(iti bhāvaḥ) /
kathamevaṃvidhasya hatyāha---"asāmānyasamullekhapratibhāpratibhāsinaḥ"---nirupamonmīlitaśakti vibhavabhrājiṣṇoḥ /
keṣāṃ "prabandhasyaikadeśānāṃ" = prakaraṇānām /
tadidamuktaṃ bhavati---prātisvikasaṃniveśaśobhināmapi prabandhāvayavānāṃ pradhānaphalasaṃbandhanibandhānugrāhyānugrāhakabhāvaḥ svabhāvasubhagapratibhāprakāśyamānaḥ kasyacidvicakṣaṇasya vakratācamatkāriṇaḥ kaveralaukikaṃ (kathāprāṇaprauḍhiprarūḍha) vakratollekhalāvaṇyaṃ samullāsayati /
yathā puṣpadūṣitake dvitīye 'ṅke--- prasthānāt pratinivṛtya nibiḍānurāgāt (andhakārāvṛtāyāṃ) vibhāvaryāmamandamadanonmādamudreṇa samudradattena nijabhāryāniketanaṃ tulyadivasaṃ nandayantīsaṃgamāya malīmluceneva praviśatā prakampāvegavikalālasakāyanipātananihatanidrasya dvāradeśaśāyinaḥ kalahāyamānasya kuvalayasyotkocakāraṇaṃ svakarādaṅgulīyakadānaṃ yat kṛtaṃ, taccaturthe 'ṅke mathurāpratinivṛttena tenaiva śvaśurasya samāveditasamudradattavṛttāntena kulakalaṅkātaṅkakadarthyamānasya sārthavāhasāgaradattasya svatanayasparśa (samāhita) māna (sasya) snuṣāśīlaśuddhimunmīlayattadupakārāya kalpate /
tathā ca sāgaradattasya vacanam
children.translated_text: 'Gives birth' — makes manifest. What? — 'The secret of new obliquity' — the esoteric teaching (<s>upaniṣad</s>) of unprecedented oblique character. 'Of some' —...
'This signet ring, bearing the mark of her name, makes clear the purity of her conduct;

children.text: mamāpi sāmānyasamudyato 'nu- tāpastu pāpasya bhavetsa śuddhiḥ // VjivC_4.14 //
children.translated_text: may the remorse that has arisen in me for sin of an ordinary kind also become that purification.' // VjivC_4.14 //

children.text: atra bhṛtya, kimiti tvayā prathamamasmākaṃ (noktamiti pṛṣṭasya) kuvalayasyottaraṃ---
children.translated_text: Here, 'O servant, why did you not tell us first?' — this is the response of <s>Kuvalaya</s> to the question:

children.text: tadopaṇikamante rāma paṇi yāta ta hiṃ evva pavisaṃti /
children.translated_text: [Prakrit:] 'Then, near the fan, O <s>Rāma</s>, your hand went precisely there, entering...

children.text: dgdhācchāditaṃ ca mae sa aṃ evva pekhkhiaṃ chanvāhanasaṃpadaṃ putana vedaissadi // VjivC_4.15 //
children.translated_text: and covered by the burnt [offering], I myself observed the fortune of the <s>chanvāhana</s> and the son — the knowledge [thereof].' // VjivC_4.15 //

children.text:
tata evāvadhāryam /
yathottararāmacarite--- pṛthugarbhabharakheditadehāyā videharājaduhiturvinodāya dāśarathinā cirantanarājacaritacitraruciṃ darśayatā nirvyājavijayavijṛmbhamāṇajṛmbhakāstrāṇyuddiśya "sarvathedānīṃ tvatprasūtimupasthāsyanti" iti yadabhihitaṃ tatpañcamāṅke pravīracaryācatureṇa candraketunā kṣaṇaṃ samarakelimākāṅkṣatā tadantarāyakalitakalakalāḍambarāṇāṃ varūthinīnāṃ sahajajayotkaṇṭhābhrājiṣṇorjānakīnandanasya jṛmbhakāstravyāpāreṇa kamapyupakāramutpādayati /
tathā ca tatra lavaḥ--- "bhavatu, kālaharaṇapratiṣedhāya jṛmbhakāstreṇa tāvat sainyāni saṃstambhayāmi" sumantraḥ---tatkimakasmādullolāḥ sainyayodhāḥ praśāmyanti /
lavaḥ---paśyāmyenamadhunā pragalbham /
sumantraḥ---(sasaṃbhramam) vatsa, sumāreṇānena jṛmbhakāstramabhimantritam /
candraketuḥ---ārya, kaḥ sandehaḥ---
children.translated_text: From that very [example] it should be understood. As in the <s>Uttararāmacarita</s> — for the amusement of the daughter of the <s>Videha</s> king, whose body was weary from the heavy burden of pregnancy...

children.text: vyatikara iva bhīmo vaidyutastāmasaśca praṇihitamapi cakṣurgrastamuktaṃ hinasti /
children.translated_text: Like a terrible convergence of lightning and darkness, even the gaze that has been directed is swallowed up and released [in futility];

children.text: abilikhitamivaitat sainyamaspandamāste niyatamajitavīryaṃ jṛmbhate jṛmbhakāstram // VjivC_4.16 //
children.translated_text: the army stands motionless as if painted — surely the <s>jṛmbhaka</s>-weapon (the yawning weapon) of unconquered power is displaying its power. // VjivC_4.16 //
A wonder!
With dark yawning[-weapon effects] that pile masses of darkness from the caverns of the netherworld, blazing with smelted brilliant fiery copper-crested lights flashing and sparkling,

by the harsh, terrible windstorms born of the force of destruction at the end of the <s>kalpa</s>, it is spread out, as if by the peaks of the <s>Vindhya</s> mountains — with hollows of blue clouds and lightning. // VjivC_4.17 //

children.text:
ityādi /
eka evāyamekadeśānāmiti bahuvacanam /
atra dvayorapi bahūnāmupakāryopakārakatvaṃ svayamutprekṣaṇīyam /
children.translated_text: and so forth. This is one and the same [weapon] for [all] the individual parts — hence the plural. Here, the mutual assistance [of the elements], whether two or many, should be imagined by oneself...
Adorned by another type [of obliquity] obtained in a single section,
the composition appears beautiful, as if a new vibration has arisen. // VjivC_4.18 //
(This is an interpolated verse.) He reveals another type of this very [obliquity]:
In each section, fashioned through the engagement of mature creative intuition,

children.text: eka evābhidheyātmā badhyamānaḥ punaḥ punaḥ // Vjiv_4.7 //
children.translated_text: one and the same expressible content, being bound again and again, // Vjiv_4.7 //
complete with fresh unprecedented depiction, radiant with <s>rasa</s> and ornamental beauty,
produces a turn of obliquity-emergence that generates wonder. // Vjiv_4.8 //

children.text:
"badhnāti"---niyantrayati nibandhayatīti yāvat /
kāṃ---"vakratodbhedabhaṅgīm"---gambhīravakrabhāvāvirbhāvitāṃ śobhām /
kiṃviśiṣṭāṃ---"udbhāvitādbhutām" = kandalitakutūhalām /
kaḥ "eka evābhidheyātmā"---tadeva vastusvarūpam /
kiṃ kriyamāṇaḥ---"badhyamānaḥ"---prastutaucityacāruracanāmātraspandamānaḥ /
kathaṃ "punaḥ punaḥ"---vāraṃ vāraṃ /
kva---"pratiprakāraṇam" = prakaraṇe prakaraṇe, sthāne sthāne iti yāvat /
nanvevaṃ punaruktatāpātratāṃ samāsādayatītyāha---"anyūnanūtanollekharasālaṅkaraṇojjvalaḥ"---avikalābhinavollāsaśṛṅgārarūpakādiparispandabhrājiṣṇuḥ /
kīdṛśaḥ---"prauḍhapratibhābhogayojitaḥ" pragalbhataraprajñāprakāraprakāśitaḥ /
ayamasya paramārthaḥ---tadevaṃ sakalacandrodayā (di) prakaraṇaprakāreṣu vastu prastutakathāsaṃvidhānakānurodhāt muhurmuhurupanibadhyamānaṃ yadi paripūrṇapūrvavirūparasālaṅkārarāmaṇīyakanirbharaṃ bhavati tadā kāmapi rāmaṇīyakamaryādāṃ vakratāmavatārayati /
yathā harṣacarite--abhinavabhaṅgīparigrahagrathitasaubhāgyopasaṃpat (dharā) dhara-vibhāvarīvirām(di) rāmaṇīyakakartro naikasthāneṣu camatkurute /
tata eva ca tadāsvādanīyam /
bahutvādatra varṇayitumaśakyam /
rājā---(sakaruṇaṃ puro 'valokya) hā devi pādapairapyapagatāsi
children.translated_text: 'Produces' — restrains, binds — this is the meaning. What? — 'A turn of obliquity-emergence' — the turn that is the emergence of profound oblique character...
The <s>kuravaka</s> tree — a tight embrace; the <s>bakula</s> tree — the caress of the face; the red <s>aśoka</s> — likewise, the stamp of the foot.

children.text: tava sukṛtinaḥ saṃbhāvyaite prasādamahotsavān anugatadaśāḥ sarve, sarvaśśaṭho na yathā vayam // VjivC_4.19 //
children.translated_text: All these, fortunate ones, are deemed worthy of your favor-festivals, following the course [of their dohadas] — but not we, who are cheated in every way! // VjivC_4.19 //

children.text:
yathā anyatra hi--- pradīptāntaḥ pureṇa kṛśānunā kavalitān vilāsaśākhinaḥ paśyannabhinavaśokāveśavivaśāntaḥ karaṇa; "sākṣāddevīmanusarantaste" iti samutpannamatinirvikalpamavayavaikaikaprasādapātrebhyo 'pi avidvadbhyo 'pi samanuṣṭhitasamucitasāhasebhyaḥ samucitatādṛśaprasādasādhanamabhyastatadāsvādānubhavasarvasvamapyātmānaṃ tatsamaya eva priyānugamanamanācarantamadhamaṃ manyamāno nirupamavrīḍāniveśanirbharaṃ nirbhartsayati vatsarājaḥ /
"dhārāveśma' ityādi, "karṇa' ityādi ca ślokadvayaṃ prāgudāhṛtamatra yojyam /
tṛtīye 'ṅke rājā---(sāstraṃ niśvasya)
children.translated_text: As elsewhere: seeing the ornamental branches being consumed by the fire blazing within the city, afflicted by a fresh surge of grief...

children.text: sarvatra jvaliteṣu veśmasu bhayādālījane vidrute trāsotkampavihastayā pratipadaṃ devyā patantyā tadā /
children.translated_text: When everywhere the houses were ablaze, the retinue of attendants fled in terror, the queen stumbling at every step in her bewilderment of frightened trembling —

children.text: hā nātheti muhuḥ pralāpaparayā dagdhaṃ varākyā tathā śāntenāpi vayaṃ tu tena dahanenādyāpi dahyāmahe // VjivC_4.20 //
children.translated_text: crying 'Ah, my lord!' again and again, overcome by lamentation — the poor one was thus burnt; yet even we, by that fire, though now extinguished, are still being burnt today! // VjivC_4.20 //

children.text:
atra śāntenāpi nirvāṇenāpi tenāmlānamālatīmukulakomaladehavidāhānumīyamānanairghṛṇyena dahanenāpyekavyāpārā(napagata)karaṇā vayamadyāpi dahyāmahe iti nūtanollekhavirodhālaṅkāreṇa karuṇā pūrvaṃ niviṣṭāpi vakratāṃ nīyate /
api ca tathā vidhātuṃ komalatvādeva devyā tadaiva dagdhaṃ, vayaṃ punarvajrasārātikaṭorimāṇo 'dyāpi dahyāmahe na bhasmībhavāma iti viśeṣaṇaṃ prastutamevollāsayati /
caturthe 'ṅke rājā---(sakaruṇamātmagatam) hā devi
children.translated_text: Here, 'even by that extinguished [fire]' — even by that [fire] which has died out — whose cruelty is inferred from the burning of a body tender as an unwithered jasmine bud — by that very fire alone...

children.text: cakṣuryasya tavānanādapagataṃ nābhūtkvacinnarvṛtaṃ yenaiṣā satataṃ tvadekaśayanaṃ vakṣaḥsthalī kalpitā /
children.translated_text: 'Your eye never departed from her face, nor ever closed; by you this chest was always fashioned as a couch for her alone.

children.text: yenoktāsi vinā tvayā bata jagacchūnyaṃ kṣaṇājjāyate so 'yaṃ dambhadhṛtavrataḥ priyatame kartuṃ kimapyudyataḥ // VjivC_4.21 //
children.translated_text: By you it was said: "Without you, alas, the world becomes empty in an instant!" Yet this one — he whose vows are hypocritical — is about to do something to the beloved, O dearest one!' // VjivC_4.21 //

children.text:
iti sakhedamāste /
atra hi kvaciditi keliklamāpanodananimittaṃ niketapṛṣṭhasaṃcāraṇīyāsu līlāsu aprayatnasulabhadarśane tanumātronmīlitasaṃpātabimbalāvaṇyaleśaśaṅkamānatvadānanāntevāsitve candramasi darśitanijavākyopārūḍhapadārthatvāt paryālocanayā (karuṇameva) pratyāyayati /
yeneti paryaṅkārdhaśayanamapi pravāsapadamiva pariharatīti tadeva vyanakti /
children.translated_text: 'By whom' — he who avoids even half the couch as if it were a place of exile — this is what [the verse] reveals.

children.text: kṣaṇāditi etāvantamapi kālaṃ tvayā virahitasya jīvataḥ kiyadaugyaṃ mama /
children.translated_text: 'In an instant' — how great is the cruelty of one who lives separated from you for even this much time!

children.text: (evaṃ) punaḥ sakalo 'pyalīka evāyaṃ premabandho 'vadhāryatāmiti tathaiva pratipādayati /
children.translated_text: Thus, again, 'Let it be understood that this entire bond of love is nothing but a pretense' — this is what is being conveyed.
'This one' and so forth — was already explained above. //
Thus [the speaker] sits in sorrow. Here, 'never' — in the pastimes that should be conducted on the rooftop of the house for the purpose of dispelling the fatigue of love-play — not...

children.text:
evametat, antaravākyakadambakābhivyaktayābhinavabhaṅgyā pūrvasmātsvādādāsvādāntarasampadaṃ kāmapi karuṇasya kurute /
pañcame 'ṅke--- rājā--(saviśeṣotkaṇṭhaṃ niśvasya)
children.translated_text: Thus it is: through the manifestation of a cluster of intervening sentences, with an unprecedented turn, some charm — a wealth of a different relish from the previous relish — [is produced]...

children.text: bhrūbhaṅgaṃ rucire lalāṭaphalake tāraṃ samāropayet bāṣpāmbuplutapītapatraracanāṃ kuryātkapolasthalīm /
children.translated_text: She should firmly arch her brow on the lovely forehead, make the cheek-surface [display] a tear-water-flooded painted-leaf design,

children.text: vyāvṛttairvinibaddhacāṭumahimāmālokya lajjānatā tiṣṭhet kiṃ kṛtakopacārakaruṇairāśvāsayaināṃ priyām // VjivC_4.22 //
children.translated_text: seeing the grandeur of flattery composed through averted [glances], she should stand with the modesty-vine bowing — or should [the lover] console this beloved with compassion simulating feigned anger? // VjivC_4.22 //

children.text: atrādhigamapratyāśāsaṃbhāvitapadmāvatīpāṇipīḍasyānaṅkuritamanorathaleśasyāpi tatkālakandalitautsukyaparavaśīkṛtāntaḥ karaṇavṛtterunmādyata iva prāptāmeva pradyotarājaputrīṃ (manvānasya) rājñaḥ prasādasamayasamucitaprakāra (cintanaṃ kāṣṭhāṃ) karuṇasyāvatārayati /

children.translated_text: In the same act,

children.text: kiṃ prāṇā na mayā tavānugamanaṃ kartuṃ samutsāhitā baddhā kiṃ na jaṭā na vā praruditaṃ bhrāntaṃ vane nirjane /
children.translated_text: 'Have I not urged my very life-breaths to follow you? Have I not bound my matted locks? Have I not wept and wandered in the forest?

children.text: tvatsaṃprāptivilobhanena punarapyūnena pāpena kiṃ kiṅkṛtvā kupitā yadadya na vacastvaṃ me dadāsi priye // VjivC_4.23 //
children.translated_text: Yet, by some lesser sin, [incited] by the temptation of obtaining you again — what have you done that you are angry and today give me no word, O beloved?' // VjivC_4.23 //

Here, of one whose desire for the hand of <s>Padmāvatī</s> had been conceived through the hope of obtaining [her], and even whose slightest trace of [fulfilled] desire had not yet sprouted — the eagerness budding at that very moment...

children.text:
"iti roditi" ityantena manāgunmādamudrāpyunmīlitā tameva proddīpayati /
ṣaṣṭhe 'ṅke rājā---hā devi !
children.translated_text: 'Thus he weeps' — the concluding words. The seal of love-madness too, being revealed, kindles that very [effect]. In the sixth act, the king [says]: 'Alas, O queen!'

children.text: tvatsaṃprāptivilobhanena sacivaiḥ prāṇā mayā dhāritāḥ tanmatvātyajataḥ śarīrakamidaṃ me nāsti niḥsnehatā /
children.translated_text: My life was sustained by my ministers with the enticement of obtaining you; so do not think me heartless for abandoning this body;

children.text: āsanno 'vasarastadānugamane jātā dhṛtiḥ kiṃ tvayaṃ khedo yacchatadhā gataṃ na hṛdayaṃ tadvatkṣaṇe dāruṇe // VjivC_4.24 //
children.translated_text: the moment for following you is near—resolve has arisen—but this is the grief: that my heart did not shatter into a hundred pieces at that terrible moment as yours did. (Vjiv 4.24)

children.text:
atra nairāśyena rāśībhūtabhūritaraśokāvegavedanādahyamānamānasapratīkārakāraṇaṃ kālindīnāmanimnagāsaṃgamanam /
tasya priyānugamamapi vastu vācyavistaraṃ prakaraṇābharaṇāyate /
"procyate kiyat" ityuktyā vividhairvā vilāsaiḥ, kutaḥ kathopakārakāditi kathāyāḥ samāśaṅkitavicchedāyāḥ prarohayatīti (?) /
kimuktaṃ bhavati---svalpo 'pi vācyaviśeṣaḥ saviśeṣavisphāritaḥ samuddhāṭitarasakavāṭadvārasarasoktivisaravikāsinyā prakaraṇavicchittyā vitanyamānaḥ kamapi vakrimāṇamāsādayati /
yathā raghuvaṃśe mṛgayāprakaraṇe--- atra hi taraṅgiṇītīralekhāsvākheṭavāṭodyatena pramādyatā daśarathena rājñā sthavirāndhatapasvibālavadho vyadhīyateti ekavākyaśakyapratipādano 'pyayamarthaḥ punaḥ paramārthasarasasarasvatīsarvasvāyamānapratibhāvidhānakuśale kavinā tādṛśyā prakaraṇavicchittyā visphāritaścetanacamatkārakāraṇatāmadhitiṣṭhati /
tathāhi---yadyatrānekanaktandinānubandhivividhamṛgayāvyāpāraparavaśīkṛtāntaḥ karaṇakavalitasakalataditara (vyāpāra) vyāvṛttyavasaraprasaradabhyāsarasasodarātmakamṛgayānurāgagarimātaḥ prāṇyetādṛgrūpo na pratihanyeta, tadā sadācārasaṃpādanacaṇe tribhuvanābhayadīkṣādhikāriṇi kiraṇamālinaḥ kule tilakāyamānasyākhilavidyāpārāvārapāradṛśvanaḥ kīrtidhanasya dhanya(daśaratha) nāmno dharitrīpateḥ pavitritatridivādhipārdhāsanasya tathāvidhākaraṇīyakaraṇaṃ maharṣiṇāpyudāhriyamāṇamanupapannaprāyameva pratibhāsetāpātataḥ /
idaṃ ca tatraiva sakalamunmīlitaṃ manāgudāhriyate /
children.translated_text: Here, the arrival at the river named <s>Kālindī</s> is the cause for counteracting the mind that is being burned by the torment of the overwhelming surge of grief accumulated through despair. Even the actual following of the beloved—the expressive expansion of the described [action]—ornaments the section. By the expression 'how much shall be told,' or with various elaborate touches, [the question arises] 'from where?'—from what is useful to the narrative—it makes the story, whose interruption was anticipated, sprout forth again (?). What is being said is: even a small particular of the expressed [content], when unfolded with distinctive expansion, when elaborated through a section-strikingness that causes the floodgates of <s>rasa</s> to open in a cascade of juicy expression—attains some indescribable obliquity. For example, in the <s>Raghuvaṃśa</s>, the hunting episode: here, on the banks of the river, while king <s>Daśaratha</s> was heedlessly engaged in hunting preparations in his hunting-enclosure, the killing of the young [son] of an old blind ascetic occurred. Although this meaning could be presented in a single sentence, nevertheless, by the poet—who is skilled in the exercise of creative power that vies with the totality of the supremely juicy <s>Sarasvatī</s> (goddess of speech)—it was expanded through such section-strikingness that it attains the status of being the cause of wonder in consciousness. For thus: if the excessive subjugation of the inner faculty through manifold hunting activities extending over many days and nights—the total withdrawal from all other activities being swallowed up [by the hunting passion]—the gravity of the hunting-passion that is the sibling of the relish of practiced habit—if one of such a kind were not checked, then the commission of such an improper act by a king named <s>Daśaratha</s>, blessed with wealth of fame, who is the ornament of the lineage of the ray-garlanded [Sun], who has purified even the half-throne of the lord of heaven—a king endowed with proficiency in accomplishing good conduct, entitled to the vow of giving fearlessness to the three worlds, who has seen the far shore of all learning—even when cited by the great sage, would appear at first glance as practically impossible. And this has all been brought to light in that very [passage]; a little is cited [here]:
Tigers, fearlessly leaping forth from caves, meeting him head-on—like wind-broken branches at the tops of blossoming <s>āsana</s> trees—

children.text: śikṣāviśeṣalaghuhastatayā sa dhanvī tūṇīcakāra śarapūritavaktrarandhrān // VjivC_4.25 //
children.translated_text: he, the archer, through the extraordinary lightness of hand [gained] from training, made them quiver-ful, their mouth-cavities filled with arrows. (Vjiv 4.25)

children.text: api turagasamīpādutpatantaṃ mayūraṃ na sa rucirakalāpaṃ bāṇalakṣīcakāra /
children.translated_text: Even a peacock with its beautiful plumage, startled near his horse, he did not make a target for his arrow;

children.text: sapadi gatamanaskaśchinnamālyānukīrṇe rativigalitabandhe keśahaste priyāyāḥ // VjivC_4.26 //
children.translated_text: his mind instantly went to the hair-braid of his beloved, its garland scattered, its binding loosened after lovemaking. (Vjiv 4.26)

children.text: lakṣyīkṛtasya hariṇasya hariprabhāvaḥ prekṣya sthitāṃ sahacarīṃ vyavadhāya dehāt /
children.translated_text: Of the deer that had been made a target, the one of <s>Hari</s>'s (<s>Viṣṇu</s>'s) might, seeing its companion standing, interposing her body,

children.text: ākarṇakṛṣṭamapi kāmitayā sa dhanvī bāṇaṃ kṛpāmṛdumanāḥ pratisaṃjahāra // VjivC_4.27 //
children.translated_text: the archer, though his bow was drawn to the ear, with a mind softened by compassion, through love, withdrew the arrow. (Vjiv 4.27)

And so forth. Through these specific sentences, beautiful with the propriety of the varied expressed and expressor, the extreme subjugation through hunting-activities is made clearly perceivable. For example:
He spent a night somewhere in the forest on a bed of delicate flowers and shoots,
accompanied by lamps of blazing great herbs, with equipage unassembled and unaccompanied by women—passing the night in forest-pleasure. (Vjiv 4.28)

children.text:
atra vanaratiriti viśeṣaṇavakratā vane sthityā vilāsagṛhakelīparyaṅke preyasī sametya madhugoṣṭhīprabhṛtyupabhogapratītipratyākhyātapratītiṃ pratipādayantyā prastutarasāveśa eva vitanyate /
triyāmeti vacanavakratollekhena ciratarasamayamandha (kāraḥ) samunmīlyate /
rūḍhivakratāmahimnā ca nirbharāndhakāranivāritaruciravyāpāraprakārāntarasāntarāyakāritvāt tatpratikūlatā pratipādyate /
ata evātivāhayāṃbabhūveti kriyāvakratvavaicitryeṇa dāruṇadehavedanāṃ śayanagataḥ apagamayāmāsa, paramapariśramavidhāne nidrā rasadāyinītyabhinananda /
yathā ca
children.translated_text: Here, the qualifier-obliquity of '<s>vanarati</s>' (forest-pleasure)—by establishing through staying in the forest that the perception of enjoyments such as intimate conversations on the lover's couch and play-bed is refuted—expands the very immersion in the <s>rasa</s> at hand. By the expression-obliquity of '<s>triyāmā</s>' (triple-watch, i.e. the whole night), the darkness of an exceedingly long period is opened up. And by the greatness of <s>rūḍhi</s>-obliquity (conventional usage), its hostility is established, since the dense darkness prevents the varieties of beautiful activities. For precisely this reason, by the variety of action-obliquity in '<s>ativāhayāṃbabhūva</s>' (he passed [the night]): lying upon his bed, he made the cruel bodily pain pass away; he celebrated the sleep as a giver of <s>rasa</s> in the accomplishment of supreme exhaustion.
Thus, his mind forgetting all other duties, the burden of governance resting on his ministers—the king,

children.text: parivṛddharāgamanubandhasevayā mṛgayā jahāra catureva kāminī // VjivC_4.29 //
children.translated_text: by the service of steadily increasing passion—the hunt stole [him] away like a clever mistress. (Vjiv 4.29)

children.text:
atra jahāreti kriyāvakratvavicchittyā, mṛgayāyā karaṇīyetarabhāvanāsuvikalāntaḥ karaṇatvamaṅkuritaṃ mahībhartuḥ /
tathā
children.translated_text: Here, by the strikingness of action-obliquity in '<s>jahāra</s>' (stole away), the state of the earth-bearer's inner faculty being easily made utterly incapable of conceiving [anything] other than what should not be done [is suggested] as budding through the hunt. Similarly:
Then, at some point, having followed the track of a <s>ruru</s> deer, unseen by his attendants in the forest,

children.text: śramaphenamucā tapasvigāḍhāṃ tamasāṃ prāpa nadīṃ turaṅgameṇa // VjivC_4.30 //
children.translated_text: with a horse whose mouth was releasing the foam of fatigue, he reached the river of <s>Tamasā</s>, crowded with ascetics. (Vjiv 4.30)

children.text:
atra tapasvigāḍhāmiti viśeṣaṇavakratayā vividhadharmācāraparāyaṇatāpasasaṃkulāṃ tamasāṃ paśyannapi śabdaśravaṇamātrāt śaraṃ vyākṛṣya śaramokṣamavikalāntaḥ karaṇaḥ kathamakurvateti prakāśyate /
"apathe padamarpayanti hi śrutavanto 'pi rajonimīlitāḥ" ityanena nyāyena paradhārādhirūḍhadurdharavyasanarāgāndakārakavalitavivekadṛṣṭayastathāvidhā aśuddhādhvani sañcaranta ityupapattirapyupapāditā /
uttarakathopakāro 'pyekadeśasyāstyeva /
tathā hi---
children.translated_text: Here, by the qualifier-obliquity of '<s>tapasvigāḍhām</s>' (crowded with ascetics), it is made clear that even while seeing [the river] crowded with ascetics devoted to various righteous practices, how could he, with unimpaired inner faculty, merely upon hearing a sound, have drawn his arrow and released it? By the principle 'even the learned, blinded by passion, place their foot on a wrong path'—the perception that those of such a kind, their eye of discrimination swallowed by the darkness of passion overwhelmed by an irresistible vice mounting the current of another [impulse], wander on an impure path—this reasoning too has been established. There is also some contribution to the subsequent narrative for a portion. For thus:

children.text: diṣṭāntamāpsyati bhavānapi putraśokā- dante vayasyahamiveti tamuktavantam // VjivC_4.31 //
children.translated_text: 'You too, O Lord, shall meet your end through grief for a son, even as I, your friend'—to him who spoke thus— (Vjiv 4.31)

children.text: iti viśīrṇatāpasavitīrṇaśāpasya tāpasaṃ prati prativacanaṃ kausalyāpateḥ---tathā hi
children.translated_text: —this is the reply of the lord of <s>Kausalyā</s> (<s>Daśaratha</s>) to the ascetic, whose curse was released as [his] son's life ebbed. For thus:
Even this curse, O Lord, is bestowed upon me with grace by the Blessed One, upon me who has not seen the beauty of a son's lotus-face;

children.text: kṛṣyāṃ dahannapi khalu kṣitimindhaneddhaḥ bījaprarohajananīṃ dahanaḥ karoti // VjivC_4.32 //
children.translated_text: for even fire, kindled by fuel, while burning the cultivated field, makes it the producer of seed-sprouts. (Vjiv 4.32)

children.text:
atra śāpa iti evaṃvidhāpacāraprāgbhāraprabhavo bhavatu nāma /
sānugraha iti anugrahaḥ punarayamanupapanna evāsyāmavasthāyām /
bhagavatetyanarthadarśanena sahajadayālunā /
yadi vā bhagavatā śāpo 'pi iti śāpānugrahayordahanavāriṇorivaikakālamekaviṣayavartitvamasatorapi bhagavat(svarūpa)saṃpatsāmarthyādeva saṃbhāvyate, adṛṣṭatanayānanapadmaśobhe mayi etasmādevānugrahādavaśyaṃbhāvinaḥ sucirakālābhikāṅkṣitasya sutāvalambanatanorjovitaphalasya vilokanotkaṇṭhāpāravaśyāt (sārthakyam) ityalamatiprasaṅgena /
asyā eva prabhedāntaramunmīlayati---
children.translated_text: Here, 'the curse'—even though produced by the weight of such an offense, let it be so. 'With grace'—but this grace is practically impossible in this state. 'By the Blessed One'—by one who is innately compassionate, even in the face of calamity. Or: the very fact that 'even the curse is by the Blessed One'—the simultaneous existence in a single domain of both curse and grace, like fire and water, even though they are non-existent [together], is conceivable precisely through the power of the Blessed One's nature. 'Upon me who has not seen the beauty of a son's lotus-face'—precisely from this grace, the fulfillment of the fruit of life—the support of a son long desired and inevitably to come—through the overwhelming longing to behold [him]—enough of this digression. He now unfolds another subdivision of the same [prakaraṇavakratā]:
That which, being a vessel for the variety of the narrative, attains obliquity—
that which is composed as a component for the beauty of a <s>sarga</s> (canto) composition and the like. (Vjiv 4.9)

children.text:
"tadvakrimāṇaṃ(prapadyate)" kiṃvisiṣṭaṃ---"kathavaicitryapātraṃ" = prastutasaṃvidhānakabhaṅgībhājanaṃ /
kiṃ tat ? "yadaṅkaṃsargabandhādeḥ saundaryāya nibadhyate" = "yat"---jalakrīḍādiprakaraṇaṃ ("sargabandhādeḥ") mahākāvyaprabhṛteḥ ("saundaryāya")---upaśobhāniṣapattyai ("nibadhyate") niveśyate /
ayamasya paramārthaḥ---prabandheṣu jalakelikusumāpacayaprabhṛti prakaraṇaṃ prakrāntasaṃvidhānakānubandhi nibadhyamānaṃ nidhānamiva kamanīyasaṃpadaḥ saṃpadyate /
yathā raghuvaṃśe---
children.translated_text: 'That attains obliquity'—of what kind?—'a vessel for the variety of the narrative'—a receptacle for the charm of the narrative arrangement at hand. What is that?—'that which is composed as a component for the beauty of a canto-composition and the like'—'that' refers to a section such as a water-sport, etc.; 'of a canto-composition and the like'—of a <s>mahākāvya</s> (great poem) and so forth; 'for the beauty'—for the production of embellishment; 'is composed'—is established. This is the ultimate meaning: in literary works, sections such as water-sport, flower-gathering, and so forth, when composed as linked to the narrative arrangement at hand, become like a treasure-house of charming abundance. For example, in the <s>Raghuvaṃśa</s>:
Then, on the <s>Sarayū</s> river, whose waves were playful with intoxicated royal geese, bearing flowers of shore-creepers,

children.text: vihartumicchā vanitāsakhasya tasyāmbhasi grīṣmasukhe babhūva // VjivC_4.33 //
children.translated_text: there arose in him, friend of women, the desire to sport in the waters, pleasant in summer. (Vjiv 4.33)

children.text:
ityādi /
jalakrīḍāsparśānantaralakṣitatvāt akhilamadavikala(lalanā)vilāsamūlādhyāsyamānotsavākulasya(kumudakanyā)kandukakrīḍālakṣaṇamutsavāntaramuttarakathopakāryupapadyate, tadvidāmāhlādamāvaiti ca /
tathā hi rājñaḥ karā(sphālanābhyukṣaṇā)divārivihārarasaparavaśāntaḥ karaṇasya (karāravindā) dalaṅkaraṇamalakṣitapatanamutpannakutūhalā kumudvatī nāma nāgakanyā jagṛhe /
tatastasminnādarodrekādanviṣṭe 'pyanāsādite pāthontarvartinaṃ nāganāyakamānīya niveditaṃ kumudamuddiśya daśānanāntakanandanaḥ samadhatta dhanuṣi dhanvī gārutmatamastram /
atha paritrāṇaparyākulaḥ kumudaḥ kumudvatīṃ svasāramābharaṇena samaṃ karakamalālaṅkāriṇā videhanandinīnandanasyār (payāmāsa) /
atra sūktāni kānicidudāhriyante /
children.translated_text: And so forth. Because the water-sport is observed immediately after, another festival—characterized by the ball-game of <s>Kumudvatī</s> the <s>Nāga</s> princess, the festival being bustling with all sorts of intoxicated women's coquetries that are the foundation of the celebration—serves as useful for the subsequent narrative, and produces delight for the knowledgeable. For thus: of the king, whose inner faculty was overcome by the relish of water-sport—splashing, sprinkling, and so forth—<s>Kumudvatī</s>, a <s>Nāga</s> (serpent) princess, seized his lotus-hand-ornament whose fall he had not noticed, out of newly-arisen curiosity. Then, when [the ornament] was not found despite being sought due to the surge of displeasure, the son of the destroyer of the ten-headed one [<s>Rāvaṇa</s>]—the archer—having brought the <s>Nāga</s> lord dwelling beneath the waters, and having been informed regarding <s>Kumud</s> [the <s>Nāga</s> king], fitted upon his bow the <s>Gārutmata</s> (Garuḍa) weapon. Then <s>Kumuda</s>, distressed for the protection [of his family], offered his sister <s>Kumudvatī</s>, along with the ornament, to the son of the delight of the daughter of <s>Videha</s>. Here some well-composed [verses] are cited:

children.text: avaimi kāryantaramānuṣasya viṣṇoḥ sutākhyāmaparāṃ tanuṃ tvām /
children.translated_text: I know you to be another body of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, who is of human purpose, called 'son';

children.text: so 'haṃ kathaṃ nātha tavācareya- mārādhanīyasya dhṛtervighātam // VjivC_4.34 //
children.translated_text: how then could I, O Lord, commit an offense against the resolve of one who should be propitiated? (Vjiv 4.34)
Seeing [the ornament] springing up from the lake like a falling celestial portent from the sky,
the child [<s>Kuśa</s>], with excessive curiosity, seized your victory-ornament—[that which was tossed up] by the impact of the hand as if it were a ball. (Vjiv 4.35)
Let that very [ornament], by this arm of yours reaching to the knee, marked with the scars of bowstring-strikes,

children.text: bhujena rakṣāparigheṇa bhūme- rupaitu yogaṃ punaraṃsalena // VjivC_4.36 //
children.translated_text: a rampart of protection for the earth—the broad-shouldered one—attain union [with the arm] again. (Vjiv 4.36)

children.text: imāṃ svasāraṃ ca yavīyasīṃ me kumudvatīṃ nārhasi nānumantum /
children.translated_text: And this younger sister of mine, <s>Kumudvatī</s>—do not refuse to accept her,

children.text: ātmāparādhaṃ nudatīṃ cirāya śuśrūṣayā pārthiva pādayoste // VjivC_4.37 //
children.translated_text: she who will for a long time ward off her own offense through service at your feet, O king. (Vjiv 4.37)

children.text:
eteṣu bhujaṅgarājavākyeṣu ādye "viṣṇo'riti rūḍhivakratayā vaktṛprabhāvāt paryaṅkībhūya bhuvanādhāreṇa anantena niṣevyamāṇasya sakalājñāpālanasaṃpādane sajjo bhujaṅgāntaro bhaviṣyatīti pratipādyate /
"sa' iti saṃvṛtivakratvena yaḥ satatameva tava vāstavyaviṣayaḥ sa evetyabhivyajyate /
katham iti padavakratayā (tvayi) bhaktiriti vidheyatāniyantritasya mama na kenāpi prakāreṇa duścaritāpannaṃ śīlamāśaṅkyamiti /
dvitīye 'pi "autpātikajyotirivāntarikṣāt" ityupamayā na kathaṃ kisalayitadigantarālataralitamarīcimaṇḍalatayā yāvadasmākaṃ akāraṇakamahābhayasaṃśayasaṃpādanamapītyavagamyate /
tṛtīye 'pi tadetaditi saṃvṛtivakratayā yasya tvatpitururasthalamiva kaustubhasya bhadrajayavibhūṣyatāviṣayaḥ iti "rakṣāparigheṇa bhūmeḥ" iti rūpakeṇa nivāritanikhilavasundharāduḥkhasya tvadvāhoralaṅkaraṇam, "śuśrūṣayā pādayo' riti caraṇaśuśrūṣāpavitreṇa pāṇināṃ saṃpāditapariṇayotsavāṃ "yaviyasī' miti drutataratāruṇyāvatāritatvadanurāgaprāgbhārām /
ata eva nārhasi nānumantumapi /
tarhyarhasyaiva gatyantarābhāvāditi pratīyate /
children.translated_text: In these speeches of the serpent-king: in the first, by <s>rūḍhi</s>-obliquity (conventional usage) of '<s>Viṣṇu</s>'—through the power of the speaker—it is established that another serpent will be ready for the accomplishment of obedience to all commands, [just as] the world-supporting <s>Ananta</s> (the infinite serpent) serves the one who is reclining on the couch [i.e., <s>Viṣṇu</s>]. By '<s>sa</s>' (he/that), through concealment-obliquity, it is suggested: 'the very one who is always the object of your dwelling [i.e., your constant companion/protector].' By 'how' (<s>katham</s>), through word-obliquity: devotion to you being the binding duty of mine—my character should not even be suspected of having committed a misdeed, by any means. In the second too, by the simile 'like a falling celestial portent from the sky'—it is understood that not only [the anxiety about] the expansive shimmering mandala of rays quivering across the intervals of the directions, but also the procurement of great causeless fear for us [is implied]. In the third too, by concealment-obliquity of 'that very [ornament]': that which has the status of adorning your father's chest like the <s>Kaustubha</s> [gem]—the auspicious victory-ornament; by the <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor) 'a rampart of protection for the earth'—the ornament of your arm, which has warded off all the earth's suffering; 'through service at your feet'—[she] whose nuptial celebration has been accomplished by hands purified through the service of [your] feet; 'younger'—one upon whom the weight of her youthful passion for you has recently descended swiftly. Therefore, 'do not refuse to accept'—[meaning] you must indeed accept, since there is no other course—this is the suggestion.
'<s>Kumudvatī</s> obtained from the descendant of <s>Kakutstha</s> a son named <s>Atithi</s>.' (Vjiv 4.38)

children.text:
ityanantaraprakaraṇe kathopakāro 'pi prakaṭameva vārivihārasya darśitaḥ /
nasmādeva ca tadavasaranidānatayā nidāghavarṇanamapi atra---
children.translated_text: In the immediately subsequent section, the contribution of the water-sport to the narrative is also clearly shown. And precisely for that reason, the description of summer too, as the occasion for it [the water-sport], is [placed] here:
Then upon him, wearing an upper garment studded with gems, a long garland hanging to the breast, exceedingly pale,
with cloth carried away by sighs—summer arrived, as if to teach the guise of the beloved. (Vjiv 4.39)

children.text:
ityādinā nibadhyamānaṃ na kathāvaicitryamātramatikrāmati /
(asmin samasta) prabandhe prakaraṇaṃ prakrāntasaṃvidhānamapi (nānāpriyakāryatantumilitarūpakāraṇaṃ prasaktam /
asyā nidarśanānyapi svayamanyānyudāharaṇaṇīyāni /
children.translated_text: — what is being composed through such [narration] does not transcend mere variety of the story. In this entire composition, the episode (<s>prakaraṇa</s>), even though carrying forward the established plot, is connected [with] the cause constituted by the interweaving of various beloved actions. Other illustrations of this too should be cited by oneself.
The narration of water-sports and the like, beautiful in its arrangement,
nourishes a pleasure that is devoted to the vital activity of the story of the composition. // VjivC_4.40 //
This is an intermediate verse. He now brings forth yet another subvariety of this [episode-obliqueness] —
Where some touchstone, as it were, of the flow of the principal <s>rasa</s> is discerned,
unattainable by the preceding and following [episodes] — that is some [special] obliqueness of the act and the like. // Vjiv_4.10 //

children.text:
"sāṅkādeḥ kāpi vakratā" "aṅkādeḥ" = aṅkasargādeḥ prakaraṇasya "sā kāpi" = alaukikī "vakratā" = vakrabhāvo bhavatīti saṃbandhaḥ /
"yatrāṅgirasaniṣyandanikaṣaḥ ko 'pi" lakṣyate" "yatra"---yasyāṃ aṅgī yaḥ "rasaḥ" prāṇarūpaḥ, tasya niṣyandaḥ pravāhaḥ tasya, kāñcanasyeva nikaṣaḥ parīkṣopalavadviṣayaviśeṣaḥ "ko 'pi" abhūta---nirmāṇanirupamo lakṣyate (nikaṣa) yojane (kāñcanasya rekho) dayairiva viśeṣaḥ /
kiṃ viśiṣṭaḥ "pūrvottarairasaṃpādyaḥ"---prakparavṛttibhiraṅkādyaiḥ saṃpādayitumaśakyaḥ /
idamatra tātparyam /
pradhānarasasarvasvakrīḍāniketanaṃ tātkimapi prakaraṇaṃ (yatra) prakaṭataraṃ ca vakratāvicchittirvidyotate /
yadīyalāvaṇyātiśayaṃ manāṅmātramapi pūrvāṇyaparāṇi vā prakaraṇāntarāṇi nānukartuṃ śakruvanti /
yathā vikramorvaśyāmunmattāṅkaḥ--- tatra hi prastutarasāsādhāraṇa(vibhāvānubhāva) mādhuryasaṃpattyā vipralambhaśṛṅgārasyāṅginaḥ sa ko 'pi (sahṛdayahṛdayā) deḥ rasaniṣyandaparispandaḥ paristīryate, yaḥ na kevalaṃ prakaraṇāntare prabandhāntare 'pyaśakyakāmanīyakakaṇikānukāraḥ /
tathā ca tadupakrama eva--- rājā (sasaṃbhramam)---ā durātman, tiṣṭha tiṣṭha ! kva nu khalu priyatamāmādāya gacchisi ?(vilokya) kathaṃ śailaśikharāt gaganamutplutya bāṇairmāmabhivarṣati ? (vibhāvya sabāṣpam) kathaṃ vipralabdho 'smi---
children.translated_text: 'Some obliqueness of the act and the like' — of the act (<s>aṅka</s>), the scene (<s>sarga</s>), and the like, the episode — 'that is some,' i.e., extraordinary, 'obliqueness,' i.e., oblique quality — this is the syntactical connection. 'Where some touchstone of the flow of the principal <s>rasa</s> is discerned' — 'where,' i.e., in which [episode]; the principal (<s>aṅgin</s>) '<s>rasa</s>' is in the form of the life-force; its 'flow' (<s>niṣyanda</s>) is its streaming forth; its 'touchstone' — like the touchstone of gold, a special domain of testing — 'some,' i.e., unprecedented, unmatched in creation, 'is discerned'; in the application of the touchstone, a distinction [appears] like the streak-mark [on a touchstone] for gold. How qualified? — 'unattainable by the preceding and following' — unachievable by the prior and subsequent acts and the like. The purport here is this: the principal <s>rasa</s>, whose playground is the totality of the [dramatic work], has some episode in which the flash of obliqueness blazes forth most conspicuously. The surpassing loveliness of that [episode], not even a fraction of it, cannot be reproduced by the other episodes, whether prior or subsequent. For example, the Madness Act (<s>unmattāṅka</s>) in the <s>Vikramorvaśīya</s> — for there, through the excellence of the sweetness of the <s>vibhāvas</s> (determinants) and <s>anubhāvas</s> (consequents) that are unique to the relevant <s>rasa</s>, there is spread a certain vital activity of the flow of <s>rasa</s> for <s>vipralambhaśṛṅgāra</s> (love-in-separation), the principal [<s>rasa</s>], that overwhelms the hearts of the sensitive — [a flow] whose charming particle cannot be imitated not merely in another episode but even in another composition. And thus, at the very opening of that [act]: 'The King (with agitation): Ah, villain! Stop, stop! Where are you going, carrying away my beloved? (Looking) What! From the mountain peak, flying into the sky, he showers me with arrows? (Realizing, with tears) Alas, I have been deceived!' —

children.text: navajaladharaḥ saṃnaddho 'yaṃ na dṛptaniśācaraḥ suradhanuridaṃ dūrākṛṣṭaṃ na nāma śarāsanam /
children.translated_text: This is a fresh rain-cloud that has armed itself — not a proud night-roaming <s>rākṣasa</s>; this is <s>Indra</s>'s bow stretched across the distance — not, indeed, a bow and arrows;

children.text: ayamapi paṭurdhārāsāro na bāṇaparamparā kanakanikaṣasnigdhā vidyut priyā na mamorvaśī // VjivC_4.41 //
children.translated_text: this too is a dense downpour of rain — not a volley of arrows; [and that] lightning, glistening like [a streak on] a gold touchstone — is not my beloved <s>Urvaśī</s>. // VjivC_4.41 //

children.text:
anenonmīlitonmādadaśāvaiśasasya rājñaḥ, kavacitaḥ śiñcitakodaṇḍadaṇḍo darpādāpatan naktañcaro 'pi śakyapratīkāro na tvasau navāmbhoda iti, nārācanicayo 'pi na tathā marmāṇi kṛntati yathāyamāsāradhārānikara iti /
kiṃ ca nabhasi vā bhūyaḥ saudāminyāḥ anvīkṣaṇadṛṣṭanaṣṭāyāḥ kṣaṇāntare darśanamāsādyate, tathāvidhasthairyāsaṃbhāvitabhūmerapi priyāyāḥ tatkimidamiti cābhiprāyo vākyena pratipādyate /
"tiṣṭhetkopavaśādi"tyādi, "padbhyā'-miti, "taraṅge' tyādikaṃ (ca) prāgudāhṛtamasmābhiranusandheyam /
yathā vā kirātārjunīye bāhuyuddhaprakaraṇam---tatrāpi kavacādikāyarakṣaṇādyupakaraṇamantareṇāpi sahajabāhubalāvalepaprakāśanaprastāvaprāptipramodamānamānasasya nirupamaniyuddhanirmāṇanirmaryādanivedyamānasāhasasāhāyyasya pāṇḍusūnoḥ sa ko 'pi vīrarasasyotkarṣaḥ prakāśate /
(tiṣṭhatu tāvat sarvamitaraṃ sacetasāmityabhiprāyaḥ) /
parameśvarasyāpi kevalamānuṣasya bāhubalādevaṃ dūramutkṣipya viyatyāndolyamānasya kavikalpitacamatkārāntarakāraṇam (spaṣṭam) /
evamanyadapyudāhāryam /
punarimāmevānyathā prathayati---
children.translated_text: By this [verse], the king, whose condition of madness has been opened up to its violent extremity — [he reflects:] even a night-roaming [demon], armored and grasping the staff of a twanging bow, descending in his arrogance, could be resisted, but not this fresh rain-cloud; nor does even a mass of iron arrows cut the vital parts as much as this shower of rain-streams does. Moreover, the lightning in the sky — [which is] seen and lost from moment to moment through a series of glimpses — may be encountered again after another instant; but the beloved, whose ground is inconceivable for such steadfastness — 'what then is this?' — such is the intent conveyed by the sentence. [The passages] 'Let her stay, [she is] in the power of anger' and so on, '[I follow] on foot' and so on, 'On the wave' and so on — cited by us earlier — should be kept in mind. Or, as the wrestling episode (<s>bāhuyuddha-prakaraṇa</s>) in the <s>Kirātārjunīya</s> — there too, for the son of <s>Pāṇḍu</s> (<s>Arjuna</s>), whose mind rejoices at the occasion for displaying his innate strength-pride of arms — even without armor and other body-protective equipment — and whose daring is boundlessly displayed through the aid given by his limitless valor in the fashioning of an incomparable combat, there blazes forth a certain supreme excellence of the <s>vīrarasa</s> (heroic sentiment) that overwhelms the hearts of the sensitive — [the intent being:] 'let all else stand aside before the sensitive.' Even for the Supreme Lord [<s>Śiva</s>], when, by the arm-strength of a mere mortal, he is flung far and swung about in the sky, the cause of some other marvelous wonder fashioned by the poet is evident. Thus, other [examples] too may be cited. He now unfolds this very [obliqueness] in another way —
The variegation through other subjects, for the accomplishment of the principal subject —
where that shines forth with a fresh delineation — that too is another obliqueness of this [episode]. // Vjiv_4.11 //

children.text:
"aparāpyasya" prakaraṇasya "vakratā" vakrabhāvo bhavatīti saṃbandhaḥ /
"yatrollasati" = unmīlati /
(kīdṛśī) "sollekhā"---abhinavodbhedabhaṅgī /
(subhagā cāsau sundarapratirūpā) "vastvantaravicitratā" = vastvantaramitaradvastu, tasya vicitratā vaicitryaṃ nūtanacamatkāra iti yāvat /
kimarthaṃ "pradhānavastuniṣpattyai" /
pradhānamadhikṛtaṃ prakaraṇaṃ kamapi vakrimāṇamākrāmati /
yathā mudrārākṣase ṣaṣṭhe 'ṅke "tataḥ praviśati rajjuhastaḥ puruṣaḥ" ityādi prakaraṇam /
tatra hi sa pumān nirupamānanayakelikuśalakauṭilyaprayojyamāno nipuṇamatirjorṇodyāne mudrodgalanasamuccalitavipakṣatārūkṣaṃ rākṣasamākṛṣṭakṛpāṇapāṇimāpatantamapaśyanniva svayamudagragrīvāvalambinā rajjuvalayena vyāpādayitum (ātmānaṃ) ārebhe /
rākṣasenāpi kautukakaruṇākrāntamanasā bhadramukha kimidamiti pṛṣṭam /
āḥ kiṃ mama mahāduḥkhapraśamakāraṇe maraṇe 'ntarāyamācarasītyācacakṣe /
tannirbandhācca vadhyabhūmimānītasya mahāsattva(mukuṭa)maṇermaṇikāraśreṣṭhinaścandanadāsasya priyasuhṛdo duḥkhāvegamasahiṣṇurviṣṇudāso 'pi matpriyamitraṃ puro 'sya pāvakaṃ praviṣṭumudyataḥ /
tato 'hamapi tadvadeva śokāvegamasahamānaḥ prathamamevātmānaṃ vyāpādayāmītyāvedayāmāsa /
kiṃ bahunā, vicitrasaṃbhāvanāgahane nītivartmani vicakṣaṇaṃmanyasya rākṣasasyāpi tathā saṃbhramaḥ santāpamujjanayāṃbabhūve, yathā vā saḥ svadehadānena candanadāsadehamocanāyopacakrame /
atrāpi kiñcidudāhriyate yathā---
children.translated_text: 'Another obliqueness' — 'of this' episode — 'is an obliqueness,' i.e., an oblique quality — this is the syntactical connection. 'Where it shines forth,' i.e., unfolds. Of what kind? — 'with a fresh delineation' — a manner of unprecedented emergence, beautiful and of charming form. 'The variegation through other subjects' — 'other subjects' means another, different subject; its 'variegation' is its varied character, its novel wonder — this is the sense. For what purpose? — 'for the accomplishment of the principal subject.' The principal, i.e., the designated episode, attains a certain obliqueness. For example, the episode in the sixth act of the <s>Mudrārākṣasa</s>: 'Then enters a man with a rope in his hand,' and so on. For there, that man — being manipulated by the incomparable skill of the sportive cunning [of <s>Cāṇakya</s>] — the clever-minded one, in the <s>Jūrṇa</s> garden, seeing <s>Rākṣasa</s> charging upon him with drawn sword, fierce in the agitation provoked by the surfacing of the hostile faction's [conspiracy] concerning the seal, and [the man] pretending as if he did not see him — began himself to attempt suicide with a noose suspended from his upraised neck. And when <s>Rākṣasa</s>, his mind seized by curiosity and compassion, asked 'Good sir, what is this?' — he declared: 'Ah! Why do you create an obstacle to death, which is the cause of the cessation of my great suffering?' And from his insistence, the jewel-merchant <s>Candanadāsa</s>, the crown-jewel of the great-souled, having been brought to the execution ground, [another figure enters:] <s>Viṣṇudāsa</s>, unable to bear the onslaught of grief for his dear friend, [declared:] 'My dear friend is about to enter the fire before him!' Then he too announced: 'I too, unable to endure the onset of grief just like that, shall put myself to death first.' In brief, in the dense forest of wondrous contrivance upon the path of statecraft, <s>Rākṣasa</s> — who considered himself discerning — was seized by such confusion and distress that he proceeded to offer his own body for the release of <s>Candanadāsa</s>'s body. Here too something is illustrated, as follows —
[Prakrit:] Firm with the binding of the six strategies, with a noose-mouth fashioned in the sequence of expedients,
<s>Cāṇakya</s>'s rope of statecraft, prepared for the binding of the enemy, triumphs! // VjivC_4.42 //
[Sanskrit shadow:] Firm with the binding of the six strategies, with a noose-mouth fashioned in the sequence of expedients,
<s>Cāṇakya</s>'s rope of statecraft, prepared for the binding of the enemy, triumphs!
Thus the <s>chāyā</s> (Sanskrit rendering).

children.text:
viśeṣaṇavakratāviśiṣṭena rūpakeṇa puruṣasyāyamabhiprāyaḥ prakāśyate /
yathā--- ta eva guṇāsta evābhyupāyāstadeva ca nītitantram, tathāpi kasyacidevāvikalakauśalaprasāritā ripukulasaṃyamanāya saṃghaṭanā aviditavividhabandhayuktā nītiprayuktā tadvidāmapi vimohamāvahati, ata eva jayatīti /
tathā ca--- "rākṣasaḥ---bhadramukha asyāgnipraveśe suhṛdaste ko hetuḥ ? kimauṣadhapathātigairupahato mahāvyādhibhiḥ ? puruṣaḥ---ajja ṇahi ṇahi (ārya na hi na hi) rākṣasaḥ---kimagniviṣakalpayā narapaternirastaḥ krudhā ? puruṣaḥ---santaṃ pāvaṃ santaṃ pāvaṃ, candauttassa jaṇavade ṇa ṇisaṃsā paḍivattī /
(śāntaṃ pāpaṃ, śāntaṃ pāpam /
candraguptasya janapadeṣvanṛśaṃsā pratipattiḥ) rākṣasaḥ---alabhyamanuraktavān kathaya kiṃ nu nārījanam ? puruṣaḥ---(karṇau pidhāya) santaṃ pāvaṃ, abhūmi kkhu eso aviṇaassa /
(śāntaṃ pāpam /
abhūmiḥ khalveṣa avinayasyaḥ rākṣasaḥ---
children.translated_text: The intent of the man [in the drama] is made manifest through a <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor) distinguished by the obliqueness of qualifiers. Namely: the very same qualities, the very same expedients, the very same web of statecraft — yet the arrangement directed at subjugating the enemy-clan, deployed by someone's flawless skill, employing a political rope whose manifold binding-devices are unknown, brings bewilderment even to those who know [statecraft]; hence it 'triumphs.' And thus: '<s>Rākṣasa</s>: Good sir, what is the reason for your friend's entering the fire? Is he afflicted by grave diseases that have exceeded the path of medicine? The man: Sir, no, no! <s>Rākṣasa</s>: Has he been banished by the wrath of the king through [a sentence comparable to] the contrivance of fire and poison? The man: Forbid the evil! Forbid the evil! In the dominions of <s>Candragupta</s>, the policy is [one of] non-cruelty. <s>Rākṣasa</s>: Unattainable! Then tell me, has he become enamored of some woman? The man: (covering his ears) Forbid the evil! Indeed, this is no ground for impudence! <s>Rākṣasa</s>:' —

children.text: kimasya bhavato yathā suhṛda eva nāśo viṣam // VjivC_4.43 //
children.translated_text: 'What — is it that your friend's destruction is poison?' // VjivC_4.43 //

children.text:
puruṣaḥ---ajja aha iṃ ? (ārya atha kim)" atra mahāvyādhibhiriti bahuvacanavakratvaṃ, agniviṣakalpayeti ca (viśeṣaṇavakratvaṃ) tathāvidhārājāpathyavidhāyī vadhyasthānasthāpito 'pi candanadāsaḥ tatkalatramadyāpi yācito na samarpayatīti vyāpādyata ityasya vakṣyamāṇasya pradhānābhidheyasya nimittamādatte /
asyeti sahajasauhārdanibarhaṇanihanyamānasya /
"bhavato yathā" vitatavyatikarotsekakāriṇaḥ sāvatmahatyecchā /
anenaiva vividhavikalpanena yo 'yamarthaḥ samuddīpyamāno navatābhājanaṃ vibhūṣyamāṇaḥ san prikāśate /
evamanyadapi tata eva vibhāvya vyākhyeyam /
pradhānaphalasiddhaścātra "...vyāpattiṃ jñātamasya svatanumahamimāṃ niṣkrayaṃ kalpayami" ityunmīlitā tatastadanantaraprakaraṇe "tasyeyaṃ mama mṛtyulokapadavī vadhyastragābadhyatām" ityādinā niṣpāditā /
tāmeva bhaṅgyantareṇa vyācaṣṭe /
children.translated_text: The man: 'Sir, indeed so!' Here, the obliqueness of the plural 'by grave diseases' (<s>bahuvacana</s>), and the obliqueness of the qualifier in 'through the contrivance of fire and poison' — such an enactor of the royal disfavor — even though <s>Candanadāsa</s>, placed on the execution ground, has even now not surrendered his [<s>Cāṇakya</s>'s] wife despite being asked — [therefore] he is being put to death: [thus] the ground is laid for the principal subject about to be stated. 'Of this [man]' — one whose innate affection is being uprooted and slain. 'Of you' — one whose pride is wrought by extensive transgression — the desire for self-destruction [as well]. Through this very variegated contrivance, the subject-matter, being kindled and adorned as a vessel of novelty, shines forth. Thus, other [instances] too, from that very [play], should be examined and explained. And the principal fruition here — 'having learned of his imminent destruction, I arrange this body of mine as his ransom' — was opened up [in that act] and then accomplished in the episode immediately following, with 'This is my path to the world of the dead — let the garland of the condemned be tied [on me],' and so on. He expounds the same through another turn of expression:
By actors skilled in producing delight in the audience,
having assumed that role — performing a play-within-a-play, // Vjiv_4.12 //
somewhere within the episode, another episode is remembered [i.e., enacted],
[which] nourishes an obliqueness that is like the totality of the entire composition. // Vjiv_4.13 //

children.text:
"sarvaprabandhasarvasvakalpāṃ puṣṇāti vakratām" = sakalarūpakaprāṇarūpaṃ samullāsayati vakrimāṇam /
"kvacitprakaraṇasyāntaḥ smṛtaṃ prakaraṇāntaram" kasmiṃmaścit kavikauśalonmeṣaśālini nāṭake, na sarvatra /
ekasya madhyavartyaṅkāntaragarbhokṛtaṃ garbho vā nāmeti yāvat /
kiṃviśiṣṭaṃ "nirvartitanaṭāntaraṃ" = vibhāvitānyanartakaṃ /
naṭaiḥ kīdṛgbhiḥ "sāmājikajanāhlādanirmāṇanipuṇaiḥ"---sahṛdayapariṣatparitoṣapoṣaṇaniṣṇātaiḥ /
(kiṃ kṛtvā) "tadbhūmikāṃ samāsthāya" sāmājikībhūya /
idamatra tātparyam--kutracideva niraṅkuśakauśalāḥ kuśīlavāḥ svīyabhūmikāparigraheṇa raṅgamalaṅkurvāṇā nartakāntaraprayujyamāne prakṛtārthajīvita iva garbhavartinyaṅkāntare taraṅgitavakratāmahimni sāmājikībhavanto vividhābhirbhāvanābhaṅgībhiḥ sākṣātsāmājikānāṃ kimapi cittacamatkāravaicitryamāsūtrayanti /
yathā bālarāmāyaṇe caturthe 'ṅkelaṅkeśvarānukārī prahastānukāriṇā naṭo naṭenānuvartamānaḥ---
children.translated_text: 'Nourishes an obliqueness that is like the totality of the entire composition' — [it] causes to shine forth an oblique quality that is in the form of the life-force of the entire drama. 'Somewhere within the episode, another episode is remembered' — in some play that flashes with the bloom of the poet's skill, not everywhere. [An episode] embedded within the interior of one [act] — what is contained within an act-within-an-act, namely a <s>garbha</s> (sub-plot). How qualified? — 'performing a play-within-a-play' — [in which] another set of actors is brought forth. By actors of what kind? — 'skilled in producing delight in the audience' — expert in nourishing the satisfaction of the assembly of the sensitive. Doing what? — 'having assumed that role' — having become spectators [within the drama]. The purport here is: somewhere, actors of unchecked skill, adorning the stage through the assumption of their own roles, when a different set of performers enacts [a play within the play], in a <s>garbha</s>-act whose grandeur of obliqueness is made to ripple — [those actors], becoming spectators [themselves], through various turns of emotional realization, produce some marvelous variety of wonder in the hearts of the actual spectators. For example, in the fourth act of the <s>Bālarāmāyaṇa</s>, [the actor] imitating the Lord of <s>Laṅkā</s> [<s>Rāvaṇa</s>], accompanied by [the actor] imitating <s>Prahasta</s>, the actor being followed by the [other] actor —

children.text: karpūra iva dagdho 'pi śaktimān yo jane jane /
children.translated_text: Like camphor, even when burnt, powerful in every person —
salutation to that seed of <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic sentiment), to that one whose weapon is flowers [<s>Kāmadeva</s>]! // VjivC_4.44 //

children.text:
ityādinā naṭāntarābhinīyamāna (vividhabhāvanāḥ bhaṅgītaraṅgitavakratāgarimaṇi garbhāṅke sāmājikībhūya (sītā) sakhībhirvibhāvanavikriyābhirabhinīyamāno manorathātiriktamānandamutpādayati sahṛdayānām /
tatsūktisarvasvaṃ ca svayamevotprekṣya vyākhyeyam /
prabandhāntaḥ prakaraṇavakratāpyasya prakaraṇasya tatraiva---
children.translated_text: — and so on; the various emotional realizations enacted by the other set of actors, [while the main characters,] in the <s>garbha</s>-act whose grandeur of obliqueness ripples [through it], having become spectators — [specifically] <s>Sītā</s>, [together] with her companions, through the emotional transformations being enacted — produces in the sensitive a delight that exceeds [mere] imagination. And the essence of that poetic expression should be imagined and expounded by oneself. The intra-composition episode-obliqueness of this episode is [also found] right there —
To be drunk with many ears, to be seen with many long eyes —
the drama '<s>Sītāsvayaṃvaraṇa</s>' (The Self-Choice of <s>Sītā</s>) was composed as if for your sake alone! // VjivC_4.45 //

children.text:
ityanena prakāśyate /
yathā vā uttararāmacarite saptame 'ṅke rāmabhadrā (nukārī) lakṣmaṇāsahakāriṇā nartako nartakenopāsyamānaḥ
children.translated_text: is made manifest by this. Or as in the <s>Uttararāmacarita</s>, in the seventh act, when <s>Rāmabhadra</s>'s imitator [in the drama-within-the-drama], attended by a dancer who impersonates <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> as his assistant —

children.text: "(nepathye) ajjautta, hā kumāra ukkhaṇa, eāiṇiṃ asaraṇaṃ araṇṇe āsaṇṇapasavaveaṇaṃ hadāsaṃ sāvadā maṃ ahilasanti /
children.translated_text: '(Backstage:) O noble husband! Alas, Prince <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>! Alone, without refuge in the forest, the pangs of impending childbirth — helpless, the wild beasts assail me!' (Prākrit)

children.text: sāhaṃ dāṇiṃ mandabhāiṇī bhārirarie attāṇaṃ ṇikkhivissāmi" // VjivC_4.46 //
children.translated_text: 'So I, the ill-fated one, shall now cast myself into the <s>Bhāgīrathī</s> (Ganges)!' (Prākrit) // <s>Vjīv</s>C 4.46 //

children.text:
(hā aryaputra, hā kumāralakṣmaṇ, ekākinīṃ mandabhāginīmaśaraṇāmaraṇye āsannaprasavavedanāṃ hatāśāṃśvāpadā māmabhilaṣanti /
sāhamidānīṃ mandabhāginī bhāgīrathyāmātmānaṃ nikṣipāmi) /
ityādinā naṭāntaretyādi pūrvavat /
aparamapi prakaraṇavakratāyāḥ prakāramāviṣkaroti---
children.translated_text: ('O noble husband! Alas, Prince <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>! Alone, ill-fated, without refuge in the forest, the pangs of impending childbirth [upon me] — helpless, the wild beasts assail me! So I, the ill-fated one, shall now cast myself into the <s>Bhāgīrathī</s>.') By this and what follows, 'by another actor' and so on — as before. [The author] reveals yet another type of section-obliqueness —
Delightful through the junctures and their conjunctions,
beautified by the arrangement — the placement of sections // <s>Vjīv</s> 4.14 //
— not marred by passages and sections seized by the wrong path —
causes a new beauty of the delineation of obliqueness to shine forth. // <s>Vjīv</s> 4.15 //

children.text:
"vakratollekhalāvaṇyamullāsayati nūtanam" = vakratonmeṣakāmanīyakamunmīlayatyabhinavam /
"aḍgānāṃ viniveśanam"---prakaraṇānāṃ viśeṣeṇa nyāsaḥ /
kasmāt---"pūrvottarādisāṃgatyāt"---pūrvasya pūrvasyottarottareṇa yatsāṃgatyamatiśayitasaṃbandhatvamupajīvyopajīvakabhāvalakṣaṇaṃ tasmāt /
kiṃbhūtaṃ "mukhābhisandhisaṃhlādi" = mukhāni ca tāni abhisandhīni, taiḥ saṃhlādi sundaraṃ hṛdayahāri /
(punaḥ kīdṛśaṃ)"saṃvidhānakabandhuram" = prastutasaṃvidhānaramaṇīyam /
idamuktaṃ bhavati---prabandheṣu pūrvaṃ pūrvaṃ prakaraṇaṃ parasya parasya prakaraṇāntarasya sarasasaṃpāditasandhisaṃbandhasaṃvidhānakasamarpyamāṇa(kāmanīyaka)tāprāṇaprauḍhiprarūḍhavakratollekhamāhlādayati /
yathā puṣpadūṣitake prathamaṃ prakaraṇam--atidāruṇābhinavavipravāsavedanānirānandasya nandayantīmasaṃmānya samāgatasya samudratīre samudradattasyotkaṇṭhāprakāraprakāśanam /
dvitīyamapi--prasthānāt pratinivṛtya niśīthinyāmutkocālaṅkāradānamūkīkṛtakuvalayasya kusumavāṭikāyāmanākalitānanasya sahacarīsaṃgamanam /
tṛtīyamapi---saṃbhāvitadurvinyavijayadattanandinīnirvāsanavyasanani bandhanam /
caturthamapi--mathurāpratinivṛttakuvalayapradarśyamānāṅgulīyakasamāveditavimalaśīlasaṃpadaḥ kaṭhorataragarbhabhārakhinnāyāḥ snuṣāyā niṣkāraṇaniṣkāsanādanāsāditatatpravṛttermahāpātakinamātmānaṃ manyamānasya sārthavāhasāgaradattasya tīrthayātrāpravartanam /
pañcamamapi---vanāntare vanapālapālitāyā nandayantyāḥ kuvalayena samudradattakuśalodantakathanam /
ṣaṣṭhamapi---vicitrasaraṇyā samāgamābhyupāyasaṃpādanamiti /
evameteṣāmanantopāyānāṃ kathārasaniṣyandatatparāṇāṃ paripāṭiḥ kāmapi kāmanīyakasaṃpadamudbhāvayati /
yathā vā kumārasaṃbhave--- pārvatyāḥ prathamatāruṇyāvatāravarṇanam, śaṅkaraśuśrūṣā, dustaratārakaparābhavapārāvārottārakāraṇamaravindasūterupadeśaḥ, kusumākarasuhṛdaḥ kandarpasya purandaroddeśāt gauryāḥ saundaryabalādvipraharato haravilocanavicitrabhānunā bhasmīkaraṇaṃ, duḥkhāveśavivaśāyā ratyā vilāpanam, vikṣatavikalamanaso menātmajāyāstapaścaraṇam, ādṛtavṛddhā (cārayā saha) manasijaviṣūdanasaṃvādanirūpaṇaṃ, citraśikhaṇḍibhiḥ śikharināthābhyarthanam, nirargalānurāgaprāgbhāraparimṛṣṭacetasā (parameśvareṇa) pāṇipīḍanam, iti prakaraṇāni paurvāparyaparyavasitasundarasamāveśasaṃbandhabandhurāṇi rāmaṇīyakadhāramadhirohanti /
evamanyeṣvapi mahākaviprabandheṣu prakaraṇavaicitryamevameva vivecanīyam /
asyaiva prādhānyamabhidhātuṃ vyatirekamāha--- "na tvamārgagrahagrastavarṇakāṅgaiḥ kadarthitam"---na tvaṅgānāṃ viniveśanaṃ vakratollāsabhāgbhavati /
children.translated_text: To state the predominance of this [quality], [the author] states the contrast — 'Not marred by passages and sections seized by the wrong path' — that is, the placement of sections does not partake of the flowering of obliqueness [when marred thus].
Of what kind [is it then]? — Marred by passages seized by the wrong path.

children.text: uttarottaraparasparānvayalakṣaṇasaṃbandhanibandhanam etadvākyārthatātparyamiti vākyavicāralakṣaṇasyopayogaḥ, pramāṇena pratyakṣādinaitat, upapannamiti pramāṇalakṣaṇasyopayogaḥ /
children.translated_text: The connection of each successive [section] with each prior, characterized by mutual syntactical relation — this is the purport of the sentence-meaning, and therein lies the utility of the criterion of sentence-analysis; that this is established — therein lies the utility of the criterion of valid means of knowledge, such as direct perception and the like.
