children.text: yuktiyuktatvaṃ nāma grathanāveśakalitaṃ bharatādilakṣaṇayojanāvilambitaṃ, saṃdhyaṅgaprabhṛtipratipādanāya kathānupayuktairvarṇakairākīrṇam //
children.translated_text: The quality of being well-reasoned consists in being set within the structure of dramatic composition, sustained by the application of the definitions of <s>Bharata</s> and the rest, and [being free from being] filled with passages — employed for the purpose of establishing juncture-elements and so forth — that are not useful to the narrative.

'Causes a new beauty of the delineation of obliqueness to shine forth' means: it unfolds a fresh charm of the flowering of obliqueness. 'The placement of sections' — the particular arrangement of the episodes. Why? — 'Through the conjunction of the prior and the subsequent' — through the relationship of the prior with each successive [section], characterized by the relation of the dependent and the supporting, which constitutes an intensified connection. Of what kind? — 'Delightful through the junctures and their conjunctions' — the junctures (<s>mukhas</s>) and the conjunctions (<s>abhisandhis</s>); delightful, beautiful, captivating to the heart through those. And again of what kind? — 'Beautified by the arrangement' — beautiful through the arrangement of the subject at hand. What has been said is this: in literary works, the prior section, by the beauty of being presented through a juicy, well-fashioned conjunction and juncture-relation with each subsequent section, bestowing the life-breath of charm through the maturity of sprouting obliqueness, produces delight. For example, in the <s>Puṣpadūṣitaka</s>: the first section — the disclosure of the mode of longing of <s>Samudradatta</s>, who has arrived at the seashore, failing to receive <s>Nandayantī</s>, joyless from the exceedingly cruel pain of fresh separation. The second also — after setting out, returning at midnight, when the <s>kuvalaya</s> (blue lotus) has been silenced by the gift of the ornament of withdrawal, the meeting with the companion in the flower-garden, his face unrecognized. The third also — the narrative-bond of the banishment-obsession of the daughter of <s>Jayadatta</s> named <s>Nandinī</s>, whose misconduct was surmised. The fourth also — the departure on pilgrimage of the caravan-leader <s>Sāgaradatta</s>, who, seeing the ring shown by <s>Kuvalaya</s> upon his return from <s>Mathurā</s>, which reveals the wealth of spotless character [of his daughter-in-law], considers himself a great sinner for having caused the groundless expulsion of his daughter-in-law, who was weary with the heavy burden of advanced pregnancy. The fifth also — in the forest, the narration of the news of <s>Samudradatta</s>'s welfare by <s>Kuvalaya</s> to <s>Nandayantī</s>, who has been protected by the forest-guard. The sixth also — the procurement of the means for the meeting through varied expedients. Thus the sequence of these [sections] — devoted to the flow of the juice of the narrative, with inexhaustible devices — brings to light a certain wealth of beauty. Or as in the <s>Kumārasaṃbhava</s>: the description of <s>Pārvatī</s>'s first descent of youthful beauty; her service to <s>Śaṅkara</s> (<s>Śiva</s>); the instruction of the Lotus-born (<s>Brahmā</s>) regarding the difficult-to-cross defeat of <s>Tāraka</s> as the higher cause; the incineration of <s>Kandarpa</s> (the Love-god), the friend of Spring, who attacked <s>Hara</s> (<s>Śiva</s>) by the force of <s>Gaurī</s>'s beauty on behalf of <s>Purandara</s> (<s>Indra</s>), by the varied fire of <s>Hara</s>'s eye; the lamentation of <s>Rati</s>, overwhelmed by the force of grief; the ascetic practice of <s>Menā</s>'s daughter, whose mind is wounded and distressed; the narration of the conversation with the destroyer of the Love-god, in the company of venerable elderly [women]; the entreaty of the Lord of the Mountains by the peacock-crested (<s>Citraśikhaṇḍin</s>) ones; the marriage by the hand of the Supreme Lord, whose consciousness is wiped clean by the forward weight of unrestrained love — thus the sections, beautiful through the well-established, concluding connection of lovely interweaving, ascend the stream of beauty. Similarly, in other works of great poets, the variety of sections should be examined in the same way.

children.text:
yathā veṇīsaṃhāre pratimukhasandhyaṅgabhāgini dvitīye 'ṅke bhānumatyāḥ svapnavṛttāntaśravaṇasamutpannadurvinayabuddherduryodhanasya vividhavipakṣavailakṣye tādṛśi samarasaṃmarde samudvṛtte, śaraśayyāśāyini mandākinīnandane, nihanyamāneṣu ca kumārasodarasaṃbandhisuhṛtsu, tathāvidhavīravṛtterabhimānino 'spandamavasthitirapyanucitā kiṃ punarvilāsavyāpṛtiḥ, tatrāpi veśyāyāmiva vilāsaḥ mahārājasya mahiṣyāṃ, (vi) cāramantareṇa taducitacittaparicitiṃ vinā ca durvinayādhyāsaḥ sakalamidamasamañjasatābhājanamupekṣyameva /
yathā śiśupālavadhe--- upendrasyendraprasthaṃ prati pratiṣṭhamānasya dvāravatīvyāvarṇanam /
children.translated_text: For example, in the <s>Veṇīsaṃhāra</s>, in the second act, which partakes of the counter-design (<s>pratimukha</s>) juncture-element — when <s>Duryodhana</s>, upon hearing of <s>Bhānumatī</s>'s dream-narrative, develops an intelligence of insolence, and in such a diverse perplexity of the opposing side, when such a confluence of battle has arisen, when the joy of <s>Mandākinī</s> (<s>Bhīṣma</s>) lies on a bed of arrows, and when the kinsmen, relatives, and friends of the prince are being slaughtered — for one who takes pride in such heroic conduct, even standing motionless is unfitting, how much more so the engagement in amorous play; and moreover, that coquetry directed at the queen of the great king as if she were a courtesan — without deliberation, without cultivating the mindset appropriate to that [situation] — the superimposition of insolence, all this, being the object of impropriety, should simply be disregarded. As in the <s>Śiśupālavadha</s> — the description of <s>Dvāravatī</s> by <s>Upendra</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) as he sets out toward <s>Indraprastha</s>.
By other sections of the poet, charming through propriety of expression,

children.text: ratnairalaṅkāra iva prabandhaḥ puṣyati śriyam // VjivC_4.47 //
children.translated_text: a work flourishes in beauty, like [a body adorned] with ornaments of jewels. // <s>Vjīv</s>C 4.47 //
Its own sub-section — animated solely by the body of the narrative with its charming play of varied turns —
they know as the <s>rasāyana</s> (elixir) of <s>rasa</s> itself. // <s>Vjīv</s>C 4.48 //

children.text: (ityantaraślokau) evamanekaprakārāṃ prakaraṇavakratāṃ pratipādya samudāyātmakasya prabandhasya tāmabhidadhāti---
children.translated_text: (Interpolated verses.) Having thus expounded section-obliqueness in its many forms, [the author] now describes the [obliqueness] of the aggregate-natured work —
Where the conclusion is achieved by disregarding the wealth of <s>rasa</s> [as found in] the different course of events in the source narrative,

children.text: rasāntareṇa ramyeṇa yatra nirvahaṇaṃ bhavet // Vjiv_4.16 //
children.translated_text: and through another, beautiful <s>rasa</s> — // <s>Vjīv</s> 4.16 //
of that very body of the narrative, whose beauty has unfolded from the root up,
for the production of the delight of the audience — that is the obliqueness of the work. // <s>Vjīv</s> 4.17 //

children.text:
"sā" "prabandhasya"---nāṭakasargabandhādeḥ "vakratā"---vakrabhāvo bhavatīti saṃbandhaḥ /
"yatra nirvahaṇaṃ bhavet" = yasyāmupasaṃharaṇaṃ syāt /
"rasāntareṇa ramyeṇa" itareṇa rasena rāmaṇīyaka (tva) vidhāyinā /
kayā "itivṛttānyathāvṛttarasasaṃpadupekṣayā"---"itivṛtte" itihāse 'nyathā---apareṇaprakāreṇa "vṛttā" nirvyūḍhā yā "rasasaṃpat" śṛṅgārādibhaṅgī "tadupekṣayā"---tadanādareṇa tāṃ parityajyeti yāvat /
kasyāḥ "tasyā eva kathāmūrteḥ" tasyaiva kāvyaśarīrasya /
kiṃbhūtāyāḥ---"āmūlonmīlitaśriyaḥ"---"āmūlaṃ" prārambhāt unmīlitā śrīḥ = vācyavācakaracanāvaicitryasaṃpat yasyāḥ sā tathoktā tasyāḥ /
kimarthaṃ "vineyānandaniṣpattyai" = pratibodhyapārthivādipramodasaṃpādanāya /
anenedamabhihitaṃ bhavati--itivṛttāntarvṛttāyāḥ kasyāścidekasyāḥ kathāyāḥ kavistannibandhanirvahaṇagatarasapaddhatiṃ parityajyābhijātānāmāhlādakāriṇā kāmanīyakena kenāpyanyena rasenopasaṃharaṇamupapādayan prabandhe kamapi vakrimāṇamādadhāti /
yathā veṇīsaṃhāre-- sa hi kāmāntarakavalitasakalabhāvabhāvanāvāritaniḥsārasaṃsāravāsanāmahimani mahābhārate śāntarasavināsinā nibandhani r(vahaṇa)paddhatau pāṇḍavakathāyāstathāvidhādbhutābhogaśobhinā vīreṇa raṇaprāṅgaṇanihatākhilārāticakradhārādhiṣṭhitarājadharmadharmarājābhyudayasaṃpāditāṃ samāptamupapādayan prabandhaprarūḍhaprauḍhavakratāvicchittyācchinnamabhijātānāmāhlādamāvahati /
te hi tathāvidhavyasanakṣetrībhūtairapi punaḥ svapakṣopabṛṃhitaparākramaparājitaparipanthibhirbhujyata eṣā rājyaśrīriti akhidyamānā vipatsvapi vipulotsāhabhājo bhavantī /
yathā vottararāmacaritam--rāmāyaṇe 'pyaṅginā karuṇena dāruṇavirahavedanābhājanajanakarājaputrīpātālapraveśāt, prabāhodara (patitasya) sodarasahitasya raghupaternibandhanirvahaṇaviparyastakathāyāḥ sakaladivyāstrakuśalalavabaladarśanotsavāntaropabṛṃhitatvena videhanandinīsaṃbhogaśṛṅgāraḥ upasaṃharaṇamātre vicchittiviśeṣapoṣaṇa (padavīṃ) bhajan abhijātānāmabhinandanīyo bhavati /
evamanyadapi svayamūhyam /
children.translated_text: 'That' — 'of the work' — of a drama, <s>sarga</s>-composition, and so forth — 'obliqueness' — the oblique character — this is the syntactical connection. 'Where the conclusion is achieved' — where the winding-up would occur. 'Through another, beautiful <s>rasa</s>' — through another <s>rasa</s>, one that produces beauty. By what? — 'By disregarding the wealth of <s>rasa</s> differently realized in the source narrative' — in the 'source narrative' (<s>itihāsa</s>), [that which has been] 'differently' — in another manner — 'realized,' the 'wealth of <s>rasa</s>' — the particular <s>śṛṅgāra</s> and other [sentiments]; 'by disregarding that' — by neglecting it, by setting it aside. Of what? — 'Of that very body of the narrative' — of that very body of the literary work. Of what kind? — 'Whose beauty has unfolded from the root up' — from the beginning, the beauty — the wealth of the variety of expressed and expressor composition — has unfolded; of that [narrative body]. For what purpose? — 'For the production of the delight of the audience' — for the accomplishment of the pleasure of the kings and others who are to be instructed. What has been said is this: the poet, setting aside the path of <s>rasa</s> involved in the conclusion of the composition of a particular narrative that is contained within the source, and effecting the conclusion through another <s>rasa</s> that delights the noble-minded with some beauty, establishes a certain obliquity in the work. For example, in the <s>Veṇīsaṃhāra</s>: for in the <s>Mahābhārata</s>, where the greatness of the impressions of freedom from the worthless essence of <s>saṃsāra</s> has been overwhelmed by the nurturing of all sentiments swallowed by some other desire, and where the <s>śānta</s> (quiescent) <s>rasa</s> pervades the conclusion — [the poet], in the course of the <s>Pāṇḍava</s> narrative, effecting the conclusion with the <s>vīra</s> (heroic) <s>rasa</s>, resplendent with the beauty of wondrous delight — with the kingdom-dharma of the dharma-king (<s>Dharmarāja</s> / <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>) established [through] the complete destruction of the entire enemy-host on the battlefield — effecting the conclusion, [the poet], having cut through with the charm of the mature obliqueness sprouted in the work, brings delight to the noble-minded. For they, even though made the field of such calamities, again — with their own side reinforced, their valor having defeated all adversaries — this royal glory is enjoyed by them — [thus they are shown as] not broken, even in misfortunes displaying vast enthusiasm. Or as the <s>Uttararāmacarita</s>: in the <s>Rāmāyaṇa</s> too, with the principal <s>karuṇa</s> (pathetic) [rasa] — from the descent of the daughter of King <s>Janaka</s> into the netherworld due to the cruel pain of separation, and from the falling of <s>Raghu</s>'s descendant together with his younger brother into the breast of [the river] — the narrative of the conclusion having been reversed, through the festival of seeing <s>Lava</s> and <s>Bala</s> (<s>Kuśa</s>), who are skilled in all divine weapons — with that reinforcement — the <s>saṃbhogaśṛṅgāra</s> (union-erotic <s>rasa</s>) with the daughter of <s>Videha</s> at the very point of conclusion, partaking of the nurturing of a particular charm, becomes praiseworthy for the noble-minded. Similarly, other [cases] too should be inferred by oneself.
That work which brings about the prosperity of the hero, whose calamities have been destroyed,
is born for the binding of the affection of those who are to be instructed. // <s>Vjīv</s>C 4.49 //

children.text:
(ityantaraślokaḥ) rāmāyaṇamahābhāratayośca karuṇaśāntāṅgitvaṃ pūrvasūribhireva nirūpitam /
asyāḥ prakārāntaramapyavatārayatiḥ---
children.translated_text: (Interpolated verse.) The subsidiary status of <s>karuṇa</s> and <s>śānta</s> [rasas] in the <s>Rāmāyaṇa</s> and the <s>Mahābhārata</s> has been determined by the earlier masters themselves. [The author] introduces yet another type of this [work-obliqueness] —
With a portion of the source narrative that nourishes the excellence of the hero through unprecedented delineation of the three worlds,
the completion of the work — // <s>Vjīv</s> 4.18 //
out of a desire to avoid the tastelessness of the narrative that follows thereafter —

children.text: kurvota yatra sukaviḥ sā vicitrāsya vakratā // Vjiv_4.19 //
children.translated_text: where a good poet accomplishes [this] — that is the varied obliqueness of the work. // <s>Vjīv</s> 4.19 //

children.text:
"sā vicitrā"---vividhabhaṅgībhrājiṣṇuḥ /
"asya"---prabandhasya /
"vakratā"---vakrabhāvo bhavatīti saṃbandhaḥ /
"kurvota yatra sukaviḥ" "kurvota"---vidadhīta /
"yatra"---yasyāṃ /
"sukaviḥ"---aucityapaddhati-prabhāvacaturaḥ /
"prabandhasya samāpanam" ("prabandhasya")sargabandhādeḥ, "samāpanam"--upasaṃharaṇaṃ samarthanamiti yāvat /
"itihāsaikadeśena" itivṛttasyāvayavena /
kiṃbhūtena "trailokyābhinavollekhanāyakotkarṣapoṣiṇā" jagadasādhāraṇasphuritanetṛprakarṣaprakāśakena /
kimarthaṃ---taduttarakathāvartivirasatvajihīrṣayā--tasmāduttarā yā kathā tadvṛtti tadantargataṃ yadvirasatvaṃ vairasyamanārjavaṃ, tasya "jihāsayā" parijihīrṣayā /
idamuktaṃ bhavatiḥ---itihāsodāhṛtāṃ kāñcana mahākaviḥ sakalāṃ kathāṃ prārabhyāpi, tadavayavena trailokyacamatkārakāraṇanirupamānanāyakayaśaḥ samutkarṣodayadāyinā tadagrimagranthaprasaṅgataḥ saṃbhāvitavirasabhāvabhayāt upasaṃhāramāṇaḥ tasya prabandhasya kāmanīyakaniketanāyamānaṃ vakrimāṇamādadhāti /
yathā kirātārjunīye---
children.translated_text: 'That is the varied' — resplendent with manifold turns. 'Of this' — of the work. 'Obliqueness' — the oblique character — this is the syntactical connection. 'Where a good poet accomplishes' — 'accomplishes' means: would fashion. 'Where' — in which. 'A good poet' — one skilled in the way of propriety. 'The completion of the work' — of a <s>sarga</s>-composition and so forth, 'completion' means: conclusion, accomplishment. 'With a portion of the source narrative' — with a part of the historical account. Of what kind? — 'That nourishes the excellence of the hero through unprecedented delineation of the three worlds' — that which illuminates the extraordinary eminence of the protagonist, shining forth uniquely in the world. For what purpose? — 'Out of a desire to avoid the tastelessness of the narrative that follows thereafter' — of the narrative that comes after that, the tastelessness, the lack of savour, the absence of straightforwardness, [and the wish] to avoid that. What has been said is this: a great poet, even having begun an entire narrative drawn from the source, by concluding with that portion of the source which bestows the arising of the incomparable glory of the hero — a cause of wonder to the three worlds — out of fear of the anticipated tastelessness arising from the succeeding portion of the text, and thereby concluding the work, establishes an obliqueness that becomes the abode of beauty for that work. For example, in the <s>Kirātārjunīya</s> —

children.text: sa hi sargabandhaḥ dviṣāṃ vighātāya vidhātumicchato rahasyanujñāmadhigamya bhūbhṛtaḥ // VjivC_4.50 //
children.translated_text: For that canto-composition [opens with]: 'Having obtained the secret command of the king who wishes to devise the destruction of enemies...' // VjivC_4.50 //

children.text: ... riputimiramudasyodīyamānaṃ dinādau dinakṛtamiva lakṣmīstvāṃ samabhyetu bhūyaḥ // VjivC_4.51 //
children.translated_text: '...may <s>Lakṣmī</s> (prosperity), like the sun dispelling the darkness of enemies, rising at the beginning of day, come to you again.' // VjivC_4.51 //

children.text: ete durāpaṃ samavāpya vīryamunmūlitāraḥ kapiketanena // VjivC_4.52 //
children.translated_text: 'These [warriors], having attained power difficult to obtain, their enemies uprooted by the monkey-bannered one [<s>Arjuna</s>]...' // VjivC_4.52 //

children.text:
ityādinā duryodhananidhanāntāṃ dharmarājābhyudayadāyinīṃ sakalāmapi kathāmupakramya kavinā nibadhyamānatvāt tejasvivṛndārakasya durodaradvārā dūrīkṛtavibhūteḥ prabhūtadrupadātmajānikāraniratiśayoddīpitamanyoḥ kṛṣṇadvaipāyanopadiṣṭavidyāyogasaṃpadaḥ pāśupatādidivyāstraprāptaye tapasyato gāṇḍīvasuhṛdaḥ pāṇḍunandanasyāntarā kirātarājasaṃpraharaṇāt samunmīlitānupamavikramollekhaṃ kamapyabhiprāyaṃ prakāśayati /
tathāhi--- yatprathamam---prāptapāśupataprabhṛtiparamāstrasaṃbhāreṇāpyekākinā (pārthena) pinākinā (saha) mahāhavaḥ, yasmin bhujayorādāyāndolyamāno viyati viṣamalocano 'pi vismayāveśavikalatāṃ vilakṣatāṃ cālabdhapūrvāṃ lambhitaḥ /
tasya pratyakṣīkṛtatryakṣasya tatprasādāsāditadivyāstrasaṃpado vyāpadāpātarakṣaṇavicakṣaṇacakradharasārathestathāvidharathottamamāsth itasya sthiratarasamarasaṃrambhabhīmasenādyupetānīkinīparaṃparāparivāritasya puruskṛtaśikhaṇḍinaḥ parāṅmukhe varṣoyasyapi pitāmahe, mahādayāloḥ"arjunasya ime bāṇāḥ neme bāṇāḥ syapi pitāmahe, mahādayāloḥ "arjunasya hame bāṇāḥ neme bāṇāḥ śikhaṇḍinaḥ" ityādinārṣeṇa vacasā sūcitam śvapacādapi (nṛśaṃsavṛttācāraṇam) /
auctiyapradhānapaddhatipravardhamānavīrarasaparivṛḍhaprabandhanibadhyamānamayaśasyamevānyathā vyāpṛtasya pṛthivīpateḥ bhūriśravaso 'pyadhīravartmanā bhujadaṇḍocchedanam /
tadvanmedinīnimagnasyandanābhyuddharaṇavyāpṛtasya vyāhṛtavirodhitāhavapaddhaterapyaṅgabharturuttamāṅgakartanam /
evamanyadapyūhyam /
children.translated_text: By such passages, since the poet, having commenced the entire narrative — from [the beginning] up to the death of <s>Duryodhana</s> — which bestows the prosperity of <s>Dharmarāja</s>, is composing it, the assembly of the valiant...
With his activity of fashioning works that surge with overflowing <s>rasa</s>,
the hero, by removing obstacles, nourishes beauty. // VjivC_4.53 //
This is an interpolated verse. He further considers another sub-type within this [obliquity]:
Through an intervening obstacle of another purpose, which produces the concealment of the connection with the principal subject,
the narrative, [seemingly] interrupted and rendered tasteless, // Vjiv_4.20 //
by the very accomplishment of that [obstacle's resolution] within it, binds upon the composition
a new, unprecedented obliquity, radiant with <s>rasa</s> that is free from [artificial] contrivance. // Vjiv_4.21 //

children.text:
"prabandhasya"---sargabandhādeḥ, "anubadhnāti"---draḍhayati /
"navām"---apūrvollekhāṃ, "kāmapi" sahṛdayānubhūyamānāṃ na punarabhidhāgocaracamatkārāṃ, "vakratāṃ"---vakrimāṇaṃ /
kāsau "kāryāntarāntarāyeṇa vicchinnavirasā kathā" "kāryāntarāntarāyeṇa"---anyakāryakṛtena ādhikārikakathāpratyūhena "vicchinnavirasā" vicchinnā cāsau virasā ca sā, vicchidyamāna (rasa) tvāt anāvarjanasaṃjñetyarthaḥ /
kimabhūtena "pradhānavastusaṃbandha(tirodhāna) vidhāyinā"---ādhikārikaphalasiddhayupāyanirodhinā /
kutaḥ "tatraiva tasya niṣpatteḥ" "natraiva" kāryāntarānuṣṭhāne "tasyā" dhikārikasya "niṣpatteḥ"---saṃsiddheḥ /
tata eva "nirnibandharasojjvalām"---nirantarāyataraṅgitāṅgirasaprāgbhārabhrājiṣṇum /
ayamasya paramārthaḥ---yā kilādhikārikakathāniṣedhikāryāntaravyavadhānāt jhagiti vighaṭamānālabdhāvakāśāpi vikāśyamānā sā prastutetaravyāpārādeva prastutavastuniṣpannendīvarasitarasanirbharā prabandhasya rāmaṇīyakavakrimāṇamādadhāti /
yathā śiśupālavadhe /
sa hi sargabandhaḥ /
trailokyarakṣādhikāravyāpṛtabāhunā vāsudevena devarṣimukhāt
children.translated_text: 'Of the composition' — of the canto-composition and the like; 'binds' — makes firm. 'New' — of unprecedented depiction; 'a certain' — experienced by the connoisseurs, not...
'That word of <s>Upendra</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>), commissioned by <s>Indra</s>, which is cherished by all people — let me speak it for a moment.' // VjivC_4.54 //
By such [verses], the message of <s>Purandara</s> (<s>Indra</s>)...
'Of <s>Śārṅgin</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>), who said "<s>oṃ</s>"...' // VjivC_4.55 //

children.text:
ityādinā tatkālakandalitakrodhānubhāvabhaṅgyā niśamyāṅgīkṛtamādhikārikaṃ māhiṣmatīnāthamanādṛtya, iṃndraprasthaṃ prati pratiṣṭhāsyamānena nimagnanikhilavīrasthitirviṣayatāmanīyata /
tatastasminneva saṃśritasakalarājake dharmarājasya rājasūyamaṇḍape madhuripora (grapūjāsaṃ) mānamasahamānenātiduḥsahavākyapāruṣyāvarodhaparaṃparāviracanacatureṇa cedirājena "kṛtārthokṛta" ityantena ca /
prabandhavakratāmeva prikārāntareṇa vyācaṣṭe---
children.translated_text: By such [passages], having heard [the message] through the turn of the <s>anubhāva</s> (consequent) of the anger budding at that moment, and having accepted the mandate — disregarding the lord of <s>Māhiṣmatī</s>, proceeding toward <s>Indraprastha</s>...
Where the hero, even when engaged in the attainment of a single goal,
in countless other goals — of equal realization with that [primary one] — // Vjiv_4.22 //
serves as the occasion, the vessel of an expansive collection of glory,
that too, from the wonder of his own greatness, is another obliquity of his. // Vjiv_4.23 //

children.text:
"sā parāpi"--anyāpi na kevalaṃ prāguktā, "asya" rūpakādeḥ, "vakratā"---vakrabhāvo bhavatīti saṃbandhaḥ /
"yatraikaphalasaṃpattisamudyukto 'pi nāyakaḥ", "yatra"---yasyāṃ, "ekaphalasaṃpattisamudyukto 'pi"--parābhimatavastusādhanavyavasito 'pi nāyakaḥ, "phalāntareṣvananteṣu" "phalāntareṣu"---sādhyarūpeṣu vastuṣu, "ananteṣu"---gaṇanātīteṣu /
"tattulyapratipattiṣu dhatte nimittatām" "tattulyapratipattiṣu"---ādhikārikaphalasamānopapattiṣu, prastutārthasiddherevādhigatasiddhiṣvati (yāvat) /
kiṃbhūtaḥ "spharāyaśaḥsaṃbhārabhājanam" "sphārasya" brahmāṇḍodarabharitvādatiriktasya, "yaśasaḥ"---kīrteḥ yaḥ "saṃbhāraḥ"---samudayaḥ, tasya "bhājanaṃ" pātraṃ bhūmiriti yāvat /
kuto hetoḥ "svamāhātmyacamatkārāt" "svamāhātmyaṃ" svasya prabhāvaḥ, tasya "camatkāraḥ" āścaryakāritvaṃ, tasmāt /
etaduktaṃ bhavati--niḥsīmamanorathamalaṅkariṣṇunaikenāṃśakena phalena saṃyuto 'pyaparimitāni tādṛśasvarūpāṇi phalānyagamyānyadhyavasāyādanicchannapi svaprabhāvasaṃpadā saṃpādayannāyakaḥ kamapi kāmanīyakanidhānakalaśaṃ prabandhasya vakrimāṇamāvahati /
yathā nāgānande tatra durnivāravairādapi vainateyāntakāde (kākinam) sakalakāruṇikacūcamaṇiḥ śaṅkhacūḍaṃ jīmūtavāhano nijadehadānādabhirakṣanna (kevalaṃ taṃ) rakṣitavān apitu sakalaṃ tatkulameva---
children.translated_text: 'That too is another' — another, not merely the previously stated; 'of his' — of <s>rūpaka</s> and the like; 'obliquity' — the oblique character exists — this is the syntactic connection. 'Where [the hero is engaged in] a single goal'...

children.text: āstāṃ vastuṣu vaidagdhī kāvye kāmapi vakratām /
children.translated_text: Let alone the skill in subject matter — the poet produces a certain obliquity in poetry
even by the designation of the names of the acts in the principal arrangement. // Vjiv_4.24 //

children.text:
"āstāṃ vastuṣu vaidagdhī" "āstām"---dūrata eva vartatām, "vastuṣu"---abhidheyeṣu prakaraṇapratipādyeṣu, "vaidagdhī"--vicchittiḥ, "kāvyaṃ kāmapi vakratāṃ kurute kaviḥ" ṭhakāvye'---nāṭake sargabandhādau ca, kāmapi vakratāṃ "kurute"---vidadhāti /
"kaviḥ'---adbhutapratibhāprasāraprakāśakaḥ /
kena---"pradhānasaṃvidhānāṅkanāmnāpi" "pradhānaṃ"--prabandhaprāṇaprāyaṃ, "yatsaṃvidhānaṃ'---kathāyojanaṃ, "nadaṅkaḥ" cihnamupalakṣaṇaṃ yasya yatra vā tattathoktaṃ, tacca tannāma ca, tenāpi /
apiśabdo vismayamuddyotayati /
idamasya rahasyam---vicāritavicitravastuvicchitteḥ prabandhasya vakratāvirbhavati (iti) kimadbhutam /
adbhutaṃ punaridaṃ yatsāratarasaṃvidhānakanibandhalakṣaṇā (yojitasara) sākṣareṇa nāmnāpi sā niveśyate /
yathā---abhijñānaśākuntala--mudrārākṣasa--pratimāniruddha---māyāpuṣpaka---kṛtyārāvaṇa--chalitarāma---puṣpadūṣitakādīni nāmāni /
evaṃvidhāni kāvyabandhānāṃ nāmadheyānyapi nirupamollekhāni (vilakṣaṇavakratāsarasā) kṣarāṇi niveditāntargataviśiṣṭasaṃbandhatayā nibadhnantyeva vakrimāṇam, na punarhayagrīvavadha--śiśupālavadha--pāṇḍavābhyudaya--rāmānanda--rāmacaritaprāyāṇi saralasvarūpāṇi /
children.translated_text: 'Let alone the skill in subject matter' — 'let alone' — let it be far away; 'in subject matter' — in the expressible contents, the things presented in the sections; 'skill' — design...
Even poetic compositions bound in a single class by master poets
nourish a priceless obliquity through their mutual distinctness. // Vjiv_4.25 //

children.text:
"puṣṇanti"--ullāsayanti, "anarghām"---aparicchedyām, "vakratāṃ"---vakrabhavam /
kena--"anyonyavailakṣaṇyena"---parasparavaisādṛśyena /
ke te "kāvyabandhāḥ"---rūpakapuraḥsarāḥ /
kiṃviśiṣṭāḥ---"apyekakakṣayā baddhāḥ"---ekenāpītivṛttena yojitāḥ /
kaiḥ---"kavīśvaraiḥ'---anyatra vistīrṇaṃ vastu saṃkṣipadbhiḥ saṃkṣiptaṃ vā vistārayadbhiḥ, vicitravācyavācakālaṅkaraṇasaṃkalanayā navatāṃ nayādbhirityarthaḥ /
idamatra tātparyam---ekāmeva kāmapi kandalitakāmanīyakāṃ kathāṃ nirvahadbhirbahubhirapi kavikuñjarairnibadhyamānā bahavaḥ prabandhā manāgapyanyonyasaṃvādamanāsādayantaḥ sahṛdayahṛdayāhlādakaṃ kamapi vakrimāṇamādadhati /
yathā ekasyāmeva dāśarathikathāyāṃ rāmābhyudaya---udāttarāghavavīracarita--bālarāmāyaṇa---kṛtyārāvaṇa--māyāpuṣpakaprabhṛtayaḥ /
te hi prabandhapravarāstenaiva kathāmārgeṇa nirargalarasāsāragarbhasandarbhasaṃpadā pratipadaṃ prativākyaṃ pratiprakaraṇaṃ ca prakāśamānābhinavabhaṅgīprāyāḥ bhrājiṣṇavo navonabonmīlitanāyakādbhutaguṇotkarṣākarṣāḥ harṣātirekamanekaśo 'pyāsvādyamānāḥ samutpādayanti sahṛdayānām /
evamanyadapi nidarśanāntaramudbhāvanīyam /
children.translated_text: 'Nourish' — cause to shine forth; 'priceless' — immeasurable; 'obliquity' — oblique character. By what? — 'Through mutual distinctness' — through the mutual...
Even when the commencement of the narrative is the same, compositions, like living beings with their own qualities — like bodies —

children.text: prabandhāḥ prāṇina iva prabhāsānte pṛthak pṛthak // VjivC_4.56 //
children.translated_text: shine forth separately, each on its own. // VjivC_4.56 //
This is an interpolated verse. He establishes yet another sub-type of this:
All the compositions of great poets possess obliquity,
[being] instructors of a new path accomplished through unprecedented means. // Vjiv_4.26 //

children.text:
"mahākaviprabandhanām"---navanirmāṇanipuṇanirupamakaviprakāṇḍa (viracitānāṃ) "sarveṣāṃ" /
(kiṃbhūtānāṃ)--"nūtanopāyaniṣapannanayavartmo padeśināṃ"---"nūtanāḥ"---pratyagrāḥ, "upāyāḥ"---sāmādiprayogaprakārāḥ tadvidāṃ gocarā ye "tairniṣpannaṃ' siddhaṃ yat "nayavartma" nīti (mārgaḥ) tadupadiśanti śikṣayanti ye (te) tathoktāsteṣām /
kimuktaṃ bhavati---sakaleṣvapi satkaviprabandhaṣu abhinavabhaṅgīniveśapeśalinyā nītyāḥ phalamupapadyamānaṃ pratipādyopadeśadvāreṇa kimapi camatkāraṇamupalabhyata eva /
yathā mudrārākṣase--- tatra hi pravaraprajñāprabhāvaprapañcitavicitranītivyāpārāḥ pragalbhanta eva /
yathā ca tāpasavatsarājoddeśa eva vyākhyātaḥ /
evamanyadapyutprekṣaṇīyam /
children.translated_text: 'Of the compositions of the great poets' — 'of all' those composed by the incomparable foremost masters of poetry, skilled in fresh creation. Of what kind? — 'of those that instruct in the path of statecraft accomplished by novel means' — 'novel' means fresh; 'means' are the modes of applying [the four expedients] <s>sāma</s> (conciliation) and the like, accessible to experts in that [field]; 'the path of statecraft accomplished by those' means the political course perfected through them; [these compositions] 'instruct,' i.e., teach — they are thus described. What is being said? — In all the compositions of good poets, through the statecraft that is rendered charming by the establishment of unprecedented turns, the fruit that is achieved through the door of conveying instruction produces some marvelous wonder. For example, in the <s>Mudrārākṣasa</s> — for there, the operations of the variegated statecraft, elaborated through the display of the power of the most excellent intellect, positively abound. And as the <s>Tāpasavatsarāja</s> episode was explained right there [earlier]. Thus other [examples] too should be imagined.
A deficiency in the delineation of obliqueness is seen even in inferior poetry;

children.text: prabandheṣu kavīndrāṇāṃ kīrtikandeṣu kiṃ punaḥ // VjivC_4.57 //
children.translated_text: in the compositions of the chief among poets — those bulbs of fame — what need be said? // VjivC_4.57 //
This is an intermediate verse. This treatise is nearly complete.
